stories.title: Man kills wife, burns body in Agra:Throws bones into Yamuna, stages fake missing story; married 4 years ago
stories.summary: In Agra, a man killed his wife and then burned her body in a tin shed behind their house. To destroy the evidence, he took the bones to Agra and threw them into the Yamuna. Moreover, to cover up the crime, the husband went to the police station on Tuesday night and filed a missing-person complaint for his wife. However, after her parents' complaint and a police investigation, the details of the case gradually came to light. When police detained the husband on Wednesday and questioned him rigorously, he confessed to the murder. Police arrested him. Based on information provided by him, they recovered bones and his wife's mobile phone from the banks of the Yamuna. The case is from the Achhnera police station area. Now, the full story Lokendra (32), who lives in Kukthala, resides 200 metres from the police outpost. He married Chandni (30), a resident of Akbara, in 2022. The couple have a two-year-old daughter. On Tuesday evening, Lokendra murdered his wife. He then burned her body in the enclosure behind their house. After this, the husband tried to mislead the police. He switched off his mobile phone and left it at home. He threw his wife's mobile phone in the Sikandra police station area. He then went to the Achhnera police station at night and reported that his wife was missing from home. Meanwhile, Chandni's family from her parental home also reached the police station. They complained that their daughter was missing and accused her husband and in-laws. The family said that Lokendra often assaulted Chandni. They continued to urge the police to trace their daughter. On Wednesday, the police reached the village and began investigating the case. They found Chandni's two-year-old daughter playing outside a shop. This deepened the police's suspicions. After finding the circumstances inside and around the house suspicious, the forensic team was called to the scene. Accused husband confesses to the murder Meanwhile, when the police questioned Lokendra firmly, the entire case came to light. Lokendra confessed to killing Chandni and burning her body. He said that after killing Chandni, he burned her body in the enclosure behind the house. He then took the bones to Agra and threw them into the Yamuna to destroy the evidence. ACP Achhnera Shailendra Singh said that Manoj had filed a complaint at the police station today stating that his sister Chandni was missing from her marital home. The police registered a missing-person report and questioned the woman's husband. During questioning, he confessed to killing his wife and burning her body over a domestic dispute. Acting on the husband's information, the police team recovered the remains of the body and the mobile phone.

stories.title: Shamli's Ayush Malik who converted to Islam disappears:Father alleges friend, mufti abducted son; now threatening him too
stories.summary: A new twist has emerged in the prominent Ayush Malik conversion case in Shamli. The pharmaceutical businessman's father has accused his son's friend and a mufti of Darul Uloom Deoband of abducting Ayush. Devraj Malik said, "My son has not returned home since appearing in the High Court on 16 September." According to Ayush's father, his son's friend Qari Sultan and Mufti Abdullah converted him again. The two are now pressuring him to give them a share of the property. Police have registered a case on Ayush's father's complaint and are investigating the matter. Ayush tells High Court: I changed my religion of my own accord The Allahabad High Court spoke to Ayush Malik after he was produced before it on 16 September. According to court records, Ayush said that he had converted to Islam of his own free will in 2014. He said that there had been no pressure, threat or inducement involved in his decision. Ayush also expressed his wish to marry Chandni Qureshi. The court granted him the freedom to live at a place of his choice, follow the religion of his choice and make a decision regarding the marital relationship in accordance with the law. Father said-friends took his son to an unknown location Ayush's father, Devraj Malik, has alleged that Qari Sultan, a resident of Jagheta Naseeb village in Saharanpur, took his son with him following a High Court order. There has been no trace of Ayush since then. Mufti Abdullah supported him in this. Devraj said the absence of his son Ayush was affecting the running of his medicine shop. The family was suffering financial losses. In his complaint to the police, Devraj alleged that Qari Sultan had come to him on 18 September. He threatened him, saying, "Ayush has been converted again. Now you people should also change your religion quickly." Friend said, "Transfer the property into my and the mufti's names" Devraj Malik alleged that Qari Sultan pressured him to transfer some of his property into his own name and some into the name of Mufti Abdullah of Darul Uloom Deoband. He also alleged that he was threatened with death, along with his wife and son, and with the seizure of his entire property if he failed to comply. In his complaint, Devraj demanded an investigation into Mufti Abdullah's alleged involvement. SP said, "The facts are also included in the FIR registered earlier" SP Narendra Pratap Singh said that a complaint had been received from Ayush's father, Devraj Malik. He said that the relevant facts had also been included in the FIR previously filed by Devraj Malik in the case. Police are taking action based on the allegations made in the complaint. FIR filed after Hindu organisations' protest Swami Yashveer, the mahant of Yog Sadhana Ashram, had released a video. He said that Chandni Qureshi had trapped the only son of the owner of Bharat Medical Store. The entire family had changed its religion under pressure. After the matter came to light, Hindu organisations began protesting and threatened to stage a sit-in outside Chandni's house. Police had registered an FIR against eight people in the case, including Chandni Qureshi, her father Islam Qureshi and three clerics. On 7 June, police arrested three accused, including Chandni Qureshi and her father. After spending one and a half months in judicial custody, the father and daughter were granted bail by the court on 24 July. He became a Hindu again after performing religious rituals just 15 days later Just 15 days later, Ayush released a video. He said, "Mother, seeing your distress, I have returned to my original faith, Hinduism, of my own free will. Please forgive me." Ayush's friend, Mohammed Sultan, filed a petition in the Allahabad High Court on 9 September. He alleged that Ayush was being forcibly confined at home. The court ordered Ayush's father to produce him before the court on 16 September. Expressed desire to embrace Islam before the court Ayush Malik was produced before the bench of Justice Sandeep Jain at the Allahabad High Court on 16 September. Ayush said, "I am around 31 years old. I have studied up to B.Pharm. I embraced Islam of my own accord in 2014. I want to marry Chandni Qureshi. My father and family do not approve of this decision." Ayush alleged that he had received threats. He has been under house arrest since June 2026. His father, Devraj Malik, outright rejected all his son's allegations. He said that some people had 'brainwashed' his son. As a father, he is extremely concerned about his son's future.

stories.title: Lekhpal loses temper at Brahmin youth:Says ‘file SC/ST case against him’; went to measure land in Hardoi, SDM seeks report within 2 days
stories.summary: A lekhpal in Hardoi allegedly threatened to have a Brahmin youth jailed under the SC/ST Act after asking his caste during a land measurement on 27 September. After the youth identified himself as a Brahmin, the lekhpal asked about the caste of the other party and, upon learning that they belonged to a Scheduled Caste, allegedly said, "Take him away and file an SC/ST Act case against him..." The incident came to light at 4 pm on Wednesday, following which Sadar Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Mayank Kundu assigned an inquiry to Sadar Tehsildar Sachindra Shukla and sought a report within two days. Read the details This case concerns Sakhaura village in the Sadar tehsil area. Situated on the banks of the Gomti, it is the last village in the tehsil. Ram Sagar Pasi, a member of the Scheduled Caste from the Behati hamlet in the same village, had applied to the tehsil authorities for possession of the land allotted to him under a land lease and for its measurement. Three days ago, on 27 September, a revenue team reached the site with the Naib Tehsildar. The team included Kaushal Yadav, the lekhpal for the Sakhaura area, and Alok Tripathi, a lekhpal from another area. Gaurav Pandey demanded that the entire land be measured During the measurement, Gaurav Pandey, son of Santosh Kumar Pandey, claimed the land and demanded that the entire plot be measured. According to Gaurav, around 30 years ago, a lease for three to four bighas of government land was issued in the name of his grandfather, Gaya Prasad Pandey. The family claims that it has been farming the land ever since. Lekhpal said to file an SC/ST case A video of the incident has also emerged, showing the lekhpal first asking Gaurav about his caste. The lekhpal asks, "What caste are you?" The reply is, "Pandey." The lekhpal then asks, "What caste does he belong to?" The reply is, "Pasi." On hearing this, the lekhpal says, "Take him away and have an SC/ST case filed against him." SDM said the remark was wrong; action will follow the report SDM Mayank Kundu said that the revenue team had gone to investigate the land dispute and conduct the measurement. An overlap was found in the area of land belonging to both parties. He said the comment made regarding the SC/ST Act was incorrect. The Tehsildar, Sadar, has been directed to submit an investigation report within two days. Action will be taken after the report is received. Lekhpal denies issuing threat Lekhpal Alok Tripathi has denied the allegation that he issued a threat. He said the video had been presented in a distorted manner. The circumstances of the case and responsibility will become clear only after the investigation report is submitted.

stories.title: Mulayam’s daughter-in-law says BJP will decide her poll seat:Doesn’t want to contest from Mainpuri in 2027; skips Akhilesh’s PDA question
stories.summary: State Women's Commission vice-chairperson Aparna Yadav arrived in Mainpuri on Wednesday. She said the BJP would decide whether she would contest the 2027 election. She said she would contest from wherever the party wanted her to. Aparna made it clear that she currently had no desire to contest from Mainpuri. Aparna Yadav arrived at 3 p.m. on Wednesday to attend an Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad programme. During the event, she spoke about women's empowerment, a drug-free India and the social role of women. Read 3 key things Aparna said... 1. Women's major contribution to making India drug-free Aparna Yadav said that she had come to attend the ABVP conference. Various issues related to women's empowerment were being presented before the young women at the event. She also discussed the contribution of women associated with Indian traditions and ancient practices. On the issue of a drug-free India, she said that women and daughters could play an important role in making the country free of drugs. The event discussed how women and young women could contribute to creating awareness against drug abuse in society. 2. Described sentiments associated with the marital home as dignified Aparna Yadav said, in response to a question from students about her experiences related to her in-laws, "I like this." She described it as highly dignified for her. When asked about Akhilesh Yadav's definition of PDA, Aparna Yadav declined to comment. She said, "This is an ABVP programme, so I have nothing to say." 3. 'The party's decision is bigger than my wishes' On the question of contesting the 2027 Assembly elections, Aparna Yadav said, “The BJP is a national party. I will contest from wherever the party decides. I do not want to contest from Mainpuri for now. I have left the decision on the seat from which I will contest to the party. The party's decision is paramount for me.”

stories.title: Man arrives in ₹7 lakh car, steals plant:Places it on seat after it doesn’t fit in boot; car bore ‘POLICE’ marking in Baghpat
stories.summary: A young man arrived in a white WagonR worth ₹7 lakh in Baghpat, stole a plant and fled. The car had 'POLICE' written on it. The man was captured on CCTV while stealing the plant. The incident took place at 5:15 p.m. on Monday, 28 September, on the Delhi-Dehradun Corridor Expressway. However, the video emerged this afternoon. NHAI officials are searching for the plant thief based on the car's registration number. Earlier, an incident of plant theft had also come to light during the inauguration of Rashtra Prerna Sthal in Lucknow on 25 December 2025. Following this, Chief Minister Yogi had said, "People travel in cars worth ₹2.5 crore and are stealing a ₹45 flower pot. I wanted to put up pictures of these flower-pot thieves at crossroads so that those who damage public property could learn a lesson." View 2 photos What the video shows On the expressway between Tatiri town and Baraut, a WagonR car with 'POLICE' written on it (UP12BM7647) stops beside the divider. The driver remains seated in his seat. Another young man gets out and walks towards the rear. He looks around. He then uproots the approximately 5-foot-tall plant from the divider and tries to put it in the boot after opening it. However, the plant does not fit because of its size. He then opens the car's rear door, places the plant on the seat and gets in through the other door. The car then drives away at speed. Flowerpots were also stolen in Lucknow on 25 December 2025 Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Rashtra Prerna Sthal in Lucknow on 25 December 2025. For the occasion, the Prerna Sthal and the surrounding area were decorated with flowers. Within a few hours of the Prime Minister's departure, people stole the pots used in the decorations. Some took them away in cars, while others stole them on scooters. The Lucknow Development Authority subsequently had the pots removed from the site. At an event held on 26 May, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took a jibe at the incident. He said, "This is not only the responsibility of municipal councillors and officials, but also of citizens. We must not damage public property. Someone arrives in a car and takes away the pots. They steal a ₹45 pot from a ₹2.5 crore car. The fuel costs more than that. At one point, I thought the photograph should be put up at a crossroads." This money does not belong to anyone else; it belongs to the public. We are only making proper use of it. When everyone joined in, Lucknow looked clean. Today, whenever anyone visits Lucknow, they say that Lucknow is clean and beautiful.

stories.title: Akhilesh says he has very good ties with Brij Bhushan:Several BJP MLAs in touch; offers former IAS officer Divya Mittal a chance to join SP
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference at the party office in Lucknow on Wednesday. Speaking about cross-voting in the Rajya Sabha election, he claimed, "Several BJP MLAs are in touch with us. But the question is, how will we accommodate all of them? We do not want to make false promises to anyone and then fail to honour them." Akhilesh said: If the Samajwadi Party forms the government in 2027, farmers will be provided free irrigation, sugarcane payments within 24 to 48 hours and affordable electricity. The Samajwadi Party's performance in western Uttar Pradesh will be historic this time. Those who won in 2022 also won only because of Samajwadi Party votes. Akhilesh says: Those with greater numbers should get the opportunity On the question of the third candidate in the Rajya Sabha, he said that decisions in a democracy should be taken according to the strength of numbers. Those with greater numbers should get the opportunity. Once the counting of votes is complete, the decision on the third candidate will be made public. Good ties with Brij Bhushan, advises former IAS officer to change her scarf Akhilesh Yadav spoke openly about the discussions taking place in political circles. Asked about former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, the SP chief said, "My relations with him are very good. We are all united on the issue of Uttar Pradesh's development." Referring to former IAS officer Divya Mittal, Akhilesh took a jibe at her. He said, "Now she will also have to decide whether to wear a green and red scarf." Akhilesh Yadav once again reiterated that this time, Rae Bareli would witness a "Lodhi versus Yogi" contest. Why Was Dhanraj Made a Candidate? The Logic of Socialism Explained Akhilesh also responded to questions being raised over the decision to nominate industrialist Dhanraj Nathwani as a Rajya Sabha candidate. He said, "We have got an opportunity to send a person from a new generation with new thinking to the Rajya Sabha. Several parties hold sway in the industrial sector, but many industrialists continue to work for society." Akhilesh said- "Dr Ram Manohar Lohia always spoke of equality in society. There is no state that does not invite industrialists. Only when industry grows in the state will incomes rise, and that will bring equality." Taking a jibe at the BJP, he said that a $1 trillion economy could not be built through merely "theft of offerings"; it required a concrete vision. Big Announcement for Farmers: Payment Within 24 to 48 Hours, Free Irrigation Addressing the farmers' conference, the SP chief expressed deep concern over the shortage of fertiliser and urea under the incumbent government. He said the SP was completely opposed to nano fertiliser. Promises for farmers if the SP comes to power- Akhilesh said-If green and red come together, the SP's colours will begin to show Akhilesh remembered the contributions of Chaudhary Charan Singh and Mahendra Singh Tikait. He said, "The green colour belongs to our farmer brothers and the red colour belongs to the socialists. When these two colours come together, the Samajwadi Party's colour will begin to be visible across the state." On the alliance with the Congress, Akhilesh said, "The Election Commission worked to remove votes in the 2022 election" Targeting the BJP's new office, Akhilesh said, "What was the need for the BJP to build such a large office? It could have rented a floor at the Election Commission of India's (ECI) office itself. In the 2022 election, the Election Commission worked to remove votes." Referring to the Supreme Court imposing a fine of ₹10 lakh in the Sambhal violence case, he said that over the past 10 years, the High Court and the Supreme Court had repeatedly raised questions about the Uttar Pradesh Police. Encounters are being carried out while wearing slippers. A second fake encounter is conducted to cover up one mistake. At the end, Akhilesh Yadav said that in 10 years, this government had failed to provide farmers with even a single power plant. This time, the people of the state are going to remove the "fake Yogi" from power. this news related to the Rajya Sabha nominations... Akhilesh gave a Rajya Sabha ticket to an Ambani close aide: Dhanraj Parimal's father was an NDA-backed MP; filed nomination with Ram Gopal SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has fielded a surprising candidate in the Rajya Sabha election. He has nominated Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, a close associate of well-known businessman Mukesh Ambani. At 11 a.m. on Wednesday, Akhilesh had Nathwani and SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav file their nomination papers. At the Election Commission office, Akhilesh held Parimal's hand and escorted him to his chair. He also congratulated him after the nomination. Dhanraj's father is a Rajya Sabha MP: Dhanraj is Group President at Reliance Industries Limited. He has been associated with the Jamnagar and Vadodara manufacturing divisions. He is also a director at Reliance New Energy Limited. His father, Parimal Nathwani, is Reliance Industries' Director of Corporate Affairs and an independent Rajya Sabha MP from Jharkhand. He entered the Rajya Sabha three months ago with the support of the NDA. Uttar Pradesh will see elections for 10 Rajya Sabha seats. Based on the current number of MLAs, the NDA is certain to win 8 seats and the Samajwadi Party 2. However, Akhilesh is preparing to field candidates for 3 seats. The suspense over who the third candidate will be continues.

stories.title: Supreme Court raps UP Police, says ‘disband it’:Suggests handing all cases to CBI; ‘This nonsense has to stop someday’
stories.summary: The Supreme Court reprimanded the Uttar Pradesh Police. Expressing strong displeasure over the police's conduct, the court said, "If every step taken by the police appears to have some agenda behind it, how will ordinary people trust them?" The bench went so far as to say, "The situation has reached a point where all cases involving the police should be handed over to the CBI. The entire police department should be disbanded. This nonsense has to stop at some point." In fact, a bench comprising Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva was hearing a case involving a motorcyclist on Wednesday. The allegation is that the complainant had caught the motorcyclist at the spot and handed him over to the police. Despite this, the police registered the FIR against an 'unknown' person. On the methods used in the investigation, the court said, "Following the rules is one thing, but crossing all limits to please someone and trying to suppress the case-the less said about this, the better." Woman complainant says: Initial police report has always been biased The woman petitioner filed a petition in the Supreme Court. While present in court, she said that the police's initial report had always been biased. Following an incident involving a motorcycle, she apprehended the accused herself and handed him over to the police. However, the police deliberately registered the FIR against an "unknown" person and left the accused column blank. The petitioner said that after the High Court intervened and a status report was sought, the police included the accused's name in the chargesheet. However, he was later given a clean chit. The motorcycle, which had no number plate at the time of seizure, was mysteriously assigned a registration number during the investigation. Court asks: How will people trust the police? The court asked the lawyer representing the Uttar Pradesh Police, "Was the FIR registered against unknown persons? If the person had been caught at the spot, why did you write 'unknown'? How will people trust the police?" The court said that leaving the name of a detained suspect blank in the initial FIR and later tampering with information related to the case completely destroys the credibility of law-enforcement agencies and public trust. The court asked- "You arrest the accused at the scene, but do not want to write his name in the FIR. Perhaps, if the equation works out, you change the name. You insert any name of your choice. You must be maintaining lists of accused in different FIRs, and putting the name of the person with fewer FIRs in a case. Is that what happens there?" Police officer to appear and explain why FIR was registered against an unknown person On the police's counter-affidavit, the court said, "We did not find the Uttar Pradesh Police's affidavit satisfactory at all. The police officer will have to appear before the court at the next hearing with a better affidavit. They will have to explain why the FIR was registered against an unidentified person when it has already been accepted that the motorcyclist was caught at the spot." The court said, “Paragraph 6 of the affidavit names the rider as Tushar. The reason why his name was initially left blank in the FIR and added later will have to be explained.”

stories.title: Farmer leader attempts self-immolation in Varanasi:Stone-pelting after police lathi-charge, farmer suffers head injury; highway blocked
stories.summary: Farmers' protest against land acquisition and toll collection on the Varanasi-Azamgarh route continued on Wednesday. After the farmers announced the protest, police increased security on the highway and at the Dherahi toll plaza. Farmers heading towards the toll plaza were stopped at various crossroads. Scuffles and heated exchanges took place between police and farmers at several locations. At around 1 p.m., farmer leader Ajit Singh and other farmers reached near the toll plaza in a government bus from the Dobhi side. He was carrying the Tricolour. As soon as he reached the toll plaza, he poured petrol over himself and took out a lighter in an attempt to set himself on fire. Police personnel immediately caught him, detained him, and took him away in a police vehicle. As Ajit Singh was being taken away in the police vehicle, the farmers surrounded it. A scuffle broke out between police personnel and farmer leaders. The police then detained other farmer leaders as well. Farmers stopped at several points on the highway Police stopped farmers coming from villages and towns towards the toll plaza at different intersections. After receiving information that hundreds of farmers were arriving, senior officials also reached the toll plaza. Around 1,000 police personnel have been deployed in the area, and continuous monitoring is underway.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan Singh says ‘all is empty without Akhilesh’:Sanjay Singh says Congress fighting its own; SP-Congress clash over seat-sharing
stories.summary: The tussle between the Samajwadi Party and Congress over seat-sharing in Uttar Pradesh is intensifying. On Wednesday, Brij Bhushan Singh was asked in Delhi about Congress's statement that it would not contest fewer than 150 seats in an alliance with the Samajwadi Party in Uttar Pradesh. In response, he said, "Everything feels empty without Akhilesh." Meanwhile, Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh said, "Congress has been harassing Akhilesh in Uttar Pradesh. Today, I heard the statement that Congress wants 150 seats. Sometimes they say they will contest all 403 seats, and sometimes they say they want 200 seats. So, are you fighting the BJP or the Samajwadi Party? You are fighting the BJP, aren't you? But your statements make it seem as though you are fighting the Samajwadi Party." You created the same situation for Tejashwi. The first time, you went into the election with 77 seats, lost many of them, and fell short of forming the government by five seats. The second time, you kept Tejashwi waiting until the very end and did not give him the seats. You took most of the seats and did not announce him as chief minister quickly. You know what the result was. First, read why it is being said that all is not well between the SP and the Congress. Now read what Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh said about Akhilesh- Former BJP MP from Gonda's Kaiserganj, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, backed Akhilesh. Speaking to the media at his residence in Delhi, he said with a smile, "The Congress has no existence in Uttar Pradesh without Akhilesh." When he was asked about the Congress refusing to contest the Uttar Pradesh election unless it was given at least 150 seats, and Akhilesh not attending the INDI alliance meeting, the BJP leader said, "We cannot say yet whether Akhilesh will attend. It is possible that a representative of his party may be attending the meeting, but the Congress has no existence in Uttar Pradesh without Akhilesh." When asked about speculation that he might go to the Rajya Sabha, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh did not respond. Received 2% of the vote in the 2022 Assembly election In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election, the Congress did not form an alliance with any major party. The party contested 399 seats on its own. The campaign was led by Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. She gave the slogan, "I am a girl, I can fight." Women were given 40% of the tickets. Despite this, the Congress performed extremely poorly. Its vote share was limited to 2.33%. The party won just two seats. Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' won from the Rampur Khas Assembly seat in Pratapgarh district, while Virendra Chaudhary won from the Pharenda Assembly seat in Maharajganj district. This was Congress's worst-ever Assembly election performance in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: Officer and mother killed in Balrampur crash:Daughter-in-law critical; car hit truck, then collided with Bolero
stories.summary: A mother and son died in a horrific road accident in Balrampur on Wednesday morning. The Swift Dzire first collided with a lorry and then crashed into a Bolero travelling along the road. Shyamnarayan (45), who was in the car, and his mother, Kailashi Devi, died on the spot. Shyamnarayan's wife, Vandana (40), was critically injured. Police sent both bodies for post-mortem examination. The accident took place near Mewalal Police Outpost on the Balrampur-Tulsipur road, around 30 km from the district headquarters. Shyamnarayan worked as a cane manager at the Tulsipur sugar mill. He was travelling to Lucknow with his wife in a Swift Dzire (UP 32 LQ 6166) to take his mother for dialysis. See two pictures... Know the full story... Shyamnarayan, a resident of the Tulsipur Sugar Mill Colony, lived with his wife, Vandana, and 16-year-old son Satyam. Satyam is studying in Class 11 in Lucknow. At around 7 a.m. on Wednesday, Shyamnarayan was driving the car himself. His mother, Kailashi Devi, and wife, Vandana, were travelling with him. It was reported that near Balaji Gas Service on the Balrampur-Tulsipur road, the Swift Dzire suddenly went out of control and collided head-on with an approaching truck. After the collision, the car also crashed into a Bolero travelling along the road. The impact involving all three vehicles was so severe that Shyamnarayan and his mother died at the scene. Bolero driver said: Car suddenly veered towards the truck The Bolero involved in the accident was travelling from Dulha Kothi in Naugarh to Lucknow. Prakash, Ram Singh, Ramratan and Chandrabhan, among others, were travelling in it. Bolero driver Rajesh said that a Swift Dzire was travelling ahead of them. Near Balaji Gas Agency, the car suddenly veered out of its lane towards a truck coming from the opposite direction. After colliding with the truck, the Dzire also crashed into their Bolero. Local residents said the car may have gone out of control because Shyamnarayan had possibly dozed off. However, the actual cause of the accident is not yet clear. Police are investigating the matter. Wife critical, referred to Lucknow Police reached the spot as soon as they received information about the accident. The police took both bodies to the district hospital, from where they were sent for post-mortem examination after the formalities. Doctors have referred critically injured Vandana to Lucknow for better treatment. Traffic on the Balrampur-Tulsipur road remained affected for some time after the accident. Police had the damaged vehicles removed and cleared the road. The family is devastated after the deaths of the mother and son and the serious injury of the daughter-in-law in the same family.

stories.title: Asian Games gold medallist Deepti Sharma reaches home:Mother cooks kadhi-rice; visits Hanuman temple before leaving for Bengaluru
stories.summary: Indian women's cricket team star all-rounder Deepti Sharma, who hails from Agra, reached home. As soon as she arrived at her home in Awadhpuri after winning the gold medal for India at the Asian Games, her family warmly welcomed her by feeding her sweets. She spent time with her family. As her daughter returned home after a long time, her mother, Sushila Sharma, prepared her favourite kadhi and rice. After eating food cooked by her mother, Deepti relived old memories with her family. The time she spent with her family was special for her. She shared her experiences of the Asian Games victory with family members, including her brother and coach, Sumit Sharma. Deepti said that winning gold for the country brings a joy of its own. They also discussed her cricket preparations and upcoming tournaments. Double celebration at home on niece's birthday When Deepthi reached home on 27 September, it was also the birthday of Radha, the daughter of her elder sister Pragati. The family was therefore in a celebratory mood. While they celebrated her niece's birthday, the residents of the colony welcomed and honoured Deepthi. Family members and local residents garlanded her with flowers. Everyone wished her continued success in her future performances. Visits temple before every major tournament Before leaving for Bengaluru on 29 September, Deepti visited the Hanuman temple near her home. She is a devoted follower of Lord Hanuman and visits the temple before major tournaments. She performed prayers at the temple, sought blessings, and prayed for the team's success. People present at the temple also congratulated Deepti and had photographs taken with her. She then left for Bengaluru. Seven wickets in the Asian Games, 14 wickets in the Asia Cup Deepti has also delivered an outstanding performance with the ball in recent tournaments. She took seven wickets at the Asian Games, while her 14 wickets in the Asia Cup played a key role in Team India's victory. After winning the gold medal, the short break she got in Agra gave her an opportunity to reconnect with her family. Home-cooked food prepared by her mother, her niece's birthday, time with her family and a visit to Bajrangbali made the stay special. Now preparing for the Zimbabwe tour Deepti has now travelled to Bengaluru for the camp ahead of the Indian team's tour of Zimbabwe. India's tour of Zimbabwe is scheduled to begin on 16 October. The tour will feature three T20s and three ODIs. All three T20s will be played in Raipur, while all three ODIs will be held in Vadodara. The Indian team will leave for Zimbabwe after the camp. Deepti will once again be among the team's key players on this tour. Now read about Deepti Sharma… Dipti would insist on going to the stadium Dipti's elder brother, Sumit Sharma, used to play cricket and went to the stadium every day for net practice. Watching him, Dipti's interest in cricket also grew. Initially, she began training with her brother at home. After that, whenever her brother went to the stadium, Dipti would insist on accompanying him. However, she was not given a chance to play there. So, she would sit on the sidelines and watch the net practice for hours. When the ball hit the stumps directly One day, Deepti arrived at Agra's Eklavya Sports Academy with her brother. She sat on the sidelines watching the other players practise in the nets. After a shot was played, the ball landed near Deepti. She picked it up and threw it towards the stumps, which were about 50 metres away. The ball hit the stumps directly and sent the bails flying. Hеmlata Kala, a selector standing some distance away, witnessed the entire scene. Kala realised that the girl had a special talent for cricket and should make it to the Indian team. She recommended Deepti's name. Hemlata Kala herself has been part of the Indian women's cricket team. Deepti was appointed DSP in the Uttar Pradesh Police Deepti was appointed DSP in the Uttar Pradesh Police two years ago. The Yogi government also awarded her ₹3 crore for her outstanding victory in the Asian Cup. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath presented Deepti with the honour at a programme held in Lucknow. Deepti helped India win the gold medal in the women's cricket event at the Asian Games held in China. She also won a silver medal with the Indian women's cricket team at the Commonwealth Games held in Birmingham in 2023.

stories.title: Akhilesh gives Rajya Sabha ticket to Ambani’s close aide:Personally filed nomination; Dhanraj Parimal’s father was NDA MP, Congress says SP cares about rich
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has fielded a surprising candidate for the Rajya Sabha elections. He has nominated businessman Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, a close associate of Mukesh Ambani. At 11 am on Wednesday, Akhilesh filed the nomination along with Nathwani and SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav. At the Election Commission office, Akhilesh held Nathwani’s hand and escorted him to his chair. After the nomination, he also congratulated him on his victory. Dhanraj is a group president at Reliance Industries Limited. He has been associated with the Jamnagar and Vadodara manufacturing divisions. He is also a director at Reliance New Energy Limited. His father, Parimal Nathwani, is a corporate affairs director at Reliance Industries and an independent Rajya Sabha MP from Jharkhand. He entered the Rajya Sabha three months ago with NDA support. Elections are to be held for 10 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh. Based on the current strength of the Assembly, the NDA is set to win eight seats and the SP two. However, Akhilesh is preparing to field candidates for three seats. The identity of the third candidate remains a suspense. On the SP giving a ticket to Nathwani, senior Congress spokesperson CP Rai said: “It would have been better if the SP chief had fielded a party worker for the Rajya Sabha. He is concerned about the wealthy, not the interests of the people.” See three pictures from the nomination: Learn about Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani: Dhanraj’s father Parimal became a Rajya Sabha MP for the fourth time three months ago Parimal Nathwani was first elected to the Rajya Sabha from Jharkhand as an independent candidate in 2008 and won again in 2014. From 2020, he was a Rajya Sabha member from Andhra Pradesh with the support of the YSR Congress Party. In 2026, he received NDA support and entered the Rajya Sabha after defeating Congress candidate Pranav Jha. Parimal once set up a cold drinks and soap factory in Mumbai. In the 1990s, he also operated around 40 PCOs in Vadodara, Gujarat. After trying his luck in the stock market, he suffered major financial losses. However, a meeting with Reliance Industries founder Dhirubhai Ambani in 1997 changed his life. The acquisition of land in Jamnagar was carried out under Nathwani’s supervision. The world’s largest refinery was later built on this land in Gujarat. He became closely associated with Dhirubhai Ambani. Parimal is also close to Mukesh and Nita Ambani and played an important role in the expansion of the Jio network. Third name to be a surprise, former MP stakes claim Akhilesh had again called his MLAs to the party office on Tuesday. Earlier, nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha election had already been purchased. Salim Iqbal Sherwani, a veteran SP leader and former MP from Badaun, had also reached the SP office. He met Akhilesh and staked his claim for a Rajya Sabha seat. Akhilesh asked him to stay in Lucknow until October 4. While leaving the office, Salim said, “We want the party to send him to the Rajya Sabha. We hope we succeed.” Election of 2 candidates certain, 12 more MLAs needed for third The Uttar Pradesh Assembly has 403 seats, of which seven are currently vacant. This leaves 396 sitting MLAs. For the election to 10 Rajya Sabha seats, the formula will be 396/11+1. Dividing 396 by 11 and adding one means a candidate will need 37 first-preference votes to be elected. The SP currently has 100 MLAs. Of these, Ramakant Yadav is in jail, bringing the effective number down to 99. Therefore, the SP will need at least 12 more votes to get its third candidate elected. The party is looking for a candidate who can bridge this gap. BJP needs 6 votes to get its 8th candidate elected The BJP, meanwhile, will need at least six more votes to get its eighth candidate elected. This makes second- and third-preference votes important. MLAs are given training for this and are told which candidate to mark as their first preference and whom to place as their second and third preferences. During counting, once a candidate reaches the prescribed quota, they are declared elected.

stories.title: Saryu, Rapti, Kuano cross danger mark:12 Gorakhpur villages surrounded by flood after Nepal rains; boats brought from Prayagraj
stories.summary: The flood threat in Gorakhpur is increasing due to continuous rainfall in Nepal. The major Rapti and Saryu rivers here are flowing above the danger mark, while the Rohin is just 1 cm below it. Water levels may continue to rise for the next few days. The river current is very strong, prompting authorities to warn people. So far, 12 villages in Gola, Bansgaon and Chauri Chaura have been affected. In view of the possibility that the situation may worsen, 10 large boats and 11 motorboats have been brought from Prayagraj. More boats will be brought in. These boats and motorboats have been sent to Bansgaon and Chauri Chaura. Boats will also be brought from Prayagraj and sent from the Barhalganj side. Given the strength of the river current, small boats will not be deployed for assistance. The administration has alerted all flood outposts. The threat is currently increasing in the Gola, Chauri Chaura and Bansgaon tehsils. Find out the status of each river According to figures recorded by 7 a.m. on Wednesday, 30 September, the Rapti river was flowing 19 cm above the danger mark. The river's water level was recorded at 75.17 metres. The Saryu River's water level at Ayodhya was 33 cm above the danger mark, while at Turtipar in Ballia district, it was 69 cm above the danger mark. Accordingly, in Gorakhpur, which lies between the two locations, the water level was also approximately 40 cm above the danger mark. People from several villages in low-lying areas are moving to safer places. If we talk about the Rohin River, its water level is 1 cm below the danger mark, but it could cross the danger level soon. People living in villages along its banks are frightened. The Kuano River is 1 metre 69 cm above the danger mark. However, the administration says the situation is not yet very dangerous, although precautions are already being taken. The administration has appealed to people not to go near the rivers or bathe in them. These villages are affected Villages in Gola tehsil are currently the worst affected. They include Bagha, Netwarpatti, Muhaljalkar, Gyanakol, Patna Mustaqil, Patna Ehtamali, Kotia Niranjan, Belwa Turant Singh, Kolkhas, Jaitpur, Vihua Mustaqil and Maibhara. Nearly 10,000 people are affected The floods have affected nearly 10,000 people so far. One large boat and 12 medium-sized boats have been deployed to help them. Flooding has affected 1,347 hectares of agricultural land. In total, 2,985 hectares of land have been affected by the floods. Other tehsils will also be affected by the floods soon.

stories.title: Ganga conservation awareness drive in Gorakhpur:1,111 lamps lit after Maha Aarti; message of cleanliness and environmental protection
stories.summary: Ganga Samagra, Gorakh province, organised a grand aarti and lamp festival at Nauka Vihar in Taramandal, Gorakhpur, on Tuesday to convey the message of reverence for the Ganga, cleanliness, and environmental conservation. More than 1,300 devotees, social workers, young people, women and members of the public participated in the event. After the grand aarti, 1,111 lamps were lit. The Nauka Vihar complex was illuminated by the glow of the lamps. Rajkishore Mishra, coordinator of Ganga Samagra's Gorakh province, said that the Ganga is the foundation of Indian culture, faith and way of life. He said the conservation of the Ganga must not be limited to worship but made part of daily life. Co-coordinator Dr. Chandrabhushan Tiwari appealed to people not to throw plastic or polluted materials into water sources. Dr. Pawan Kumar Pandey described the 1,111 lamps as a symbol of public awareness and environmental consciousness. Mridula Mishra presented a song on the Ganga. Dinesh Pandey and Durga Prasad conducted the programme.

stories.title: Akhilesh preparing to give BJP a "surprise":Poaching 10 MLAs to win third Rajya Sabha seat...? What is the full plan
stories.summary: An election is being held for 10 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh. When Akhilesh Yadav was asked about the candidates at a press conference on Monday (28 September), he said, "Be prepared for a surprise..." Today, in the UP Explainer, we will decode Akhilesh's 'surprise plan'... Question 1: How will Akhilesh win over BJP or its allies' MLAs? Answer: To understand this, we will first need to understand the position of the Samajwadi Party, the BJP and its allies in the Legislative Assembly... Take part in this Bhaskar poll and share your opinion- Question 2: What will happen if Akhilesh gets his third candidate elected? Answer: This will have three major political implications... (A) The BJP will suffer a major setback. It will inject fresh enthusiasm among Samajwadi Party workers before the election. The party will gain a significant psychological advantage over the BJP. (B) Akhilesh Yadav will emerge as a highly formidable and astute strategist in the political arena-one who knows how to turn the tables even with limited resources. Akhilesh's influence will grow within the opposition INDIA alliance. His clout will increase in seat-sharing arrangements and major decisions. (C) If the third candidate belongs to a particular caste or section-for example, Dalits or the extremely backward classes-Akhilesh's 'PDA' formula will prove even stronger on the ground. Question 3: Will legislators who cross-vote not lose their membership? Answer: No... In Rajya Sabha elections, parties do issue a 'whip' (directive), but it cannot force legislators to vote for a particular candidate. Legislators can vote for a candidate from any party at their own discretion - that is, according to their 'inner conscience'. In 2024, seven Samajwadi Party legislators voted for BJP candidate Sanjay Seth. As a result, the SP's Alok Ranjan lost. The anti-defection law does not apply to Rajya Sabha elections. Generally, if a legislator votes against the party line during voting on a budget or a bill in the House, their membership is terminated. However, Rajya Sabha elections are not legislative proceedings of the House but an electoral process. Therefore, cross-voting does not result in the loss of a legislator's membership. It can be understood this way. To prevent the buying and selling of votes, the open ballot system is in force in Rajya Sabha elections. Under this system, after marking their ballot paper, a legislator has to show it to the authorised polling agent of their party. This immediately tells the party which legislator has cross-voted. If a legislator refuses to show the ballot paper or shows it to an agent of another party, their vote becomes invalid. Even if an MLA's membership of the Legislative Assembly is not cancelled, the party can take disciplinary action against the legislator. A show-cause notice can be issued to them. They can also be expelled from the party. However, expulsion from the party does not cost them their seat in the Assembly. Such members are known as unaffiliated MLAs. At present, Cabinet Minister Manoj Pandey, Abhay Singh and Rakesh Singh are unaffiliated MLAs. ------------------------------------- this explainer... Where is the deadlock between the SP and Congress, and why is there no seat-sharing despite the alliance being finalised? What is Akhilesh hiding by saying, 'Everything is fine'? For nearly a week, Samajwadi Party and Congress leaders traded sharp remarks over the alliance. Speculation began that the alliance was about to collapse. Then, on Sunday (27 September), Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav issued a statement. He said, "We are fighting on the surface, but united internally. This is part of our strategy." Questions are now being raised: if the alliance is settled, what will be achieved through these statements? Why have the seat-sharing talks not been finalised? Read in UP Explainer...

stories.title: 1,100-year-old temple collapses into river in 2 seconds:Temple hangs over Saryu in Barabanki; boats ply in Unnao
stories.summary: Due to heavy rainfall in the hilly areas of Nepal, rivers in Uttar Pradesh are in spate. The water levels of more than eight rivers, including the Ghaghra and Saryu, are continuing to rise. A temple was swept into the Sharda River in just two seconds in Lakhimpur. The 1,100-year-old Baba Narayan Das Temple is hanging over the Saryu River in Barabanki. Villagers are performing a havan to save the temple. In Unnao, the Ganga’s water level has reached close to the danger mark. Residential areas near the river have been flooded, with boats being used in the streets. In Bijnor, the river water receded from the state highway after two days. In Bahraich, Ghaghra water is flowing across roads. Erosion has begun along the Elgin-Charsadi and Bhikhāripur-Sakraur embankments in Gonda. Meanwhile, the weather has been clear across the state since Wednesday morning. There has been bright sunshine along with light, cool winds. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the monsoon’s withdrawal from Uttar Pradesh has begun. It has already withdrawn from parts of western UP, including Muzaffarnagar and Aligarh. A light rain alert has been issued for seven cities today. Earlier, fog similar to that seen in January was reported in Amethi, Rampur and Badaun on Tuesday morning. Visibility dropped to around 25 metres at several places. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath conducted an aerial survey of flood-affected areas in Kushinagar by helicopter. He told people, “The government stands with them.” BHU weather scientist Manoj Srivastava in Varanasi said: “Monsoon withdrawal from Uttar Pradesh has begun. Its impact has completely ended in Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh and surrounding areas. The monsoon will gradually withdraw completely from the remaining parts of the state as well. stories.title: Youth caught opening sewer chamber in Varanasi:Four youths reached Kaal Bhairav ward; handed over to police; questioning underway
stories.summary: The Jal Nigam filed an FIR after sacks were found in a municipal corporation sewer chamber. Meanwhile, in Kal Bhairav Ward, a youth was caught descending into a sewer chamber without authorisation after the local councillor acted promptly. Police also apprehended three other people during the operation. Subsequently, considering the seriousness of the matter, the municipal corporation submitted a written complaint at Kotwali police station and sought action. The councillor Sanjay Kumar Gujarati said that no complaint had been made from his ward. Despite this, these people reached the spot and were opening the sewer lid. Local residents informed him. He reached the spot and questioned them, but they were unable to say who had sent them. They were subsequently handed over to the police. Last month, too, during the cleaning of the main sewer lines in more than half a dozen wards, including Shivala, Sarainandan and Nagwa, sandbags, sawdust, stones, plywood and plastic materials were found stuffed inside them. As the main lines were blocked, sewer water began overflowing into the adjoining lanes, severely disrupting daily life. At first sight, this was viewed as part of a major conspiracy to disrupt the city's cleanliness and civic amenities. According to the corporation's public relations officer, Sandeep Srivastava, it is not only illegal for any non-departmental or unauthorised person to open a government chamber or enter it, but also extremely dangerous from a safety perspective. Whether the act is part of a larger conspiracy or was driven by some other criminal motive is entirely a matter for the police investigation. The police are currently questioning the arrested accused in custody and searching for his absconding associates.

stories.title: Nagenthran urges Madurantakam electorate to think about horse trading and then vote
Akhilesh plans ‘surprise’ for BJP:Plans to win 3rd Rajya Sabha seat by breaking 10 MLAs; what’s the plan?
stories.summary: Elections are being held for 10 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh. When Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav was asked about the party's candidates at a press conference on Monday (September 28), he said, ‘Be prepared for a surprise…’ In today's UP Explainer, we decode Akhilesh Yadav's 'surprise plan'. Question: How will Akhilesh break away MLAs from the BJP and its allies? Answer: To understand this, we first need to look at the strength of the SP, BJP, and their allies in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly. Question: What if Akhilesh manages to get his third candidate elected? Answer: It would have three major political implications. (A) A setback for the BJP The BJP would suffer a significant setback. The result could energise SP workers ahead of the next elections and give the party a psychological advantage over the BJP. (B) Akhilesh's position in opposition politics could strengthen Akhilesh Yadav could emerge as a more influential strategist capable of turning the tables despite having fewer resources. His standing within the opposition INDIA bloc could improve, giving him greater influence in seat-sharing negotiations and major decisions. (C) A boost to the PDA formula If the third candidate belongs to a particular caste or social group, such as Dalits or Extremely Backward Classes, the result could further strengthen Akhilesh's PDA formula on the ground. PDA stands for Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak (Backward Classes, Dalits and Minorities). Question: Can MLAs who cross-vote lose their Assembly membership? Answer: No, not merely for cross-voting in a Rajya Sabha election. Political parties issue whips, or directions, during Rajya Sabha elections. However, these directions cannot force MLAs to vote for a particular candidate. Legislators can vote for a candidate of their choice, following what is often described as the 'voice of conscience'. In 2024, seven SP MLAs voted for BJP candidate Sanjay Seth, leading to the defeat of the SP's Alok Ranjan. Anti-defection law does not apply The anti-defection law does not apply to Rajya Sabha elections in the same way it applies to voting on legislative business. Generally, if an MLA votes against the party line during voting on a Budget or a Bill in the House, the legislator may face disqualification under the anti-defection law. However, Rajya Sabha elections are an electoral process rather than legislative proceedings. Therefore, cross-voting in these elections does not, by itself, lead to disqualification from the Assembly. Open ballot system The open ballot system is in place in Rajya Sabha elections to prevent horse-trading. Under this system, an MLA must show the marked ballot paper to the authorised polling agent of their own party. This allows the party to identify legislators who have cross-voted. If an MLA refuses to show the ballot paper or shows it to an agent of another party, the vote becomes invalid. Rebel MLAs can be expelled from the party Although an MLA's Assembly membership is not automatically cancelled for cross-voting, the party can initiate disciplinary action against the legislator. It may issue a show-cause notice and even expel the MLA from the party. However, expulsion from the party does not automatically end the legislator's Assembly membership. Such members are known as unaffiliated MLAs. At present, Cabinet Minister Manoj Pandey and MLAs Abhay Singh and Rakesh Singh are unaffiliated legislators.

stories.title: Gomtinagar railway station like airport:Wait for train in AC, shop while you wait; 26 lifts, 21 escalators
stories.summary: A grand glass-and-steel building, giant LED screens glowing at the entrance, and tight security resembling that at an airport, this is Lucknow's Gomtinagar Railway Station. As soon as you enter the station premises, you will not find the usual chaos associated with Indian railway stations. Separate elevated ramps have been built for arriving and departing passengers. As you enter the main terminal through the elevated road meant for departures, a grand 28-metre-wide air concourse welcomes you. Built above the railway tracks, it is essentially a large bridge-like roof from where passengers can enjoy a panoramic view of the surroundings, much like an airport lounge. Cool air-conditioning, comfortable chairs and natural light filtering through the glass roof give the space the feel of a mall or luxury lounge. Dozens of lifts and escalators are continuously operating to take passengers down to the platforms. The platforms are equipped with digital display boards, automated announcements, and Wi-Fi, and are spotlessly clean. Here's what makes Lucknow's Gomtinagar Railway Station special... Entire structure built around 40 feet above ground Gomtinagar Railway Station is divided into two terminals. The North Terminal is on the Vibhuti Khand side, while the South Terminal is on the Gomtinagar side. As you enter the station from the Vibhuti Khand side, you can see an around 200-metre-long overbridge that leads directly to Gomtinagar Railway Station. The entire structure has been built around 40 feet above ground level. Standing here gives you the feeling of being on the ground, but the entire structure is actually elevated. The station has 26 lifts and 21 escalators. Ticket counters have been provided, along with automatic ticket vending machines. At a regular railway station, passengers use a foot overbridge to move from one platform to another. Here, instead, a 28-metre-wide and around 100-metre-long concourse has been built. The corridor is transparent, allowing passengers to see from above which train is arriving at which platform. Digital boards displaying information about arriving and departing trains have also been installed inside. The station has automatic sensor-based glass gates. From here, passengers can reach any platform in just a minute. 22 trains halt here A total of 22 trains currently halt at the station, eight of which originate from here. Passengers can board trains such as the Vande Bharat to Patna, Pushpak Express, Awadh Express and Amrit Bharat from Gomtinagar. Preparations are underway to shift trains currently stopping at Charbagh, including the Shatabdi Express, Tejas, Double Decker and Mass Express — to Gomtinagar Railway Station in the coming days. For passenger safety, more than 50 high-resolution CCTV cameras have been installed across the station. The entire campus is monitored from a command centre. If any suspicious activity is detected, the command centre alerts the GRP and RPF. An underground parking facility for 800 vehicles has been built at the station. It is among the railway stations in the country with one of the largest parking facilities. Solar panels have also been installed on the upper section of the station. An official at the station says that whenever there is a power cut, the air-conditioning system is sometimes connected to the solar panels for some time. The solar system helps reduce electricity consumption as several facilities can run on solar power. Passengers say: 'Never seen a station like this' At the station, we met Sunil Tiwari from Chhapra, Bihar, who was waiting for his train with his family. Sunil said the best thing about the station was the peaceful atmosphere. He said, Even if someone arrives here tired, they can relax. There are arrangements for sleeping and the entire campus is air-conditioned. Waiting for the train is also a pleasant experience here. Neeshu said the facilities here were much better than those in Bihar. She said, Work is also happening there and things will improve further in Bihar, but this is much better. It is very clean and the seating arrangements are also good. Indravati, who was also present at the station, said there was a huge difference between this station and others. She said, “I have never seen such facilities at a railway station before. Abhishek Maurya from Gorakhpur said the station had been built beautifully. He said, It is becoming even more developed than Charbagh. I was very happy to see it. I haven't seen a station like this anywhere else in UP yet. I feel that once it is fully completed, there may not be a better railway station in the country. Madan Tiwari said he had visited Lucknow earlier but was visiting this station for the first time. He said, I haven't seen such facilities at other stations. It is good and a new experience. Similar facilities should be introduced at other stations too. Better facilities for passengers will improve things. Phase 2 to give station a luxury mall-like look From Atal Bihari Vajpayee's vision to a world-class station 2002-03: The site was initially a regular halt. Former Prime Minister and former Lucknow MP Atal Bihari Vajpayee laid the foundation for developing it as an alternative to Charbagh. Platforms were built in the initial phase. 2014-18: MP Rajnath Singh initiated efforts to expand the station. On August 21, 2018, the project to develop it as a world-class railway station was approved. Current status: After delays caused by the Covid pandemic, Phase 1 is now almost fully complete. A three-storey North Terminal building has been constructed on the Vibhuti Khand side, while a two-storey South Terminal building has been built on the Gomtinagar side.

stories.title: ‘I’ll accept being called a traitor’:Manoj Pandey hits back at Akhilesh, ‘won’t compromise on Sanatan or Ram’
stories.summary: On Akhilesh Yadav's 'PDA Rath Yatra' and his statement, 'We will not let the fugitive win', Cabinet minister in the Yogi government Manoj Pandey said, This is a mockery of democracy. The election will not be fought from Vikramaditya Marg, but on the ground in Unchahar. The people there will give a befitting reply in 2027. Responding to the SP's taunt of calling him a traitor, Pandey said, If standing with Lord Ram, the nation and the poor is treachery, I am ready to commit this treachery one crore times. Read Dainik Bhaskar's exclusive conversation with Manoj Pandey on his three decades of experience in the Samajwadi Party, questions raised over the Mahakatha held in Raebareli, the Rajya Sabha election 'surprise', and his comparison of the working styles of Mulayam Singh Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav. Question: Akhilesh said in Raebareli that he would not let the 'fugitive' win. Was he referring to you? Answer: Manoj Pandey did not enter politics to make money. Nor did I enter politics to enjoy a life of luxury. Some of my former colleagues have given me a particular name, Manoj Pandey, the traitor. This is the same Manoj Pandey who suffered broken legs and broken hands while working for the Samajwadi Party and went to jail 29 times. I also had one vote in the SP government formed in 2012. I also made a one per cent contribution. Whether I am a traitor or not will be decided by the people of this country. You and I will not decide it. Question: Akhilesh says he will not let you win. What would you say to that? Answer: This is a mockery of democracy. It is arrogance and ego, and remember this. These are the people; they listen and understand everything. By saying this, you are challenging the voters of an entire Assembly constituency. Remember, this is not a challenge to Manoj Pandey. It is a challenge to the farmers, poor, backward classes, Dalits and youth of Unchahar. It is a challenge to our mothers and sisters, that we will not let Manoj Pandey, who works for you, win. I believe Unchahar has accepted this challenge. Question: Akhilesh said he would spring a surprise in the Rajya Sabha. Is anyone from the SP in touch with you? Answer: Political parties and their leaders need to boost the morale of their party and protect it. A great thinker once said that when a party is in crisis and people repeatedly reject it in a democracy, it becomes a challenge for any political party to retain its workers. At such a time, if opposition parties make statements saying, 'We are going to form the government', 'We will win five Rajya Sabha seats' or 'We will win all the Legislative Council seats', we have no objection. But the Election Commission of India has announced the dates for the results. The results will also come. Uttar Pradesh will see them. Question: Akhilesh has repeatedly claimed that he will form the government on the strength of PDA. How do you see this? Answer: If the opposition leaders of today had seen Marich from the Satyug, they would have committed suicide right here. Ten days ago, a statement came from the party's national spokesperson and national general secretary saying that even a prostitute is better than Brahmins. Ten days later, they will say P in PDA stands for Pandit. Ten days after that, a rath will come out with another definition of P written on it. Do you think the people of Uttar Pradesh are so ignorant? Fine, it is your shop. Sell whatever you want and give it whatever brand name you want. Question: There is a trend in UP where different leaders are organising religious kathas. Is this politics? Answer: I do not understand the lens through which you are looking at it. But I am overwhelmed by the way the country has viewed it. I bow at the feet of Bholenath. How can I express my gratitude to him for the unprecedented katha that the people of Unchahar organised together? I was also there as a worker. More than 3.5 million people attended the katha, with 7-8 lakh people present every day. Come and see where the PDA was. The PDA was right there. Who was backward, who was upper caste, who was poor and who was rich, everyone came together with one chant: 'Om Namah Shivay, Har Har Mahadev'. This is Sanatan. People who abuse Sanatan, people who hurt Sanatan, perhaps the Unchahar katha has opened your eyes. Question: There are allegations that you organised the katha for a show of strength and to collect donations. Answer: Those who keep abusing Lord Ram and then wear saffron clothes in the name of stealing offerings, only to take them off and throw them away 10 days later. Those who have ordered firing on karsevaks and turned the waters of the Sarayu red with their blood, and then start talking about something else — may God give them wisdom. That is all I can say. Question: In the BJP, people say that 'Babua' (Akhilesh Yadav) wakes up at noon. Answer: No. We were workers in the SP. Whenever I needed to meet him, I would take an appointment and meet him. I stay overnight in Raebareli. Yes, I can say that I have seen Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath working. That is why I have spoken to him at 11.30 pm and also at 6 am. I have seen the lives of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister. I can say with confidence that I have not come to your platform to unnecessarily praise anyone. Question: So, when you were in the SP, you never spoke to him that late? Answer: No. The schedule that is given is the schedule according to which a person speaks. In our system, if there is an emergency, the Home Minister can come to speak even at 4 am. You can speak to the Chief Minister even at 1 am. An incident had taken place, and I spoke to the Chief Minister over the phone at 1 am. Question: What is the difference between Mulayam and Akhilesh's politics? Answer: There is no similarity between the two, so there is no question of explaining the difference.

stories.title: 'Blue drum' murder case:Muskan, lover Sahil found guilty of killing husband, chopped body found in cement-filled container; sentencing on 14 Oct
stories.summary: A Meerut district court on Wednesday convicted Muskan and her lover for jointly murdering her husband, Saurabh, chopping his body into pieces and hiding them in a blue drum in Meerut. The court delivered its verdict 576 days after the incident, following testimony from more than 22 witnesses over 126 hearing dates, and will announce the sentence in 15 days. The murder took place on March 3, 2025. The trial began in the District Judge's court in July 2025. The police filed a 1,000-page charge sheet. On September 19, the court reserved its verdict. Muskan and Sahil were anxious before the verdict. Muskan had been praying in jail for the past three days. Sahil had stopped talking to fellow inmates. Sahil was asking the jail staff about the verdict. PHOTOS from the case

stories.title: Millionaire businessman's son appears dejected in Kanpur jail:Used to live in AC at home, restless for 5 days; happy after wife's release
stories.summary: Five days after being jailed for allegedly murdering his millionaire businessman father, Vinod Minocha’s son Subrat is struggling to adjust to prison life in Kanpur. Used to living amid comforts and facilities at home, Subrat has been finding it difficult in jail. Jail Superintendent Rajesh Pandey said none of his family members has visited him so far. According to jail officials, Subrat appeared highly stressed on the first day. He remained withdrawn throughout the day and barely spoke to other inmates. At night, he became restless due to the heat and humidity. When the jail administration asked him about food, he refused to eat. He went through the entire night without food. The next morning, he was served porridge, jaggery and tea for breakfast. However, he has now gradually started interacting with other inmates. Subrat is currently lodged in the mulahiza barrack, where new inmates are kept under initial observation and undergo health checks. His regular barrack will be allotted after 14 days as per jail rules. Subrat happy after hearing about Shalu’s release According to jail officials, Subrat had been repeatedly asking about Shalu, who was also in jail. He had expressed a desire to meet her. When he learnt on September 28 that Shalu had been released, he appeared quite happy. Meanwhile, Shalu was released from jail around 1 am on September 28 and reached her home in Lucknow’s Thakurganj. According to the family, the first thing she did after reaching home was go to her son Shrijay, who was asleep at the time. Shalu kissed his forehead and kept looking at him for around 10 minutes. After seeing her son for the first time in around 21 days, Shalu broke down in tears. She also hugged her mother and cried for a long time. Seeing his daughter cry, her father Naresh Arora too could not hold back his tears. Shrijay hugged his mother as soon as he saw her Naresh Arora said that when Shrijay woke up around 7 am on September 29, he was extremely happy to see his mother Shalu in front of him. He hugged her tightly and stayed with her throughout the day. He did not let her out of his sight even for a moment. Shalu fed her son with her own hands. Relatives and acquaintances also continued to visit the house throughout Tuesday to meet Shalu. Subrat was sent to jail on September 24 On September 24, Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal announced the breakthrough in the Vinod Minocha murder case and arrested his son Subrat Minocha before sending him to jail. During questioning, Subrat told police that his father had relationships with several women. He alleged that his father spent a lot of money on them. According to Subrat, whenever he asked his father for money, Vinod refused to give it to him. He was also afraid that his father might marry another woman and bring her home, which could make her another claimant to the family property. According to police, Subrat told investigators that he had no regret over his father’s murder. However, he said he was upset that his father had been killed in a painful manner. Businessman Vinod Minocha was murdered on September 5 Vinod Minocha, a pharmaceutical businessman and resident of Flat C-104 in Ratan Orbit, Indira Nagar, was murdered on September 5. He was stabbed 17 times. On September 24, police arrested his son Subrat for allegedly murdering him and sent him to jail. Speaking to the media, Subrat had said his father had relationships with several women and that this was why his mother Punita did not live with him. According to Subrat, he feared that another woman might come to his house and claim that she was pregnant with Vinod’s child. He therefore allegedly got his father killed through his former employee Vishal Gautam and Vishal’s associate Rajkishore. During the initial investigation into the businessman’s murder, police treated Shalu as an accused and sent her to jail. However, subsequent investigation found her innocent. Police then submitted a closure report in Shalu’s favour in court on Friday, September 25. After hearing the matter on Monday, the court ordered her immediate release from jail. Read in sequence: How did Subrat frame his wife in his father’s murder?

stories.title: Class 9 student shot dead in Jhansi:Intruder enters Jhansi home by scaling wall; she was visiting grandmother
stories.summary: 19-year-old Class 9 student was shot dead in Jhansi. She was alone at home. When her grandmother reached the house, she found the door locked from inside. The door did not open even after she called out for a long time. When people nearby looked over the wall, they saw the girl's body lying in the courtyard. Blood was flowing from her temple. Senior Superintendent of Police Vikas Kumar reached the spot after being informed. Police sent the body for a post-mortem examination. The incident took place at around 3.30 p.m. on Wednesday in the ITI area. See 2 pictures Now, the sequence of events in detail... Grandmother returned from work, but the door did not open Somi Raikwar, who lives in the ITI area, is originally from Khodan village. Her father, Bhagwandas, has died. As a result, Somi's mother, Sheela, lives alone in the house in the ITI area. Somi currently lives with her family in Sipri Bazaar. Her daughter, Chanchal Raikwar, studied at Arya Kanya School. A few days ago, Somi sent her daughter Chanchal to stay with her mother, Sheela. On Wednesday afternoon, her grandmother went out for some work. During this time, Chanchal was alone at home. At around 3.30 p.m., Sheela returned home and knocked on the door. However, there was no response from inside and the latch did not open. She then called nearby residents for help. The residents climbed the wall and looked inside, finding Chanchal lying in the courtyard. Police suspect murder was linked to an old enmity It is being reported that Somi's family had an old enmity with a person living in Khodan. Because of this, Somi had also left Chanchal with her grandmother. Police are currently investigating the case while keeping this enmity and other angles in mind. It is said that the accused entered the house by scaling the wall after finding an opportunity in broad daylight. He then shot Chanchal dead and fled. Given the seriousness of the incident, a forensic team and the SWAT team reached the spot along with police officials and conducted an investigation. The team collected crucial evidence from the scene. Police also questioned people living nearby. The police are also searching for the accused based on the evidence recovered from the scene and footage from CCTV cameras installed in the area.

stories.title: Lekhpal throws 26-year-old girlfriend's body into Yamuna:Carries her in a sack in Agra; said, “She was adamant about getting married”
stories.summary: The body of a 26-year-old woman who had been missing from Agra for eight days was found in the Yamuna in Etawah on Tuesday. The police then arrested Shivjeet Bhadauria, a lekhpal posted in Fatehabad tehsil. A case has been registered against him for kidnapping, abetment to suicide and destruction of evidence. The police sent the lekhpal to jail on Wednesday. The lekhpal said that Vishakha was insisting on getting married and hanged herself from a fan over the issue. The case falls under the jurisdiction of the MM Gate police station. Now read the full case Lekhpal Shivjeet Bhadauria is a resident of Rudhmuli village in Bah. Vishakha was also from the Bah area. She was living in Noori Darwaza in the MM Gate area and preparing for the Super TET after completing her BTC. During this period, Shivjeet and Vishakha grew close. They began going out together. The lekhpal also promised to marry her. Dispute escalated after the lekhpal got married In May this year, the lekhpal got married elsewhere. When Vishakha found out, she began arguing with him. Meanwhile, one day, the lekhpal's wife saw Vishakha's photograph on his mobile phone. She then also began arguing with her husband. After conflict broke out at home, the lekhpal distanced himself from Vishakha. Meanwhile, Vishaka suddenly went missing on 29 September. Her family was unable to contact her. They then filed a missing-person report for Vishaka at the M.M. Gate police station. The police investigation and call details revealed the name of revenue official Shivjeet Bhadauria. The police detained the revenue official and questioned him, after which he confessed to the murder. Revenue official said - took body away in car and threw it into Yamuna Revenue official Shivjeet told the police, "Vishaka came to my room on 30 September. She had a heated argument with me about getting married. After that, she put a noose around her neck and hanged herself from the fan. I took her down and took her to hospital, where doctors declared Vishaka dead." After this, I panicked. I took Visakha's body by car to Etawah, which borders Bah, and threw it into the Yamuna. After the lekhpal's statement was recorded, the police began searching for Visakha's body in the Yamuna in Etawah, which borders Bah. At around 4 p.m. on Tuesday, villagers informed the police that a girl's body was lying in a sack on the banks of the Yamuna near Miholi village. On receiving the information, Badpura Station House Officer Kripal Singh reached the spot with a team. Visakha's family members were called to identify the body. After they identified it, the body was sent for a post-mortem examination. Visakha was preparing for Super TET Vijaya's father, Vijay Ojha, said that Vishakha was living in Agra's MM Gate police station area and preparing for the Super TET examination. Shivjeet Singh, the village revenue officer, lived about 300 metres from our house. They used to mine sand from the Yamuna. Our family also has farmland along the Yamuna. The mining was damaging our fields. For this reason, I complained to the Bah sub-divisional magistrate in 2017. After this, the administration seized several tractors involved in the mining. It was after this that they began holding a grudge against our family. Family says daughter was kidnapped over old enmity The family alleges that Shivjeet kidnapped Vishakha on 29 September because of the old enmity. He subsequently murdered her, then put her body in a sack and threw it into the Yamuna near Kachora Ghat. DCP City Sayyad Ali Abbas said that the lekhpal had been sent to jail.
