stories.title: Passengers jump from moving train seeing checking in UP:TTE knocks on toilet door; 371 caught
stories.summary: A stampede broke out during ticket checking on a train in Barabanki on Wednesday afternoon after several ticket examiners (TTEs) entered the coach with police personnel at the same time, prompting passengers without tickets to jump out of the train. A video of the incident has also emerged, showing several people falling after jumping out. Several passengers locked themselves inside the toilets to escape, but the TTEs knocked on the doors and brought them out. Fines were then collected from the passengers one by one. Railway police detained 371 people during ticket checking on 5-6 trains. The incident took place at 2 p.m. at Rasauli railway station. See 2 pictures... Passengers jumped from train travelling from Ayodhya to Lucknow A train travelling from Ayodhya to Lucknow (64215) arrived at Rasauli railway station in Barabanki at around 12 p.m. on Wednesday. As soon as the train arrived, the checking team boarded it in large numbers. Checking began as soon as the train started moving. Passengers without tickets panicked when they saw this. They began running around inside the coaches to save themselves. Passengers started jumping from the moving train. Some of them were women. They too began jumping from the moving train with their luggage. Railway police brought passengers out of the toilets Passengers who had boarded the train without tickets hid in the toilets to avoid being caught. The railway police team deployed with the checking team began searching for the ticketless passengers. The toilet doors were then opened, and the passengers hiding inside were brought out. The checking team inspected tickets on several trains, including the Garib Nawaz Express and the Ayodhya Cantt-Lucknow MEMU. A total of 371 ticketless passengers were caught, and the railway team collected a fine of ₹286,580 from them. Thirty-six cases of rule violations were presented before the ACJRM Court. A video has also emerged showing people travelling without tickets fleeing and hiding in the toilets. Following the incident, railway officials appealed to passengers not to travel without tickets and not to make dangerous attempts, such as jumping from the train, to evade checking. Divisional Railway Manager Sunil Kumar Verma said- “This campaign against ticketless travellers will continue. These people cause inconvenience to passengers travelling with tickets. They also cause significant losses to the department's revenue.”

stories.title: From lakhpati to crorepati in 6 years:Know assets declared by Dhruv Tripathi, Ajay and Sanjayan; Fortuner, Thar also listed
stories.summary: A major disparity in the assets of candidates contesting the Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers' constituency election has emerged from their election affidavits, with the declared movable and immovable assets of three-time teacher legislator and BJP candidate Dhruv Kumar Tripathi and his wife rising from around ₹10.45 lakh in 2020 to around ₹2.52 crore in 2026. Six years ago, the couple jointly owned movable assets worth around ₹10.45 lakh. Samajwadi Party candidate Dr Sanjay Tripathi has declared movable assets worth ₹16.93 crore in his name. Another candidate, Ajay Singh, owns total assets worth around ₹5.38 crore. He also owns SUVs such as a Fortuner, Innova and Thar. Dhruv Tripathi's assets increased more than 24-fold in six years According to the affidavit filed for the 2020 election, Dhruv Kumar Tripathi had movable assets worth ₹6,08,008. These included ₹45,000 in cash, ₹1,70,561 deposited in the bank, LIC/SBI Life policies worth ₹2,69,946 and 25 grams of gold. At the time, his wife had movable assets worth ₹437,147 in her name. These included ₹12,000 in cash, ₹9,482 in bank deposits, an SBI Life policy worth ₹57,665, 70 grams of gold and 250 grams of silver. In 2020, both declared that they had no immovable assets or liabilities in their names. In the affidavit filed in 2026, Dhruv Tripathi's movable assets increased to ₹10,520,652.97. These include an Innova Crysta car, gold and silver, cash, shares and other investments. His wife's movable assets also increased to ₹20,22,177.87. Immovable assets added, total assets worth around ₹2.52 crore The market value of immovable assets declared in Dhruv Tripathi's name in 2026 was ₹7,620,651. Immovable assets worth ₹5,040,651 were declared in his wife's name. Together, their movable assets are worth around ₹1.25 crore and their immovable assets around ₹1.27 crore. Their total declared assets amount to around ₹2.52 crore. However, the 2026 affidavit also lists a car loan of ₹1,345,718 against Dhruv Tripathi. Dr Sanjayan Tripathi's movable assets worth ₹16.93 crore Samajwadi Party candidate Dr Sanjayan Tripathi appears to be the wealthiest among the major candidates in this election. According to his election affidavit, he has movable assets worth ₹16,93,83,440.94 in his name. In addition, movable assets worth ₹1,20,64,601.27 have been declared in the name of his dependent. The asset details include an Innova and a Renault Duster car, 700 grams of gold and 3 kilograms of silver, along with shares, LIC and other investments. In other words, Sanjayan Tripathi's affidavit lists not only vehicles and precious metals but also a large amount in shares and other investments. Sanjayan's annual income around ₹35.80 lakh According to the income tax return, Dr Sanjayan Tripathi declared a total income of ₹3,580,240 in the financial year 2025-26. During the same period, his wife declared a total income of ₹1,289,830. Thus, the two have a combined declared annual income of ₹48,70,070. The election affidavit also provides information about a case registered against Dr Sanjayan Tripathi. Ajay Singh has assets worth ₹5.38 crore Ajay Singh, who is contesting the election for the teachers' MLA seat, has declared total assets worth around ₹5.38 crore in his affidavit. According to the affidavit, Ajay Singh has movable assets worth ₹17,813,696.50 in his name. His dependent has movable assets worth ₹8,497,694. In addition, the estimated market value of Ajay Singh's immovable assets has been stated as ₹2.75 crore. Adding the movable and immovable assets of Ajay Singh and his dependant, the total declared assets amount to ₹53,811,390.50, or around ₹5.38 crore. Fortuner, Innova and Thar also included Ajay Singh's movable assets include several expensive vehicles, apart from jewellery, shares and other assets. His declared vehicles include a Toyota Fortuner, Toyota Innova and Mahindra Thar. The affidavits of the leading candidates in the teachers' MLC election thus reveal different forms of wealth. Dhruv Tripathi's assets have increased significantly over six years, while Dr Sanjayan Tripathi's declared movable assets exceed ₹16 crore and Ajay Singh's total declared assets exceed ₹5 crore.

stories.title: Husband sees wife with lover, chases and shoots both:Woman shot 4 times, youth twice in Firozabad; she was living separately from husband
stories.summary: In Firozabad, a young man opened fire on his wife and her lover. He shot his wife four times and her lover twice. Both have been referred to Agra in serious condition. A video of the shooting has also emerged. The incident took place at the Kotla Chungi crossing at 10 p.m. on Tuesday. See 3 pictures First, find out what the video shows The video that has surfaced shows the husband entering the shop and speaking to his wife and her lover. A scuffle also breaks out between them. The husband then comes out of the shop, takes a licensed revolver from the pocket of his lower garment and first fires at the lover. As soon as the shot is fired, the son tries to stop his father, but he continues firing. The lover falls on the road after being shot, while the wife starts running along the road to save her life. Meanwhile, a crowd caught the husband who had opened fire and informed the police. The police reached the spot, took the husband into custody and recovered the licensed revolver from him. Sunny was hit by one bullet in the centre of his chest, lower down, and another on the right side below the ribs. As his condition was critical, he was referred to Agra. Shipra was hit by one bullet in her left shoulder, one in her abdomen and another in the ribs on her left side. One bullet grazed her hand and passed through. The two got married 10 years ago Bundy (40), who lives near Kotla Chungi intersection, runs an intermediate college. He married Shipra (35), a native of Mathura, 10 years ago. The couple also have two sons. Bundy and Shipra have been quarrelling for the past two years. Because of this, Shipra has been living at her parental home. According to the police, Shipra Firozabad had gone to her aunt's house on Tuesday. She was talking to Sunny Thakur, an internet provider who runs a shop at her aunt's house. Sunny is a resident of Dwarkapuri. Bunty arrived there soon afterwards. Following a brief argument, Bunty opened fire. Shipra said, ‘I was called to speak to my in-laws.’ Shipra said, "My husband has been quarrelling with Bunty. My aunt had called me to her house so that I could speak to my in-laws. My husband arrived there soon afterwards and started firing." Meanwhile, after learning that Shipra had been shot, her family members reached the government trauma centre. Her brother Shashank said that Shipra has two sons. Shipra and her brother-in-law Bunty had quarrelled after he became involved with another woman. After that, Shipra began living with us. Both children also live with us. SSP Aditya Langhe said that the investigation is currently under way. The accused has been taken into custody and is being questioned. Action will be taken based on the evidence that emerges. The questioning has revealed that Shipra and Sunny were having an affair. The video that has emerged shows Shipra and Sunny sitting inside the shop with the lights switched off.

stories.title: Lover shoots Army man’s daughter, later dies by suicide:Incident takes place on Agra road; girl critical
stories.summary: In Agra, a young man shot a young woman before shooting himself. The woman suffered serious injuries in the shooting and has been admitted to the military hospital. The man died at the scene. The incident caused panic in the area. Arun and the young woman, Honey, were reportedly in a relationship. An argument broke out between them over an issue. Arun then shot the woman before shooting himself. The incident took place near St Peter's College in the Sadar police station area. See 3 pictures : Read the full account now Arun Kumar, 25, was a resident of Itaura in Malpura. He worked at the Sainya toll plaza. The young woman had come to meet him at Maa Pitambara's Sapphire Colony. One of her friends was also present there at the time of the incident. Arun and the young woman first quarrelled over something. During the quarrel, Arun first shot the young woman with a country-made pistol and then shot himself in the temple. Arun Kumar died on the spot, while the young woman was seriously injured. The young woman is a BSc student The injured woman has been identified as Honey, daughter of Prem Kumar. Her father is a soldier. She is a resident of Sadabad and is reportedly a BSc student at Munnilal College. She had been living in rented accommodation near the scene of the incident while pursuing her studies. The young man was married According to local residents, the young man was married and had children. The reason behind the incident has not yet been established. As soon as the police at Malpura police station were informed of the incident, they reached the spot. After some time, the ACP and ADCP also reached the scene. The police sent the young man's body for a post-mortem examination. Evidence is also being collected from the scene. The police are investigating the case. This report is being updated.

stories.title: 20-year-old daughter held captive for 2 months, starved:Bhadohi woman reduced to skeleton; brother says father did wrong things
stories.summary: In Bhadohi, a father held his 20-year-old daughter captive for two months and did not even give her food or water. Acting on information from neighbours, police rescued her from beneath a tin shed room. She was found in an extremely weak condition. The extent of her hunger and thirst can be gauged from the fact that she drank 1.5 litres of water at once in the ambulance. According to doctors, the skin on her body had begun to decay because of the unhygienic conditions, and her toenails had grown considerably. Tests at the district hospital found her haemoglobin level to be just 6 grams and her platelet count to be 59,000. Doctors said the young woman's body had become extremely weak because she had not been given adequate food and water for a long time. The incident took place in an area of the district headquarters. Meanwhile, the young woman's minor younger brother alleged that their father had been sexually abusing his sister. According to the brother, when he saw this, their father threatened him and forced him to remain silent. Now, here are the full details of the case... The young woman's father lives with her and his 15-year-old minor son in an area of the district headquarters. He runs a samosa shop. He had married three times. His first wife died about 10 years ago. He had a son with his first wife, who died of an illness. After this, he married for the second time. His second wife also died about five years ago. They had a 15-year-old son and the young woman who was found injured. After his second wife's death, he married for the third time, but about two years later, his third wife left him. The family now consists of the father, his second wife's 15-year-old son and his daughter. Neighbours alerted police after foul smell came from the house A neighbour said the young woman was good at her studies. She had enrolled in a BA course some time ago. She also attended spoken English classes for some time. However, she had not been seen for several days. By Monday afternoon, a foul smell had been coming from the house for quite some time. The police were then informed. When the neighbours reached the house with the police, the young woman was found on the roof in an extremely poor condition. She was not wearing any clothes. The neighbours dressed her and took her to Maharaja Chet Singh District Hospital. She was suffering from hunger and thirst, drank 1.5 litres of water According to the neighbour, the young woman drank around 1.5 litres of water on the way. When she said she was hungry, she was given biscuits and breakfast. She was extremely restless to eat and drink. Wound-like marks were also found on her body. Marks indicating that her hands and legs had been tied were also found. According to the neighbour, the young woman had previously been normal and attended school. 15-year-old brother said: Dad threatened him and silenced him The young woman's 15-year-old brother alleged that their father did not allow his sister to leave the house. According to him, she had been confined to the terrace for around two months. The brother alleged that their father sexually abused his sister. He said that when he discovered this, their father threatened him as well. According to the brother, their father had said that if he told anyone, he would kill both him and his sister. He remained silent out of fear. Their father did not allow anyone to enter the house. He sells samosas at a shop in the city. Whenever someone came to the house, he would call them over to where he was. Doctor says: Fat layer and muscles in body severely depleted According to district hospital EMO Dr Dhirendra, the young woman was brought to the hospital in a critical condition at around 8 p.m. on Monday. In faltering speech, she said that she had not been given food for around two months. According to the doctor, the fat layer and muscles in her body had severely depleted. This indicates that she had not received adequate food for a prolonged period. Father says-She was not held captive; she had fever and loose motions The young woman's father has denied allegations that she was held captive. He said his daughter had been suffering from fever and loose motions. She had also developed boils and sores on the back of her body, for which she was receiving treatment. According to her father, she was given the food cooked at home. She had been unable to walk for the past three to four days. However, he had not admitted her to hospital. SDM and CO reach hospital After receiving the information, Gyanpur SDM Arun Dixit and CO Chaman Chawda reached the district hospital. Both officials spoke to the young woman and her father. Doctors said the young woman would be kept under continuous observation. SDM said- “A young woman had been ill for several days, and the family had been unable to get her proper treatment. As a result, her body had become weak. She is now receiving treatment.”

stories.title: 11 district chiefs changed, 20 IPS transferred in UP:Ravina Tyagi named Barabanki SP, Yashveer Singh gets Jaunpur charge
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government transferred 20 IPS officers on Wednesday afternoon. Eleven police chiefs were changed in 13 districts. The SPs of Jaunpur, Muzaffarnagar, Barabanki, Hapur and Mau were removed from their posts. Six police chiefs have been given charge of other districts. Lucknow DCP Ravina Tyagi has been made the Barabanki SP, while Azamgarh SP City Madhuban Singh has been given charge of Hapur. Check out the list below : Sanjay Kumar sent to Prayagraj PAC Sanjay Kumar is a State Police Service officer who was promoted from PPS to IPS. Questions had been raised over his performance in a district like Muzaffarnagar. He has now been moved to Prayagraj PAC as Commandant. Gyananjay Singh moved from Hapur Gyananjay Singh had been posted in Hapur for a long time. His coordination with senior officers was reportedly not good, and he had come under the scanner of a senior officer over different incidents. Complaints of corruption in the Hapur police also came during his tenure and were reportedly sent to Lucknow. Following this, Gyananjay Singh was removed from Hapur and posted as DCP in the Prayagraj Police Commissionerate. Police working in Jaunpur had also faced questions In September, police action came under question after the Karanja Kala firing and a murder case in Jaunpur. Action was taken against 10 policemen. Several station in-charges were changed on September 20, while two policemen were sent to the police lines. On September 24, five accused, including two policemen, were arrested in cases related to extortion and illegal collection. Questions had been repeatedly raised over the way the police were working in the district.

stories.title: Rajpal Yadav’s cheque-bounce case:Actor to sell ancestral property to clear dues; SC agrees to payment plan
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has accepted actor Rajpal Yadav’s proposal to sell his ancestral property to clear the outstanding dues in a long-running cheque-bounce case linked to a loan taken for his 2012 film Ata Pata Laapata. The court also took note of arrangements made for an immediate payment of ₹2 crore. ₹1.15 crore ready, buyer to pay another ₹85 lakh According to a Bar Bench report, a three-judge Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted that Rajpal Yadav had brought demand drafts worth ₹1.15 crore, which will be deposited with the court registry. Rajpal has been directed by the Supreme Court to deposit the remaining ₹85 lakh by October 13, 2026, after presenting a demand draft of ₹1.15 crore toward a ₹2 crore total interim payment. Another ₹85 lakh is to be paid by a prospective buyer of Rajpal's ancestral property The buyer, who was present in court, has agreed to deposit the amount by 11 October Monday. The court said that once the payment is made, it will lay down a schedule for clearing the remaining dues. The counsel said- We have ₹1.15 crore already. We also have a buyer of the ancestral property. The only difficulty is that Pitru Paksha is going on and people do not want to get the registration done. The buyer is also present in Court. He is ready to come forward and pay ₹85 lakh so as to reach ₹2 crore. He does not want to go in for registration of the sale documents at this point. He wants Navratri to commence, which is from Monday onwards. But he is ready to pay ₹85 lakh in advance. Ancestral property is valued at more than ₹30 crore Rajpal Yadav’s counsel told the court that the ancestral property is valued at more than ₹30 crore. The complainant’s counsel agreed to the proposal and said that if ₹2 crore is paid immediately, Rajpal could be given three months to clear the remaining amount. Case linked to ₹5 crore loan for film Ata Pata Laapata The dispute relates to around ₹5 crore that Yadav and his wife received from Murli Projects for the production of Ata Pata Laapata. After the film could not be completed within the agreed timeline, the parties entered into multiple agreements concerning repayment. Rajpal had issued security cheques to the company, several of which were later presented and dishonoured. This led to criminal complaints under the Negotiable Instruments Act. The Delhi High Court had earlier upheld Yadav’s conviction and sentenced him to three months in prison. The Supreme Court proceedings followed Yadav’s challenge to that order. After surrendering at Tihar Jail Rajpal Yadav surrendered before the jail authorities and remained in prison until the Delhi High Court temporarily suspended his sentence after he deposited ₹1.5 crore with the complainant. Then- Supreme Court earlier warned Rajpal Yadav The latest development comes days after the Supreme Court strongly criticised Rajpal for failing to comply with its earlier direction to deposit ₹2 crore. On 5 October, the court gave him another deadline and warned that his place was in jail if he failed to honour the payment undertaking. The Supreme Court had strongly criticised Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav for failing to deposit ₹5 crore. During the hearing in Rajpal Naurang Yadav Anr v. M/S Murli Projects Pvt Ltd, Rajpal Yadav produced a copy of a ₹50 lakh demand draft and said that the amount was being processed by the bank. "Is this genuine or not? We don't know," the Bench remarked. Rajpal Yadav's counsel said the draft was with the bank and was being processed. ‘He is a film actor and acting here also’: Counsel Counsel appearing for Murli Projects accused the actor of showing disregard for the Court. "He is a film actor. He is acting here also. He has no respect for the majesty of the institution," the counsel said. When Rajpal's counsel argued that the complainants were not poor, Justice Bagchi strongly objected. ‘You should know when to open your mouth’: Judge "They may be richer than you, but they are poor to the extent you have swindled them. This arrogance needs to be put in its right place. You should know when to open your mouth. Your place is in jail," the judge said. ₹2 crore payment plan considered During the latest hearing, on 7 October, the court considered the proposed property sale and the immediate payment arrangements before deciding to proceed with a schedule for the remaining dues.

stories.title: Imran Masood on SP-Congress seat sharing:Says finalise seats, respect grand old party; ‘It isn’t 2017, it’s party of 2027’
stories.summary: Amid the tussle between the Samajwadi Party and the Congress over seat-sharing ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Congress's newly appointed working president and Saharanpur MP, Imran Masood, has demanded that the allocation of seats be finalised soon. Masood said the Congress wants to give the SP the lead in the alliance, but the party's dignity and share should also be taken into consideration. Masood said: "Our only demand is that you finalise this many seats now. Proceed only after finalising them. Respect our dignity, and we will take care of your dignity." He said that the Congress was no longer the Congress of 2017. It was the Congress of 2027. The party had undergone considerable changes over the past ten years. Despite this, the Congress wants the SP to remain in the lead in the alliance. Masood said his party and its workers also had their own aspirations, and that it was his responsibility not only to save the party but also to take it forward. 'We are ready to accept whatever proposal Akhilesh makes' Signalling flexibility in the Congress's stance on seat-sharing, Masood said that the party was ready to accept whatever proposal Akhilesh Yadav put forward. He said both parties had to contest the election together and that it was important to maintain mutual respect. Masood had earlier also said that the seat-sharing agreement should be finalised soon. The statement came at a time when Akhilesh Yadav, responding to a question about seat-sharing, had said, "It is not about the seat, but about the victory." In response, Masood had said that the point was correct, but "there can be no victory unless there is a seat." 'There is a storm called Rahul Gandhi; only those who stand with him will remain' Linking the alliance and the Congress's role to Rahul Gandhi's leadership, Masood said, "This is Rahul Gandhi's storm. Those who stand with him will remain with him, while the rest will be blown away like pieces of straw." Calling it a battle of ideologies, he said the contest was between two ideologies. According to him, those who remain with Rahul Gandhi will stay with him in this political battle. He said there was now no middle path left. Rhetoric intensifies over seat-sharing between Congress and SP Before the 2027 election for Uttar Pradesh's 403 Assembly seats, leaders have continued to issue statements over seat-sharing in the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance. The Congress leadership has said the parties will contest the election under the alliance and that seat-sharing will be finalised soon. Akhilesh Yadav, meanwhile, is stressing the chances of victory and the unity of the alliance rather than the number of seats. Rajendra Gautam, the Congress's Uttar Pradesh in-charge, has also said that the formula for an alliance with the SP must be settled in October at all costs. This will give candidates sufficient time to prepare. He expects the SP leadership to allocate at least 150 seats to the Congress.

stories.title: Ashutosh Dixit, educated in Lucknow, to head Air Force:Family linked to DAV College; to become new IAF chief on October 31
stories.summary: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who studied in Lucknow, will take command of the Indian Air Force. The central government has appointed him as the next Chief of the Air Staff. He will take charge on 31 October after the retirement of the current Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh. He has a long-standing connection with the capital Ashutosh Dixit has had a deep connection with Lucknow. He completed his early education in the capital. His father, PC Dixit, was a sociology teacher at DAV Degree College. The family lived in Lucknow for a long time. This is why his appointment has generated particular excitement among people connected with the capital. Has flown aircraft ranging from the Mirage-2000 to the Tejas Ashutosh Dixit is an experienced fighter pilot. During his nearly four-decade military career, he has clocked more than 3,500 hours of flying. He has flown several aircraft, including the Mirage-2000, MiG, Jaguar, Tejas and Hawk. He is also an experimental test pilot and a qualified flying instructor. Has been part of several important military operations In his career, Dixit has served in several important military operations. He has been associated with Operation Safed Sagar, Operation Rakshak and Operation Sindoor. He has also commanded a fighter base in the western sector and a fighter training base in the southern sector. From Vice Chief to Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is currently the Vice Chief of the Air Force. He has previously served as Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Central Air Command and as Chief of Integrated Defence Staff. He has also held several important positions at Air Headquarters. Received four major military honours For his services, he has been awarded the Vayu Sena Medal, Vishisht Seva Medal, Ati Vishisht Seva Medal and Param Vishisht Seva Medal. After assuming office on 31 October, he will become the country's 29th Chief of the Air Force.

stories.title: Probe begins into wrong surgery at BHU Trauma Centre:CMO forms panel on Human Rights Commission’s directive; surgery performed on March 7
stories.summary: A fresh investigation has begun into the alleged wrong surgery performed on a patient at the BHU Trauma Centre on March 7, 2026. Acting on the directions of the Human Rights Commission, Varanasi Chief Medical Officer (CMO) Dr NP Singh has formed a team to investigate the case. The patient, who was undergoing treatment for a spinal cord tumour, was allegedly taken to the operation theatre for surgery on another patient with a leg fracture. Doctors reportedly made an incision in her thigh before realising that they had the wrong patient. The Human Rights Commission has also written to the District Magistrate seeking an investigation. The Institute of Medical Sciences (IMS), BHU had earlier conducted an internal inquiry and submitted its report to the commission. However, the commission raised objections to the report and asked the DM and CMO to conduct a fresh investigation and submit a report. The woman died at the hospital on March 27, a few weeks after the incident. Her family had lodged a complaint. CMO asked to examine treatment and medical records The woman, who was admitted to the BHU Trauma Centre on March 7, was a neurosurgery patient. According to CMO Dr NP Singh, the Human Rights Commission has directed the authorities to form a team and conduct a fresh investigation. The team has also been asked to examine treatment records, medical documents and investigation reports related to the surgery. What happened at the BHU Trauma Centre? Two patients named Radhika were admitted to the Trauma Centre. One was suffering from a spinal cord tumour, while the other had a leg fracture. On March 7, the woman suffering from the spinal cord tumour was allegedly taken to the operation theatre for the fracture surgery. During the procedure, doctors reportedly did not find the fracture they were expecting. They then suspected that the wrong patient had been taken into the operation theatre. The incision on her thigh was stitched and she was sent back, according to the family's complaint. She later underwent neurosurgery on March 18. The woman died at the hospital on March 27. Family complained to BHU Vice-Chancellor The woman, Radhika Devi, 71, was from Ballia. Her grandson, Mrityunjay Pal, complained to BHU Vice-Chancellor Prof Ajit Kumar Chaturvedi and IMS-BHU Director Prof SN Sankhwar. The Vice-Chancellor sought a report, following which the alleged lapse came to light. The family also alleged that the subsequent internal inquiry was not handled properly. According to the complaint, Dr Amit Rastogi, whose team was allegedly involved in the incident, was initially made chairman of the inquiry committee. After the issue came to light, the inquiry officer was changed. Radhika Devi had been suffering from a spinal cord tumour. Her grandson Mrityunjay Pal brought her to the Trauma Centre on February 25. She was examined by Dr Anurag Sahu in the neurosurgery department and admitted for treatment. After investigations, March 7 was fixed as the date for surgery. According to a complaint submitted by Mrityunjay Pal to the IMS-BHU director on April 1, the neurosurgery team was supposed to operate on his grandmother. However, he alleged that a team of orthopaedic doctors took her to the operation theatre instead.

stories.title: UP flood situation worsens:Neem Karoli Taposthali submerged in Lucknow, schools flooded; 6-foot crocodile enters Shahjahanpur colony
stories.summary: Five districts in Uttar Pradesh are in the grip of severe flooding, with six rivers flowing above the danger mark. In Lucknow, the Gomti's water level has continued to rise for the ninth consecutive day. Floodwater has entered the Neem Karoli Taposthali, while the Khatu Shyam and Chandrika Devi temples have been submerged. Around 40,000 houses in the Faizullaganj area are waterlogged. Government and private schools have also been flooded, while streets and main roads remain under water. With water and food supplies becoming a concern for people trapped by the flooding, some families have started leaving their homes. Water continues to flow through residential areas in Sitapur In Sitapur, water from the Sarayan and Kathna rivers is still flowing through residential areas. In Gonda, 10 villages are affected by the floods. 6-foot crocodile enters Shahjahanpur colony In Shahjahanpur, a 6-7-foot-long crocodile entered a residential colony along with the floodwater. Residents managed to capture the crocodile after considerable effort.

stories.title: Lucknow guard shoots dog for barking:Stopped his bike, got off and fired at it with his rifle
stories.summary: A dog was shot dead after it allegedly barked at a man riding a motorcycle in the Talkatora area of Lucknow district. The entire incident was captured on CCTV, which showed the man stopping his bike, taking out a rifle and shooting the dog before leaving the spot. The incident took place around 6.30 am near Green Field School in Rajajipuram. An NGO later approached the police and lodged a complaint. CCTV captures entire incident According to the CCTV footage, three dogs started barking at the man as he rode past the area. He stopped his motorcycle and got off after apparently becoming angry. He then took a rifle from his shoulder, took a bullet from his pocket and loaded the weapon before firing at one of the dogs. The dog died on the spot, after which the man left the area on his motorcycle. The man was wearing a blue uniform and a helmet and appeared to be a security guard. However, his identity and occupation have not yet been confirmed. First, 3 pictures... Police register case Inspector Kuldeep Dubey said a case had been registered and that the accused would be identified with the help of CCTV footage. Police said further action would be taken after identifying him. Two similar cases reported earlier Around four months ago, a young man named Raman Gautam allegedly beat a dog to death with an iron rod in Lucknow. He then dragged the body to a canal and threw it into the water. A video of the incident later surfaced, following which police arrested Gautam and sent him to jail. Youth killed dog, skinned its body In another case reported in Lucknow around the same time, a young man allegedly killed a dog and removed its skin. According to villagers, the man first caught the dog and brutally beat it. He then allegedly slit its throat with a sharp weapon before skinning its body. A video of the incident also surfaced. After it emerged, a large number of villagers reached Nigohan police station and lodged a complaint against the accused.

stories.title: 4 cricketers killed on Purvanchal Expressway:Ertiga crashes into truck at around 100 kmph; 2 injured
stories.summary: Four cricketers were killed and two others injured after their Ertiga crashed into the back of a truck on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur early Wednesday. The players were travelling from Lucknow to Deoria when the accident occurred around 5 am. According to the police’s preliminary investigation, the accident may have happened after the driver dozed off. The car was travelling at around 100 kmph, police said. The Ertiga was badly damaged in the collision. Passers-by and Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) security personnel broke open the car doors and pulled those trapped inside to safety. The injured were taken by ambulance to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared three people dead. Three injured people were then referred to Ayodhya Medical College, where one more person died. The accident took place under Baldirai police station limits. ‘We were all asleep when the car crashed’ Injured survivor Jayanto Sharma said everyone in the car was asleep when the accident occurred. “We woke up when the car crashed. We saw that the car had rammed into a truck. Our companions were covered in blood. Passers-by broke open the doors and pulled us out,” he said. See pictures… Four players killed The deceased were identified as Nitya Prajapati, 22, Irfan Ansari, 20, Anant Yadav and Aniket, 24. Nitya, Irfan and Anant were from Deoria, while Aniket was from Bhagalpur. The injured were identified as Raju, 22, from Deoria and Jayanto Sharma, 30, from Birbhum district in West Bengal. Aniket’s family Aniket was from Churiya village under Lar police station limits in Deoria district. His father, Amarjeet Singh, works as a salesman at a liquor shop, while his mother, Rambha Devi, is a homemaker. His younger brother, Ankit Singh, is a student. He also had two sisters, Riya and Rishu. His family members said Aniket was a very good cricketer.

stories.title: Son leaves to get mother’s medicine, returns 6 hours later:Lucknow flood leaves feverish woman without drinking water amid waterlogged streets
stories.summary: There is water everywhere in Faizullaganj, Lucknow, but there is little drinking water. Sick and elderly residents are struggling to get medicines, while family members can take hours to reach them through the flooded streets. In the 10 days since the flooding began, three deaths linked to illness have been reported in the area. Meena Kannaujia died in Kailash Vihar on October 2, one-and-a-half-year-old Shifa died in Lohra Mau on October 3, and 72-year-old Banshilal, who had a fever, died in Annapurna Nagar on October 5. A Dainik Bhaskar reporter visited the flood-hit area on October 7 to assess the situation on the ground. While travelling by boat, the reporter heard someone shouting from a distance: “Boatman brother, come here... please come here.” The reporter asked the boatman to stop. A young man was walking through waist-deep water towards the boat, carrying a sack containing essential items, including his mother’s medicine. See two pictures- Could not get home for 5 hours because no boat was available The man, Aakash, had been calling out to the boat. Seven people were already travelling in the old, damaged boat. The boatman repeatedly had to scoop out water that was leaking into it as he moved forward. When the boat reached Aakash, he said he had walked nearly 3km through waist-deep water to get there. Aakash said his mother was ill and that he had left home around five hours earlier to get her medicines. However, he could not return because he could not find a boat. The worry about his mother was visible on his face. The boatman allowed him to board and eventually took him home. When Aakash reached home and saw his mother, there was visible relief on his face. She was burning with fever. Here are some pictures of the flood- ‘There is no water to drink. How will we survive?’ Prabhat Devi was in tears as she spoke. “It is almost 3 pm, but I have not eaten even a grain of food or had a sip of water. One son is with me. My other son has taken his sick children to a friend's house,” she said. She said the family had waited for around three hours for a boat. “When no boat came, my son left with the children. There is water inside the house. We have been sitting on the roof in the sun since morning. We do not even have a sip of drinking water. I do not understand how we will survive,” she said. Prabhat Devi said her condition had deteriorated during the night. In the morning, her son stopped around 10 boatmen and asked for help, but no one came. He eventually walked nearly 4km through water up to his chest to get her medicines. It took around six hours to get the medicine and return. “We feel completely helpless. I have never experienced such suffering in my life,” she said. ‘Woman died because she could not get treatment’ Utkarsh Mishra, a resident of Daudnagar, said the area was flooded with water up to chest level. “No municipal corporation or administration official is coming to see the situation. The condition is extremely bad,” he said. He said an elderly woman in the neighbourhood had been suffering from fever for several days. Because of the flooding, she could not be taken to hospital in time and died. “For the first time, we had to take out a funeral procession through the floodwater,” he said. Utkarsh alleged that political leaders visit the area to seek votes during elections and show a sense of belonging, but no one was coming forward to help during the crisis. He said a plan to build an embankment had been approved around 10 years ago, but it has still not been constructed. ‘20,000 families forced to leave’ Ashutosh, who came from Aliganj to distribute relief material in Faizullaganj, said the situation was heartbreaking. “Seeing the conditions here makes you want to cry,” he said. He claimed around 20,000 families had been forced to leave their homes. He also said valuable belongings kept on the ground floors of around 40,000 houses — including televisions, refrigerators and air conditioners — had been destroyed. “Crores of rupees have been lost, but even basic help is not reaching people from the government. Small children are not even getting milk. People surrounded by floodwater are desperately looking for drinking water. There is so much suffering here,” he said. ‘Goods worth thousands destroyed’ Adarsh, who was standing in floodwater on the ground floor of his house, said water had surrounded his home for a week. His shop is also located inside the house. As the water rose, he managed to move some goods to the first and second floors, but goods worth more than ₹10,000 were still damaged. He said people living in rented accommodation above the shop had also left their belongings behind and moved away. There was no information about when they would return. Power had also been cut for the previous 24 hours. With no way to charge mobile phones, contacting people was becoming difficult. Adarsh said the biggest concern was that thefts had also started in some homes amid the crisis. “We are surrounded by problems from every side,” he said. Finally, two more pictures-

stories.title: Pundarik Goswami says, 'Ram Mandir consecrated under Yogi govt':Krishna Janmabhoomi should regain grandeur; ‘World learns etiquette from Lucknow’
stories.summary: Kathavachak Pundrik Goswami has said the grandeur and divinity associated with Lord Krishna should also be restored in Mathura, while praising the Yogi Adityanath government for its work on security, religious places and administration. Goswami is currently in Lucknow, where his Shrimad Bhagwat Radha Raman Katha is being held at the DAV College ground in Ashiyana from October 4 to 10. In an exclusive conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Goswami spoke about the Ram Mandir, Krishna Janmabhoomi, the Yogi government, religious discourses ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Gen-Z, mobile phone addiction and Lucknow's culture. Here are the key excerpts from the interview… Question: Yogi Adityanath is a saint. How do you view his tenure as Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister? Answer: There have been major improvements in two or three areas in Uttar Pradesh. People have particularly experienced a major change in terms of fear and security. There was a time when women were afraid to step out after evening. There has been a major change in that situation today. There has also been significant control over land mafias in religious areas. From an administrative perspective, the firmness of this government is remarkable and unique. Another important thing is that, over the past few years, Lord Vishwanath and Lord Ram have been re-established in our lives. Whatever way you look at it, this is a major change in our lives. Question: How do you view the allegations of donation irregularities in Ayodhya and the formation of a new committee? Answer: This is a matter of administration. The important thing is that the matter came to light and immediate action was taken. The system was changed and an effort was made to correct it. It was unfortunate because I have also served there. But it is not that the matter was ignored or treated as normal. Changes were made. The committee was replaced, a process for disciplinary action was put in place and changes were also made among those holding positions. The investigation and the overall process are still under way. Therefore, it would not be appropriate to use very harsh words so quickly. We should have faith in the process that is under way. I would like to make one suggestion. When we have built the architecture of a temple according to Indian traditions, our temples have also traditionally had their own systems of management. At our Radha Raman Temple, there is a position called bhandari. The bhandari manages the temple's stores, donations and other related matters. There are qualifications and a proper process for the position. Ancient Indian temples had large properties, which were protected for years. There was a system behind this. Therefore, the traditional service and management systems followed by ancient temples should also be incorporated into the management of such large religious places. This could further reduce the possibility of administrative mistakes. Question: Should Mathura also have the grandeur and divinity of Krishna Janmabhoomi? Answer: Mathura is associated with Shri Krishna and Balarama, so the divinity and grandeur of Lord Krishna should also be established there. Processes in this direction are already under way. I would appeal to people not to treat this as a government issue or as any party's agenda. It should be viewed as a distinctive feature of Indian identity. The party that understood the importance of this received the people's love. Even if a party comes to power 40-50 years from now, Ram, Krishna and Shiva do not belong to any party. They belong to the entire country. If every party moves forward by paying respects to them, giving them importance and expanding places associated with them, the people of India will show it their love. Question: Religious storytelling events have increased ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. How do you view this? Answer: What harm is there in that? A religious discourse is like the wish-fulfilling Kalpavriksha tree. Whoever is in need can sit beneath the tree of the discourse and have their wish fulfilled. The intention of the person organising the discourse can be anything. Some listen to it with financial goals in mind, some for fame, some for service and some with the aim of attaining salvation. What matters is that the person organising it remains sincere towards the discourse and that it serves to awaken religious and cultural consciousness. Today, everyone is beginning to understand that, within Sanatan Dharma, the Bhagavata and Ram Katha are forms of discourse that directly touch the hearts of the people. The discourse has been described as a wish-fulfilling tree. Therefore, whatever desire prompts someone to seek its shelter may be fulfilled. Even if someone has a political objective, the discourse can fulfil that objective as well. The good thing is that the person has at least sought the shelter of the discourse. Question: What is your mantra for maintaining the impact of a Katha for a long time? Answer: The biggest mantra is sang shuddhi — choosing one's company carefully. Suppose you buy a piece of land. If the municipal corporation turns the neighbouring plot into a dumping ground, the value of your land will fall several times over. But if a famous cricketer buys the neighbouring plot, its value will increase. If the land around us can affect the value of our land, then the people we live with also affect our lives. You felt good during the Katha because the entire atmosphere there was spiritual. After that, it becomes very important to consider who the people around us are and whom we spend time with. The scriptures speak about sang shuddhi. If your company is good, you can experience Vrindavan even while living in Lucknow. Therefore, we should choose our friends and company wisely. If your company is spiritual, the joy and impact of the Katha will remain in your life even after it ends. Question: Some people consider Gen-Z misguided, while others see it as an aware generation. What do you think? Answer: My birthday was celebrated at Talkatora Stadium on July 20, around 100-200 metres from Jantar Mantar. Around 5,000 Gen-Z people were present there. One Gen-Z group was protesting, while another was around me at the stadium. So tell me, which one was Gen-Z? Social media will not decide who Gen-Z is. We were also wondering whether people would turn up, but perhaps more people were sitting in that stadium than were present at that protest. Therefore, Gen-Z should not be defamed. For political purposes, Gen-Z, Alpha or Millennials can all be influenced. But today's Gen-Z is also showing great interest in the religious world. Look at this Katha pandal — around 70% of the people sitting here are Gen-Z and are listening to the Katha. So I think the term is a good one. Gen-Z is simply a generation born during a particular period. It is logical and rational, and it also has a strong interest in religion. We know that Gen-Z. Question: How do you view mobile phone addiction? Answer: Anything in excess is harmful. Even drinking too much water can harm the body. Anything that goes beyond its limit will cause harm. Society has used different mediums at different times. When books were common, the term ‘bookworm’ emerged. When television arrived, people started talking about ‘couch potatoes’. Now that phones have arrived, we talk about ‘phone addiction’. The problem has remained the same in all three periods: excessive use of anything is harmful. The reach of phones is much wider today. We are also present on Reels and try to ensure that good content reaches people. The responsibility is to use the right things in the right amount. If the habit of watching and listening to good things grows, it will benefit society. Question: Maharaj ji, how do you view Lucknow? Answer: Lucknow is a very beautiful and remarkable city. The whole world learns manners from Lucknow. This is Lakshmanpur and it is a city centred on service. In the entire story of Lord Ram, Lakshman established the spirit of service and dedication. The same values can still be seen in this city. What Lucknow says reaches the entire state. Uttar Pradesh is so large that what happens here reaches the entire country and then the world. That is why I am always excited to come here. The audiences here are very well informed and listen to the Katha with great dignity and refinement. We conduct Kathas in many places, but Lucknow has a long tradition and culture of listening to religious discourses. First Katha at Vice-President's residence From January 1 to 7, 2025, former Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar listened to a Shrimad Bhagwat Katha by Pundrik Goswami at the Vice-President's residence in New Delhi. It was described as the first Katha held at the Vice-President's residence. Pundrik Goswami is the grandson of renowned saint Atul Krishna Goswami Maharaj and the son of well-known Bhagwat Katha preacher Shreebhuti Krishna Goswami Maharaj. He belongs to the tradition of Shri Gopal Bhatt Goswami, one of the six Goswamis of Vrindavan.

stories.title: 4 Gurukul students die in Vrindavan:Victims entered tank to clean it, exposed to toxic gas; one rescued
stories.summary: Four students studying at a gurukul in Vrindavan died after they entered a water tank to clean it and were apparently exposed to toxic gas. One other student was rescued and is in critical condition. The incident took place at Maharshi Panini Sanskrit Gurukulam in Chaitanya Vihar. The students entered the tank around 10 pm to clean it. See pictures One student collapsed inside tank According to people at the gurukulam, one student entered the tank first but soon lost consciousness, apparently after being exposed to toxic gas. When the other students called out to him, he did not respond. Four other students then entered the tank one after another to rescue him. They also lost consciousness, triggering panic at the gurukulam. Police pulled all five students out of the tank and took them to hospital. Doctors declared Manu Katare, 20, Devansh, 17, Vishu, 18, and Aryan, 18, dead. Rudraksh, 18, remains in a critical condition. Manu and Devansh were from Jabalpur and Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh, respectively. Aryan was from Kaushambi, while Vishu was from Meerut. District Magistrate Chandra Prakash Singh reached the spot and spoke to the students and people at the gurukulam. According to SSP Shlok Kumar, speaking to a news agency, said, DM Chandra Prakash Singh said the gurukulam had a water tank about 12 feet deep. There was a foul smell coming from the tank, following which five students entered it to clean it. “Possibly due to toxic gas, four children died, while one child is completely healthy and survived,” the DM said. He said an investigation was underway to determine how and why the incident happened and who was running the gurukulam. He added that Chief Minister Mohan Yadav had taken immediate cognisance of the incident and that all possible assistance would be provided to the families of the victims. According to a person at the gurukulam, the students first used a motor to drain water from the tank. Some water remained, which they removed using buckets. Once the water had been drained, one student went inside and became unconscious. Other students then entered the tank to rescue him. Gurukulam has 120 students Maharshi Panini Sanskrit Gurukulam in Chaitanya Vihar provides Sanskrit education and currently has around 120 students. It is run by a person known as Ashish Guruji. The three-storey building has 43 rooms and the gurukulam has been operating for the past three years. Local resident Deepak Datt Dubey said one student had initially entered the tank to clean it. After he became unconscious, four other students went inside to rescue him and also lost consciousness. All five were subsequently pulled out.

stories.title: Nitin Nabin in Kashi says Opposition fighting for infiltrators:Himanta says, ‘Rahul, listen, you can’t harm Modi’
stories.summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Wednesday accused Leader of Opposition in Delhi Rahul Gandhi of trying to create anarchy over the issue of anti-social elements during his visit to Varanasi, asking, “The question arises: whose fight is he fighting?” His remarks came alongside Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's assertion that “earlier, the moment a mafia set its eyes on land, it became theirs.” The Opposition is talking about giving rights to infiltrators, but the people of India will never allow them to be given these rights. If the names of such people are removed from the voter list through SIR and questions are raised about democracy over it, then the question should be raised against the Opposition itself. The people of the country will respond to this anarchist thinking. UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said, “Earlier, there was a reign of anarchy. At that time, the picture of UP looked frightening to all of us. But today, under Modi ji’s guidance, the mafia has been reduced to dust.” Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma warned Rahul. He said, “Listen to this. As long as the power of Sanatan exists in India, you cannot even harm Narendra Modi.” In fact, Opposition MPs are protesting in Delhi, demanding the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul Gandhi said Gyanesh Kumar is not a legitimate election commissioner and must be removed. On Tuesday, MPs of the INDIA bloc had taken out a march. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that people have witnessed the changing Kashi and Uttar Pradesh over the past 12 years. He said that there was a time when the situation in UP was such that any land where a mafia figure set foot would be considered his. Similarly, any land that caught the eye of a Samajwadi Party worker would also become theirs. Yogi said that at that time, daughters were afraid to step out of their homes after sunset, while traders were forced to live in an atmosphere of fear. Before festivals, disturbances would begin instead of celebrations. There was a reign of anarchy, and the picture of UP looked frightening.

stories.summary: Amitabh Bachchan has apologised to the people of Babupatti village in Uttar Pradesh’s Pratapgarh district over the delay in opening a library named after his father, Harivansh Rai Bachchan. Speaking on Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC), the actor promised that the library would open soon. The library, inaugurated by Jaya Bachchan on March 5, 2006, has remained unused for nearly 20 years. Although the building was constructed, books never arrived, and a lack of maintenance has left it in a dilapidated condition, with broken windows, doors and flooring. A Dainik Bhaskar team visited Babupatti, around 30 km from the district headquarters, and spoke to villagers. While Amitabh’s latest assurance has revived their hopes, some residents say he has made similar promises on KBC before without any visible results. Read the full report… Amitabh Bachchan has never visited his ancestral village Babupatti, in Raniganj tehsil, is the ancestral village of poet Dr Harivansh Rai Bachchan. Amitabh Bachchan has never visited the village. The Bachchan family donated its land in the village, where the library was subsequently built. In 2004, then Samajwadi Party MP from Machhlishahr, CN Singh, contributed ₹22 lakh from his MP Local Area Development Scheme fund towards its construction. On March 5, 2006, Jaya Bachchan and Amar Singh visited Babupatti to inaugurate the library. Jaya Bachchan had promised to return with Aishwarya During her visit, Jaya Bachchan offered prayers and performed an aarti at the Chaura Devi shrine. She also met women from the village. Jaya told villagers that she would return with her daughter-in-law, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, after her son Abhishek Bachchan’s wedding. She also spoke about getting a girls’ degree college established in the village. The visit raised hopes that the Bachchan family would return and contribute to the village’s development. However, the college never opened, and Jaya did not return with her son and daughter-in-law. The library building was constructed, but books never arrived. Without maintenance, it gradually fell into disrepair. Its windows and doors are broken, and sections of the flooring have also been damaged. Amitabh apologises to villagers on KBC On Friday, October 2, Chandraprakash Tiwari, a resident of Dadwa Mahokhari village in Patti tehsil, appeared opposite Amitabh Bachchan on the hot seat of Kaun Banega Crorepati. When asked about his village, Tiwari did not name it directly but said he was from a village near Babupatti. Hearing the name prompted Amitabh to speak about his family’s ancestral village and the delayed library project. Amitabh said, “This was the birthplace of our ancestors. My father came from there. We wanted to do something there, but there were some obstacles. The people there are very angry with us. We apologise to the people of Pratapgarh and Babupatti. We will open the library. Please do not worry.” He added that the idea had come from his wife, who felt that children in the village needed a place to study. “My wife had gone there, and it was her idea that there was no place for children to study. Why not build a library for them? I agreed. The building was constructed, but it has been lying empty. Now, we will fill it with books,” he said. Villagers hopeful but recall earlier promises Despite previous assurances that did not lead to a visit or the opening of the library, villagers say Amitabh’s latest statement has renewed their hopes. Rishabh Dwivedi, a resident of Babupatti, said villagers felt proud when the actor acknowledged the delay and apologised. However, he added that the actor did not need to apologise if the promised work could be completed. “Whenever KBC airs, Amitabh Bachchan remembers the village. He has spoken about visiting and doing something for us on the show three times before, but there was no response afterwards,” Dwivedi said. He added that he had been trying to contact Amitabh Bachchan and his family through messages on X, formerly Twitter, and Instagram for the past 10 years but had received no reply. Purushottam Dwivedi said Amitabh had given several assurances but had not visited the village. “Amitabh has given many assurances, but he has not come. There is a feeling of disappointment that such prominent people make promises, but we do not see the results. This time, I am completely hopeful that he will come. Everything has its time. If we get the chance to welcome him to our village, we will feel blessed,” he said. Another villager, Amitabh Srivastava, said his family was delighted by the actor’s statement and hoped he would visit. He suggested that some difficulties might have prevented the actor from coming earlier. Fresh development plan raises hopes Separately, the Dr Harivansh Rai Bachchan Prabodhan Pratishthan, an organisation based in Maharashtra, has adopted the village under the Matrubhoomi Yojana. Under the first phase of the development plan, ₹1 crore is proposed to be spent on the village. The organisation will contribute ₹1 crore, while the Panchayati Raj Department will sanction an additional ₹40 lakh, according to the report. The department has approved the proposal, and the village is now awaiting the organisation’s funds. The proposed works include a concrete road named after Dr Harivansh Rai Bachchan, streetlights and a library. Vikas Yadav, the village head/administrator, said the organisation’s founder, Nivrutti Yadav, may visit Babupatti on October 11. He said the information had been conveyed by phone around 15 days earlier.

stories.title: Congress, which sought 200 seats in UP polls, surrenders:Fields no candidate for any of 11 MLC seats; aspirants kept waiting
stories.summary: Congress, which has been seeking an equal share of seats from the Samajwadi Party (SP) for an alliance in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, has surrendered in the MLC polls. The party has not fielded a candidate for any of the 11 MLC seats. Aspirants kept waiting until the last day of nominations for the party to take a final decision. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to eight candidates who had been campaigning with the Congress flag for the past 10 months. They said the party had betrayed them. They now face the challenge of protecting their political credibility. Read the full report... Congress had announced 5 graduate, 3 teacher MLC candidates Congress had announced five candidates for the MLC elections last year. They included Vikrant Vashishtha from the Meerut-Saharanpur graduate seat, Raghuraj Singh Pal from the Agra graduate seat, Dr. Devmani Tiwari from the Lucknow graduate seat, Sanjay Rai Priyadarshi from the Varanasi teacher seat, and Arvind Singh Patel from the Varanasi graduate seat. Later, after Dr Devmani Tiwari withdrew from the Lucknow graduate seat, the party replaced him with Sarita Mishra. Congress also announced Dev Bhaskar Tiwari from the Gorakhpur-Faizabad teacher seat, Ajay Kumar Singh from the Prayagraj-Jhansi graduate seat and Akash Agrawal from the Agra unaided teachers' seat. Congress had set a target for these candidates to enrol as many voters as possible. Campaigns were also launched for this purpose. The party later claimed to have enrolled more than 800,000 voters. ‘The in-charge kept assuring us until 3 days before nominations closed’ Raghuraj Singh Pal, Congress's announced candidate from the Agra graduate MLC seat, belongs to the Dhangar community. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, he said, “Everything was going well. We spent a year travelling around and enrolling voters. We raised the Congress flag.” “We had established the party firmly in an MLC election where nobody used to even mention Congress. On October 2, Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’ was appointed as the new state president. Then, on October 3, we were told that the party would not contest the MLC elections.” ‘I called the state president, and she said, “Whom should I speak to this early?”’ Arvind Singh Patel, Congress's announced candidate from the Varanasi graduate seat, said, “If the party itself does not want to contest the election, it should at least support us. The state president had assured us that she would speak to senior party leaders about this.” Patel said, “I called the state president at 9 am on October 6, the last day for nominations. She said, ‘Whom should I speak to this early?’ She had met the Congress high command in Delhi just a day earlier.” ‘Congress betrayed us at the last moment; I have nothing to do with the party now’ Akash Agrawal, who had earlier served as an independent MLC from the Agra unaided teachers' seat, took a different route from the other candidates. After Congress went back on its word, he contacted the SP chief and was subsequently declared the party's candidate. The remaining candidates are now contesting as independents. Sanjay Rai Priyadarshi, who is now contesting independently from the Varanasi teacher seat, said, “I had been involved in SP politics from the beginning. The SP has fielded Lal Bihari Yadav from this seat. Getting an SP ticket was difficult, which is why I joined Congress. For a year, I travelled across the eight districts under the Varanasi seat and built a voter base. I have 16,000 voters directly connected to me through my social groups. But Congress betrayed me at the last moment.” Raghuraj Singh Pal has also filed his nomination as an independent from the Agra graduate seat. Similarly, Dev Bhaskar Tiwari, principal of Mau DAV College, has filed his nomination as an independent from the Gorakhpur-Faizabad teacher seat. MLC polls seen as litmus test ahead of UP Assembly elections The elections for 11 MLC seats in Uttar Pradesh are being seen as a litmus test ahead of the Assembly elections. The results could indicate the public mood ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls. The SP and BJP have announced their respective candidates, while Congress has refused to contest the MLC elections altogether. The elections are being held for five graduate and six teacher quota seats. Only graduates and teachers will be eligible to vote. A strong performance in these elections could give a party a morale boost ahead of the Assembly polls. The results could also provide an indication of which way the political winds are blowing in the state.

stories.title: Ravita and lover found guilty of killing husband:Strangled him, then left snake on bed; sentence to be announced on October 16
stories.summary: A Meerut court on Wednesday found Ravita (24) and her lover Amardeep (27) guilty of killing her husband Amit. The couple had allegedly strangled Amit 17 months ago and then left a snake on his bed to make his death look like a snakebite. The court has reserved its final order in the case. The sentence will be announced on October 16. Ravita, who has been lodged in the women’s barrack of Meerut District Jail for the past year, was brought to court for the hearing. Amardeep, who is out on bail, was also to be presented before the court. Woman officer brings Ravita to court Woman sub-inspector Anu Collis, who had arrested Ravita, brought her to the court for the hearing. Anu Collis was seen smiling while taking Ravita to the court. This was also the first time the woman officer appeared before the media after the QR code case. Amit Kashyap alias Mikky, a resident of Akbarpur Sadat village, lived around 4 km from the Meerut-Pauri Highway. Police said Ravita and their neighbour Amardeep were in a relationship. Amardeep worked with Amit in tile and stone fitting work and often visited his house. According to the police, Ravita and Amardeep strangled Amit and then left a snake near his body on the bed. Snake found under Amit’s body Amit was found dead at his house on April 12, 2025. A snake was found trapped under his body. The family initially suspected that he had died after being bitten by the snake. The snake was caught and kept in a box. Snake charmers were called to catch and identify the snake. They caught a viper but said it did not have a poison gland under its teeth. The gland had been removed, meaning the snake could not kill a person by biting them. This increased the family’s suspicion. Marks were also found on Amit’s neck, along with scratch marks on his body. Police then sent the body for a post-mortem. The post-mortem report showed that Amit had died due to suffocation, not a snakebite. Police then started investigating the case as murder. During the investigation, they learned about the alleged relationship between Ravita and Amardeep. Police claimed that the two had planned the murder together. Police also questioned the person who had arranged the snake. Ravita and Amardeep were later arrested and sent to jail. Mobile calls became key evidence ADGC Farzana, who is representing the prosecution, said police filed a chargesheet of more than 500 pages. It includes statements of 12 witnesses and other evidence. She said the post-mortem report and mobile call records are among the most important evidence in the case. After Amit’s death, Ravita and Amardeep spoke to each other more than 70 times in four days. The mobile number used by Amardeep to talk to Ravita was registered in the name of a youth named Sonu from Jagriti Vihar. During his statement, Sonu said he did not use that mobile number and did not know Ravita or Amardeep. The investigation later found that Amardeep had obtained the SIM card in another person’s name and used it to stay in touch with Ravita. More than 500 calls between the two were found from the same number, which became an important piece of evidence. Both sides have completed arguments The trial is being heard in Additional District Judge Court No. 12. ADJ-12 Jaiveer Singh will pronounce the verdict. ADGC Farzana said all 12 prosecution witnesses have completed their statements and arguments from both the prosecution and defence sides have also been completed. Amardeep will be brought before the court for the verdict, while Ravita will also be brought from jail. The court may award life imprisonment if they are found guilty. Ravita had accused husband of assault While being taken to jail, Ravita had alleged that Amit used to beat her every day and behaved badly with her. She claimed that he knew she spoke to Amardeep on the phone and had himself made her talk to him. Ravita also claimed that Amit had told her he would call Amardeep to the house and asked her to help him kill Amardeep, saying he would later kill her too. Amardeep had said before being sent to jail that he had an argument with Amit over a ₹3,500 money dispute a few days before the murder. He claimed that some people later helped them settle the dispute, but Amit had allegedly sent some men to attack him. Amardeep said he then planned Amit’s murder to save himself. He also told police that he bought the snake for ₹1,000 from snake charmers in Mohammadpur village in the Mawana area. He claimed that one of their associates came and sold the snake to him.

stories.title: Youth collapses during police recruitment run, never gets up:Suffers chest pain after 9 laps in Ghaziabad; holds pole before collapsing
stories.summary: The 23-year-old man from Shamli suddenly fell ill while participating in a police recruitment race in Ghaziabad on Tuesday. After completing around nine laps, he complained of chest pain and stood holding onto a pole for some time. Tried to resume running but collapsed After some time, he attempted to resume the race but suddenly collapsed on the ground. Police personnel rushed him to the Joint District Hospital in Sanjay Nagar, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place around 1 pm on Tuesday (6 Oct). Vivek was preparing to join the police force Candidates were undergoing the physical test for police recruitment at the ground of the 47th Battalion PAC in Govindpuram from October 3 to 9. The race began around 11 am on Tuesday. Vivek, son of farmer Balendra and a resident of Purmafi village in Shamli, had also arrived to take part in the test. Vivek started running with the other candidates and completed nine laps. However, he soon began feeling unwell and developed breathing difficulties. Despite this, he tried to continue running but suddenly collapsed on the ground and did not get up. Family in mourning after promising youngster’s death Former village head Bijendra Kumar said Vivek was a bright student and had been preparing for recruitment into the police force. His father, Balendra, is a farmer, while his mother is a homemaker. Vivek was the younger of two siblings, and his elder sister is married. The family was devastated after receiving news of his death. His body was later taken to Purmafi village, where his last rites were performed in a sombre atmosphere that evening. Station House Officer Virendra Kasana said they had received information that Vivek, a resident of Purmafi, had taken part in the recruitment process and fallen ill. He was admitted to hospital, where he died.

stories.title: Friend killed over ₹15,000 in Prayagraj:Five boys repeatedly strike his head with cleavers, cut off one finger
stories.summary: Five friends jointly killed a 17-year-old boy in Prayagraj. They repeatedly attacked his head with a cleaver. The boy had lent his friends ₹15,000. His friends then cut off a finger from one of those hands. Shantanu had been missing since Monday night. His body was found lying by the Manseta drain on the banks of the Ganga on Tuesday morning. After receiving the information, police reached the spot and questioned his family members and local residents. Police have arrested four friends, including Ujjwal, who is accused of the murder. Now read the entire incident in sequence Shantanu Dubey, 17, was a resident of the Kohna settlement in Jhunsi. His father, Deepak Dubey, is a pilgrimage priest. According to the family, Shantanu left home at around 9:30 p.m. on Monday. When he did not return for a long time, his family began searching for him. However, there was no trace of Shantanu. On Tuesday morning, police were informed that the body of a boy was lying in the bushes near the Manseta drain on the banks of the Ganga. When the police reached the spot, they found injury marks on the body. It emerged that he had been attacked on the head with a sharp-edged weapon. Police tried to have local residents identify the body. Later, family members who reached the spot identified it from Shantanu's T-shirt. The family told police that Shantanu had received a call from someone before leaving home. Ujjwal killed Shantanu with the help of four friends Police officers had formed three teams to search for Shantanu under the leadership of ACP Jhunsi Arun Parashar. The investigation from different angles revealed that Shantanu was friends with some youths who lived in Jhunsi. He was also involved in a dispute with one of them over ₹15,000. As the police took the investigation forward, they found that one of the young men had been missing since the previous night. This deepened their suspicion of his friends. The family members said that the young man involved in the dispute over money was named Ujjwal. Police searching for Ujjwal detained him on Tuesday evening. He initially continued to deny having any knowledge of the incident. When the police questioned him strictly, Ujjwal confessed to killing Shantanu. He said that he had killed Shantanu along with four friends. Ujjwal did not want to repay the borrowed money During questioning, Ujjwal said, "I borrowed ₹15,000 from Shantanu several months ago. I work at an ice cream factory. My friends and I used to spend time with Shantanu. I was facing financial difficulties, so I could not repay the money." Shantanu kept pressuring me to return the money. About two and a half months ago, he even got his father and brother to beat me and my friend Harsh. He began demanding the money every day. I became fed up with this. I told my friends about it, and we then made a plan. We decided that I would return two or three thousand rupees. If he did not agree, we would kill him. After making him drink alcohol, repeatedly struck him with a cleaver As part of the plan, Shantanu was called over at 9:30 p.m. on Monday. He was first made to drink alcohol. They had eaten and drunk there several times before, so Shantanu did not suspect anything and came over. After he became heavily intoxicated, I began talking to him about money. My friends pinned him down, and I attacked him He told us to take two to three thousand rupees and settle the matter. He then started arguing and abusing us. That was when my friends pinned him down, after which I pulled out a cleaver and repeatedly struck him on the head. Bleeding heavily, he began to run, but stumbled and fell a short distance away. He could not get up again. After the murder, my friends and I left the body there and fled. City DCP Sagar Jain said, Based on a complaint from the family, an FIR naming five people has been registered. Four of them, including the main accused, have been taken into custody and are being questioned.
