stories.title: Sleeper bus catches fire on Noida Expressway:Passengers flee leaving belongings; hear explosion-like sound; second such incident in 12 days
stories.summary: A sleeper bus caught fire while travelling on the Noida Expressway on Tuesday evening. The passengers panicked and began running away, leaving their belongings behind. Fortunately, no one was injured. However, all the passengers' belongings were destroyed in the fire. The incident occurred near Sector 148 at around 5:30 p.m. There were 32 passengers on board. According to eyewitnesses, a sound resembling an explosion was heard inside the bus when it caught fire. The flames then spread rapidly. Within a short time, the entire bus was reduced to ashes. This is the second incident of a moving bus catching fire within 12 days. Earlier, on 24 September, nine passengers were burnt alive when a sleeper bus caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway. See 3 pictures... Now read the details... According to the police, the bus (BR28P3433) was travelling from Delhi's Red Fort to Muzaffarpur in Bihar on Tuesday. It caught fire on the expressway in the Knowledge Park area of Greater Noida. Passengers panicked after the bus conductor raised the alarm. Passengers rushed to get off the bus. They left their belongings inside and got out. A fire brigade team reached the spot as soon as it was informed about the fire. Firefighters brought it under control after considerable effort. The cause of the fire has not yet been ascertained. The bus belongs to Jamna Travels. It was registered with the Gopalganj RTO. Greater Noida ADCP Abhay Kumar Mishra said information had been received that a bus travelling to Bihar had caught fire. As soon as the information was received, fire brigade and local police teams reached the spot and brought the fire under control. He said 32 passengers had boarded the bus in Delhi. All the passengers have been safely evacuated, and arrangements have been made to take them to their destinations. He said eyewitnesses suspected that the fire had been caused by a short circuit in the engine. However, the exact cause of the fire is being investigated. Further legal action will be taken in the case. 12 days ago, nine passengers were burnt alive in a bus A moving sleeper bus caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway on the night of 24 September. The bus was travelling from Delhi to Mahoba. Nine passengers died in the accident. Around 35 passengers were on board. Twenty-six passengers managed to get out and save their lives. In the FIR filed in connection with the accident, passengers said they had smelled something burning in the bus before it caught fire. The passengers alleged that they informed the driver and conductor, but the bus was not stopped in time. Police began investigating the case and also arrested the manager of the bus operating company.

Dharampal owns 3 weapons, Priyanka richer than husband:Shruti Gangwar has 1.25kg gold; how much property do UP BJP Rajya Sabha candidates own?
stories.summary: All eight BJP candidates for the Rajya Sabha elections filed their nominations on Tuesday. Their affidavits relating to assets and criminal cases show that one is fond of rifles and revolvers, while another is passionate about cars. When it comes to hobbies, Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Dharampal Singh stands apart. The minister has a particular fondness for firearms and owns a rifle and a revolver. In addition, a revolver is registered in the name of his wife, Vandana Devi. Gopi Krishna Pandey, who lives in Kanpur, is not far behind when it comes to a fondness for firearms. He owns a 'Webley Scott revolver' worth ₹2 lakh. Webley Scott is a highly renowned British weapons manufacturer. This revolver is known worldwide for its durability and lethal striking power. This is particularly significant for India, and especially Uttar Pradesh, because under the 'Make in India' initiative, Webley Scott's factory has been established in collaboration with an Indian firm, Sial Manufacturers Private Limited, in Sandila, Hardoi district. It is the first foreign arms manufacturer to set up a plant in Uttar Pradesh. When it comes to wealth, Jaunpur's influential leader, former Rajya Sabha MP and MLC Vidyasagar Sonkar is the wealthiest. With movable and immovable assets worth ₹16.41 crore, he is the richest among the BJP candidates. He has movable assets worth ₹2.16 crore and immovable assets worth ₹14.25 crore. His wife Rekha has movable assets worth ₹2.34 crore. Interestingly, she has no immovable assets, such as a house or land. The couple also owns around 925 grams of gold and 5 kg of silver. Radhakant Ojha is also part of this race to wealth, with assets worth ₹11.85 crore. He owns a premium Kia Carnival and an Alto. His movable assets are worth ₹3.87 crore and his immovable assets ₹5 crore. His wife, Sumitra Ojha, owns movable assets worth ₹2.07 crore and immovable assets worth ₹99 lakh. When it comes to education, Shruti Gangwar appears to be the most qualified. She studied chemical engineering at the University of Roorkee in 2000. The university is now known as IIT Roorkee. Shruti also leads in terms of gold and silver holdings. She owns around 1.25 kg of gold and 5 kg of silver. Their total value is estimated to be more than ₹1.5 crore. Priyanka Rawat has more assets than her husband, Raghunath. She is ahead of her husband in both movable and immovable assets. Priyanka has the highest liabilities. She has debt of around ₹1 crore, while her husband has debt of ₹37 lakh. Thus, among the eight candidates, the couple has the highest debt. OBC Morcha president Ramprakash Pal ranks last on the list of assets. He has total assets worth ₹1.37 crore (₹19.86 lakh in movable and ₹1.17 lakh in immovable assets). He owns just two scooters. One is registered in his name and the other in the name of his wife, Neetu Pal. Interestingly, Ramprakash himself travels on an old 2015-model scooter, while his wife owns a new 2021-model scooter. Agra's Rampratap Singh is the only candidate facing criminal cases. There are two cases against him. One case was registered in Lucknow under sections related to holding an unlawful public meeting, rioting and promoting enmity between different groups. The other case was registered in Agra for printing election material without identification. Both cases are pending in court.

stories.title: Thai wife arrives at Kanpur businessman’s home:Claims he married her, cheated her of ₹60 lakh; now wants her to change religion
stories.summary: A Kanpur leather businessman allegedly tricked a Thai woman into marrying him two years ago, then cheated her out of ₹60 lakh in the name of starting a business. When the woman asked businessman Mohammad Irfan to return her money, he began refusing. The businessman came to Kanpur from Thailand and stopped answering his wife's calls. On Monday, the woman, Upsorn, reached his house on Latouche Road in search of her husband. There, she learnt that the man she had married was already married. The woman said, "I met Mohammad Irfan when he came to Thailand for business." "We were in a relationship there for four years. We got married two years ago. After the wedding, Irfan came to Thailand to meet me every two months. Meanwhile, he cheated me out of my money. When I asked him to return it, he set the condition that I leave Thailand, live here and convert my religion." The woman lodged a complaint about the entire matter with ADCP East Shiva Singh on Tuesday. She also handed over her wedding photographs and other documents to the police. The investigation was handed over to ACP Anwarganj Manjay Singh. The ADCP said an FIR had been registered on the basis of the woman's complaint. Irfan has been taken into custody. Now, here is the full story in chronological order... He used to stay at the woman's home in Thailand on business trips Upsorn, a woman from Thailand, told ADCP Shiva Singh, "Mohammad Irfan, a resident of Latouche Road, is a tannery businessman. He often travelled to and from Thailand for business. During this time, we became friends on Instagram. Later, when Irfan arrived in Thailand, we met. After that, whenever Irfan came to Thailand, he would stay at my house." Upsorn said, "While we were in a relationship for nearly four years, Irfan proposed marriage to me. Two years ago, we got married according to Thai customs." Upsorn also showed the ADCP her wedding invitation, photographs, passport and other documents. Woman says she was pressured to change her religion Upsorn said, "When I asked Irfan to return my money, he began putting me off. Irfan told me that if I wanted to live with him, I would have to convert to Islam and remain in a burqa. I refused to do so. Irfan then returned to India in February 2026. Initially, he claimed that he was ill." After that, he stopped answering my calls and blocked my number. When I was unable to contact him despite calling several times, I came to Kanpur on Monday. Accompanied by an acquaintance, I went to Irfan's house on Latouche Road. There, I learnt that Irfan was married. I then went to the ADCP with Advocate Mehtab Ali to file a complaint. The businessman's first marriage took place 14 years ago Following a complaint by the Thai woman, Upsorn, the police began investigating the case. The investigation revealed that Irfan's first marriage in Kanpur took place in 2012. He has three children. He runs a tannery in partnership in Jajmau under the name Irfan Tannery. Rehan is also a partner in the business. Now, read the police questions and the woman's answers... Police: Did he actually hide the fact that he was married? Thai woman: Yes... Besides, when I asked him to return my ₹60 lakh, he said I would have to change my religion and come to India to live with him. Police: When did you find out that he was already married? Woman: Yesterday, when I went to his house. That was when I found out that he had been married for 14 years. He also has three children. Police: What do you want from the government and the authorities? Woman: I was deeply shocked yesterday. I just want my money back. All I want is for the Government of India to help me recover my money. I have to make payments every month to a bank in my country. I also have to repay the people I borrowed money from. ADCP Shiva Singh said, Irfan married a woman from Thailand after giving her false information. He also took around ₹60 lakh. When she demanded the money back, he told her to live permanently in India and convert her religion. The matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Priya Saroj flaunts desi look in purple saree in US:MP Iqra Hasan says, ‘Stunning beauty’; to marry cricketer Rinku on December 4
stories.summary: Cricketer Rinku Singh's fiancée and Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj is currently in New York, US, where she attended an event wearing a purple sari. Priya has shared her pictures on Instagram, and they are receiving a great deal of appreciation. Her colleague in Parliament, Iqra Hasan, also praised her. She wrote, "Wow, beautiful," meaning, "What stunning beauty." Priya Saroj attended events in New York linked to the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. In a social media post, she said that a briefing was held at the United Nations on India's participation as part of a delegation of MPs. This was followed by discussions with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) on inclusive and sustainable development. Seen in a saree with a pink border Priya wore a purple saree during the event, with a pink border. The saree's pallu had light embellishments. She paired it with a matching blouse. Her overall look had no excessive embellishments, and she kept her style quite simple. See 3 pictures of Priya Saroj on foreign soil... Light jewellery and natural makeup Priya wore light jewellery with her sari. Small earrings, a watch on her wrist and a small black bindi on her forehead completed her look. She wore light makeup and initially left her hair loose, later tying it into a bun. Priya's traditional Indian look was well received even on foreign soil. People on social media are praising her simplicity and elegant look in the pictures. Rinku and Priya to marry in Lucknow on 4 December Cricketer Rinku Singh and Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj will get married on 4 December at the Ramada Hotel in Lucknow. Both families have begun preparations for the wedding. Rinku and Priya got engaged on 8 June 2025 at The Centrum Hotel in Lucknow. Several prominent guests from the worlds of cricket and politics are expected to attend the wedding. Priya Saroj became an MP at the age of 25 Priya Saroj was born on 23 November 1998 in Karkhiyanv, Varanasi. After turning 18, she joined the Samajwadi Party and remained active in the party's programmes. At the age of 25, she defeated the BJP's BP Saroj to win the Lok Sabha election. Her father, Toofani Saroj, has also served as a three-time MP from Machhlishahr. Rinku's father delivered gas cylinders Rinku Singh said in an interview that his father worked delivering gas cylinders. All five brothers in the family also helped their father with his work. Rinku started playing cricket amid financial difficulties. As he could not afford club cricket, he practised at a government stadium. For a tournament, his mother borrowed ₹1,000 from a shop and gave it to him. Rinku and Priya first met at a cricketer's wedding Rinku Singh and Priya Saroj first met around three years ago at a cricketer's wedding in Delhi. After Rinku hit five sixes in IPL 2023, he grew closer to senior cricketers. Around this time, the wife of a senior cricketer introduced Rinku to her friend, Priya Saroj. Priya and the cricketer's wife had studied together at Delhi University. Priya holds a BA LLB degree from Delhi University. The meeting at the wedding ceremony gradually turned into conversations and then a relationship.

Ten years ago, those who had become a menace used to target police officers and create fear and panic. Today, when they see a police vehicle, they wet themselves. No one can dare harass a girl walking along the road or a sister who has stepped out for work. They know that if anyone behaves in this manner, their next journey will not be in this world but in the next. CM Yogi was speaking in Lucknow as HCL Tech marked 10 years. He said Uttar Pradesh had completely changed over the past 9.5 years. Earlier, electricity was reserved for a few families. Now, it is available in every home. Today, young people from across the world have to come to Lucknow for their careers.

stories.title: Patient dragged 200m on floor in Ayodhya:Admitted for 3 days; CMS says person was helping
stories.summary: Patient admitted to Ayodhya District Hospital was dragged along the ground for 200 metres across the hospital premises. A young man held the patient by both hands and dragged him across the floor. The incident took place at 1 p.m. on Monday, but the video emerged on Tuesday. Chief Medical Superintendent (CMS) Dr Rajesh Singh, clarifying the matter, said that the person who dragged the patient was not a member of the hospital staff. He was an attendant accompanying another patient. Patient was brought in an ambulance on Saturday The video shows a young man holding the patient by the hand and dragging him along. The scene is from the corridor outside the district hospital’s laboratory. During this, several people can also be seen walking past. According to CMS Dr Rajesh Singh, the patient was brought to the district hospital by ambulance at around 6 pm on October 3. He was initially admitted to the general ward. As he had no attendant, he was shifted to the unattended patients’ ward at around 7 pm on Sunday. He is currently admitted to the same ward. Now read what the CMS said in his clarification He was taken to the laboratory for a sputum test CMS Dr Rajesh Singh said, "The patient was taken to the laboratory for a sputum test at around 1 p.m. on Monday afternoon. After the test, he was supposed to return to the ward. At that time, perhaps no hospital employee was present with him." For this reason, he asked a person present there to take him to the unclaimed ward. That person was an attendant of another patient. He dragged the patient by holding his hand. The distance between the laboratory and the unclaimed ward is around 200 metres. The CMS said that the person claimed he was helping the patient. The patient had asked him to take him to the unclaimed patients' ward, which was why he was taking him there. When some people told him that he was being filmed, he left the patient there. CMS says hospital employee stopped man from dragging patient When the CMS was asked about some people's claim that the young man had dragged the patient along the entire route in this manner, he said that as soon as hospital employees learnt that the patient was being dragged, an employee stopped the man on the way. The patient was then placed on a stretcher and taken to the unclaimed patients' ward. Social Worker Says: Conditions in Unclaimed Patients' Ward Are Poor Cow protector and social worker Ritesh Das has raised questions about the incident. He said the conditions in the hospital's unclaimed patients' ward were poor. No one was available to look after it. The patients remained distressed. He said he would complain about the matter to the Chief Minister and district-level officials. The care of unclaimed patients and the ward's arrangements should be investigated.

stories.title: Supporter tells Brij Bhushan he saw bicycle in dream:Former MP laughs, says ‘bhakk’...; crowd joins in laughter
stories.summary: A supporter of former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh reached his residence in Gonda on Tuesday to meet him. When Brij Bhushan asked how he was, the supporter said, "I dreamt last night that his election symbol was a bicycle." Brij Bhushan Singh burst out laughing on hearing this and, saying, "Bhakk," walked on. The people accompanying him also burst into laughter. The incident took place at 10 a.m. The supporter's name is Ravi Ranjan. He is a farmer. A video of this amusing incident has also emerged. See two photos... Now understand the full matter Brij Bhushan Singh left the gym at 10 a.m. and was on his way to meet the public. Ravi Ranjan, a resident of Semra Sheikhpur village, came to meet him. Ravi folded his hands and greeted Brij Bhushan. Ravi Ranjan said, "Baba, I have come on your behalf. I will vote for you. Your election symbol has been announced. Last night, I dreamt that your election symbol was a bicycle." Brij Bhushan said, ‘I am currently with the BJP’ When Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh was contacted about the development, he said, "There is a village nearby called Semra Sheikhpur. Ravi Ranjan is from that village. He had told people to make a video. When he was asked what he would do with the video, Ravi Ranjan said that he would go viral. At present, I am with the Bharatiya Janata Party." Brij Bhushan said, "He is free to say what he is saying. I cannot stop anyone. Many people come to meet me." Earlier, on 9 June, a video had gone viral in which he appeared to be asking Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh for money to buy a mobile phone. Brij Bhushan had said, ‘Good relations with Akhilesh’ There has also been discussion in recent days about the good relations between Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Both leaders have praised each other. On 30 September, Brij Bhushan had said, “I do not speak against him, and he does not speak against me. I am in the BJP and he is a Samajwadi Party leader. We have good relations.” There had also been speculation recently that Brij Bhushan Singh would go to the Rajya Sabha from the Samajwadi Party. However, dismissing the speculation, he had said that he would not contest the Rajya Sabha election and would contest the Lok Sabha election in 2029.

stories.title: Gyanesh Kumar’s mother says ‘demons dirtied home’:Sprinkles Gangajal after Congress writes ‘vote thief’ on Agra wall
stories.summary: The ancestral home of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in Agra was purified on Tuesday. Gyanesh Kumar's 76-year-old mother, Satyawati, said, "On 28 September, some people with demonic tendencies came outside the house. They had dirtied the house. It is now being purified." She said it was a religious ceremony. It was being conducted peacefully and for peace. Women from the Akhil Bharatiya Mathur Vaishya Mahasabha gathered outside the house. They were all dressed in yellow. The women took out a kalash procession. They then reached the CEC's house, where Gangajal was sprinkled as part of the purification ritual. The recitation of the Sunderkand is now under way. Gyanesh Kumar's ancestral home is in Vijay Nagar, Agra. On 28 September, Congress workers staged a protest outside the house. During the protest, the house wall and main gate were blackened with soot. The words 'vote thief' and 'traitor' were also spray-painted on them.

stories.summary: The police stopped the Save Democracy March of 19 opposition parties in Delhi, which was held to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav was detained. In protest, SP workers began demonstrations across Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday. In Gorakhpur, SP workers took to the streets and raised slogans of “Vote Chor, Istifa Do” (Vote thief, resign). Police tried to stop the protesters at several places. In Lucknow, a scuffle broke out between workers and police. Police dragged protesting SP workers along the road. In Agra, amid a scuffle with SP workers, policemen snatched the CEC’s effigy and ran away. One policeman tripped an SP worker, causing him to fall to the ground. He then slapped and kicked him. Meanwhile, in Delhi, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said, If Gyanesh Kumar is impartial, he should listen to us. This is about saving democracy. The police should not behave this way with children and protesters.

stories.title: Priyanka touches Yogi’s feet, files Rajya Sabha nomination:BJP’s 8 candidates file papers; all set to be elected unopposed
stories.summary: Eight BJP candidates filed their nominations for the Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha elections on Tuesday. Former Barabanki MP Priyanka Rawat and Gopi Krishna Pandey sought blessings from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath by touching his feet. Dharampal Singh was the first to file his nomination, while Shruti Gangwar, daughter of Jharkhand Governor Santosh Gangwar, was the last. BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary and both Deputy Chief Ministers, Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, were also present. After the nominations, a BJP worker got into an argument with a police personnel. The argument soon escalated into pushing, shoving and abusive language. BJP workers intervened and calmed both of them down. A video of the incident has also surfaced. SP's Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parmal Nathwani had already filed their nominations. The SP had initially planned to field a third candidate, but Akhilesh Yadav ruled it out. In such a situation, all 10 candidates for the Rajya Sabha seats are expected to be elected unopposed. Shruti Gangwar was the last to file her nomination See 2 pictures

stories.summary: The fourth video of Rasik Dulari Sharan, a disciple of saint Premanand in Vrindavan, from before his suicide has surfaced. It shows him leaving the room and walking towards the stairs. He is wearing a white half-sleeved kurta and a yellow dhoti. The 25-year-old Rasik Dulari is slowly making his way towards the gallery, staggering and adjusting his dhoti. It appears that he may have suffered an injury to his leg or elsewhere on his body. He walks 19 steps before turning towards the other side of the gallery to climb the stairs. Rasik Dulari Sharan died by suicide after jumping from the fourth floor of the Keli Kunj Trust building on the morning of 25 September. His last rites were performed on the banks of the Yamuna on 26 September. All four of his videos have surfaced over the past nine days. When asked by Bhaskar where the CCTV footage had come from and who was releasing it, the police said that an investigation was under way. More than 30 people associated with the Keli Kunj ashram have been questioned in the case. Learn about the four videos First video: The first video of Rasik Dulari Sharan's suicide emerged on 27 September. It shows Rasik Dulari Sharan suddenly falling feet-first onto the road from a height of 40 feet. His head hits the ground and splits open. He begins to writhe in pain. Blood begins to spread across the road. Meanwhile, two cyclists happen to be passing by. One of them was a disciple wearing yellow clothes. Both are shocked to see the scene. In addition, a vehicle supplying water also reaches the spot at the same time. Second video: The second video, which surfaced on 3 October, shows Rasik Dulari Sharan sitting on the roof's boundary wall. After six seconds, he lies down on the floor. He suddenly gets up and jumps from the boundary wall. Hearing the noise, another disciple rushes to the spot and looks down. Third video: In the 33-second third video that emerged on 4 October, Rasik Dulari Sharan is seen climbing the stairs to the roof. Bloodstains can be seen on his dhoti. As he climbs the stairs, he appears to be having some difficulty walking. Fourth video: A 12-second video emerged on 5 October. In it, Rasik Dulari Sharan can be seen coming out of a room. He is wearing a white half-sleeved kurta and a yellow dhoti. He has white sandalwood paste applied to his forehead. He is not wearing slippers or wooden sandals. He is walking slowly, staggering and adjusting his clothes. He then turns towards the other side of the gallery to climb the stairs. Had been living in Guru Kripa Kunj building for three months Rasik Dulari had been living in the four-storey Guru Kripa Kunj building in the Varah Ghat area of Vrindavan for three months. He took his own life by jumping from the building's roof. According to the police, Rasik Dulari Sharan was taken to Sarvodaya Hospital in critical condition, where he died. Eyewitnesses had claimed that Rasik Dulari was bleeding from his private parts. A grinder covered in blood was found in the room. It is suspected that the disciple injured his private parts with the grinder. Post-mortem finds cuts on private parts Rasik Dulari Sharan Das's post-mortem examination was conducted by a panel of two doctors on 26 September. It was also videographed. According to the preliminary report, injury marks were found on the head, legs and waist. In addition, cuts were found on the private parts. Took initiation from Premanand Maharaj two years ago Rasik Dulari Sharan was originally from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh. He came to Vrindavan around two years ago and took initiation from Premanand Maharaj. He subsequently changed his name from Deepak Lodhi to Rasik Dulari Sharan. He knew electrical work. Therefore, he was assigned this service at the ashram. Deepak was the second-born among two brothers and one sister. He had an elder sister, while his younger brother's name was Manish. Mother said: She was not allowed to meet him Loung Bai, the mother of Rasik Dulari, who arrived after being informed of her son's death, said that she had last spoken to her son two years ago. She received information that her son had fallen, after which she hurried to Vrindavan. She said that she had come to meet her son earlier as well, but was not allowed to meet him. She said that God would take action against those responsible.

stories.title: Air Force Day rehearsal in Ghaziabad:Helicopter flies with Tricolour over Hindon station, woman leads three-not-three drill for first time
stories.summary: Air Force Day will be celebrated on October 8. Ahead of Air Force Day, the Indian Air Force is conducting a rehearsal at Hindon Air Force Station on Tuesday. The rehearsal began around 8 am and will continue until the afternoon. Eight contingents of Air Force personnel, including 35 personnel and a flight leader, are taking part. For the first time, a woman Air Force personnel is leading the Three-Not-Three drill. The rehearsal began with the national anthem. Army helicopters are currently flying over the station carrying the Tricolour, while Air Force personnel and officers on the ground are saluting the national flag. All personnel are dressed in blue uniforms. The Chief of the Air Staff and several senior Air Force officers are present at the event. Their family members have also come to watch the rehearsal. The Air Force has also put up an exhibition of aircraft and weapons at the station. For the first time, the BrahMos missile (SSM) is being displayed during the Air Force Day rehearsal. The missile has been jointly developed by India’s DRDO and Russia’s NPO. See Photos

stories.title: Fire breaks out at labour room inside Lucknow airport:300m from terminal; smoke visible from 2km away, doused in an hour
stories.summary: A fire broke out at a labour room in the Lucknow airport complex on Tuesday morning. Six fire engines extinguished the blaze within two hours. The site of the fire is 300 metres from the terminal and 100 metres from the runway. However, flight operations were not affected. No casualties have been reported. The cause of the fire is not yet known. A temporary three-storey PVC building has reportedly been constructed in the airport complex. Around 300 workers live there. The workers are currently building a new hotel. The fire broke out at 6 a.m., triggering panic. It quickly spread throughout the PVC building. Smoke could be seen rising from 2 km away. stories.title: Principal’s testimony completed in Gorakhpur:Confirms school CCTV footage; constable raped and killed girl
stories.summary: The cross-examination of the fifth witness in the case involving the kidnapping, rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl from Gorakhpur District Hospital was completed on Monday. The Chief Legal Aid Defence Counsel completed the cross-examination of Garima Upadhyay, principal of Saraswati Vidya Mandir, Chiutahan, Maniram, in the court of the Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge, POCSO. The principal had provided the CCTV footage installed at the school to the investigating officer. The prosecution proved it in court as evidence. The hearing on other evidence will take place on 6 October. So far, the prosecution has produced five witnesses in the case. After the statements of the girl's elder sister and other witnesses were recorded, the principal of the school in Chiutahan was produced before the court in connection with evidence related to the CCTV footage. Her examination-in-chief was conducted first. She was then summoned again to have the pen drive containing the preserved footage authenticated. On Monday, the defence completed her cross-examination. Complete case details The girl suddenly disappeared on the night of 28 July after going to give food to her elder sister, who was admitted to the district hospital. A search by the family revealed that a young man wearing a police uniform had taken her away. As the investigation progressed with the help of CCTV footage and surveillance, it was revealed that constable Abhishek Yadav, posted with Dial 112 and a resident of Ghazipur, had abducted the girl. During questioning after being taken into custody, the accused admitted that he had killed the girl after raping her. The girl's body was found on 30 July on the banks of the Rohin river in Chiutaha. The constable was subsequently dismissed from service and sent to jail.

stories.title: 181 houses, mosques demolished in Kashi’s Dal Mandi:₹132 crore compensation paid, action continued for 12 months; model road by December
stories.summary: Under the Dalmandi project in Varanasi, 181 identified houses have been demolished. On Monday, the PWD took action against the remaining five or six houses using Pokland machines and JCBs. Workers also climbed onto the houses and demolished some sections by hand. According to PWD officials, no new houses now remain for demolition in Dalmandi. The identified sections of houses where action had already been taken are being separated and the structures are being completely razed. The target is to complete the entire dismantling work by the beginning of November. Along with the houses in Dalmandi, six mosques had also come within the project's scope. According to PWD officials, compensation of around ₹191 crore had been assessed for the buildings and mosques. Of this, around ₹132 crore has so far been paid to the affected people. KK Singh said the land acquisition process had been continuing. After the publication under Section 19, the affected people had been paid the compensation amount. Demolition began on 29 October 2025 For the Dalmandi project, 181 buildings were identified after the houses were measured in July 2025. The process of registration and compensation then began. Demolition action started on 29 October 2025. Public Works Department engineer KK Singh said 172 houses had been completely demolished. Around 70% of five or six houses had been removed, while machines and labourers carried out demolition work on the remaining five or six houses on Monday. They said that no new house remains to be dismantled. Work will continue to remove the remaining parts of the houses where action has already begun. Work on sewers, water supply and underground electricity begins Preparations for road construction have begun alongside the demolitions in Dalmandi. Work has started on laying a deep sewer line, drinking water pipeline and underground electricity cables from the Chowk police station side. The PWD aims to complete the new road and open it to the public by December if the work continues at the same pace. KK Singh said that opening the road to the public by December would be a major achievement for the department. He also described the district administration's support as crucial to the project. 650-metre road to be 60 feet wide Around 650 metres of road, from Dal Mandi's new road to Chowk police station, is to be developed as a model road. Under the project, the road will be around 60 feet wide. It will comprise a 30-foot carriageway and 15-foot pavements on either side. Electricity, sewerage and water infrastructure will be installed underground beneath the road. This will also eliminate the tangled network of electricity wires that has been visible in Dal Mandi for a long time. Here is what the Dalmandi project is about... Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for the project Dalmandi Lane in Varanasi is to be developed as a model road. The Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for the project during his 51st visit to Kashi. The state government has released ₹215.88 crore for it. As many as 186 building and shop owners will be paid ₹191 crore in compensation. Meanwhile, MLA Neelkanth Tiwari performed the ground-breaking ceremony for Dalmandi on 9 August. According to PWD officials, the 650-metre Dal Mandi lane from Nai Sadak to Chowk police station will be widened to 60 feet. It will have a 30-foot road and 15-foot pavements on both sides. Electricity, sewerage and water infrastructure will be installed underground. The tangle of overhead wires will be cleared. 650-metre road to be built at a cost of ₹220 crore Dal Mandi, which runs from Nai Sadak to Chowk police station, is 650 metres long. A proposal to widen the road to 17.5 metres has already been approved. For this, a budget of ₹215 crore was sanctioned on the last day of the 2024-25 financial year, and ₹2 crore was released. The PWD team surveyed the width of the road at each location and determined which houses fell within its alignment. After measuring 181 houses, the registration process began, followed by demolition work. Six mosques were also included. PWD officials prepared the data, based on which compensation was assessed. The amount is approximately ₹191 crore. So far, 172 houses have been demolished, and work is underway on nine houses.

stories.title: Businessman returning from birthday party, 2 sisters-niece killed:Scorpio hits dumper in Muzaffarnagar, falls 20 feet below highway
stories.summary: A businessman, his two sisters and his niece were killed in a road accident in Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh. His mother, wife and another niece are in a critical condition. The businessman was returning after celebrating his maternal uncle's 75th birthday in Haridwar when a dumper coming from the opposite direction rammed into the Scorpio. The Scorpio then fell about 20 feet below the highway. The accident took place in the Purkazi police station area, 40 km from the district headquarters. Passers-by informed the police after hearing screams. The police broke open the Scorpio's door, pulled everyone out and took them to a community health centre. Four people were declared dead there. The deceased were identified as businessman Adesh Goyal, his sisters Nisha and Rakhi, and Nisha's 14-year-old daughter, Shraddha. Adesh's mother, Kusum Devi, his wife, Ruby, and Rakhi's daughter, Vaishnavi, were injured in the accident. Two pictures of the accident- Read the full story... Property dealer Aadesh Goyal, a resident of Harinagar, 3 kilometres from the district headquarters, travelled to Haridwar in an SUV on Monday evening with his wife Ruby, mother Kusum Devi (65), Nisha (36) and her 14-year-old daughter Shraddha, and his younger sister Rakhi (30) and her seven-year-old daughter Vaishnavi. The family attended Mausa Radheshyam's 75th birthday party. After the programme ended, they were returning to Muzaffarnagar at around 11 p.m. The family had no idea that their journey back from the same ceremony where they had celebrated just a few hours earlier would turn into a tragic accident. Near the Solani River bridge at Badhiwala on the Purkazi-Laksar State Highway, a soil-mining dumper coming from the opposite direction collided forcefully with the Scorpio. The impact sent the Scorpio out of control, causing it to overturn into a ditch near the bridge. The occupants became trapped inside the vehicle. As soon as the accident occurred, passers-by reached the spot and informed the police. The police team began rescue operations with the help of local residents. As the field was waterlogged, rescuers faced difficulty getting into the ditch to bring out the injured. After considerable effort, everyone was pulled out and sent to the Community Health Centre in Purkazi. Brother, two sisters and niece die in hospital At CHC Purkazi, medical officer Dr Sumit Chaudhary declared Adesh Goyal, his sister Nisha, younger sister Rakhi and Nisha's daughter Shraddha dead. The family was thrown into turmoil after receiving news of four deaths at once. Adesh's mother Kusum Devi, his wife Ruby and Rakhi's daughter Vaishnavi were injured in the accident. As all three were in critical condition, they were referred to a higher medical centre. Son Tushar's wedding was scheduled for 25 November After the accident, the dumper overturned some distance away. Its driver fled the scene. Police are searching for him and investigating the circumstances of the accident. Upon receiving the information, SDM Praveen Kumar Dwivedi also reached the spot and inspected the site. Order's son Tushar is scheduled to get married on 25 November. Amid the wedding preparations, the deaths of four family members at once plunged the household into mourning. The family had been celebrating just a few hours earlier after returning from the birthday celebration, but the accident left everyone in deep shock.

stories.title: Flood-hit residents say ration is fine, but embankment needed:CM says compensation for collapsed homes; embankment work to begin soon
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath visited the Itaunja area on Monday to meet people affected by the floods. He spoke to the families and assured them of help. Relief material and ration kits were distributed to around 300 flood-affected families. The Chief Minister said compensation would be provided as per the rules if homes were damaged or collapsed in the floods. Medical and veterinary camps would be set up in the affected areas. Arrangements would also be made for green fodder for livestock so that people did not face any difficulties. The villagers appeared pleased with the Chief Minister's visit. They said the relief material was good, but building embankments to prevent floods in the future was more important. They said villages were affected by floods every year. The Chief Minister assured the villagers that preparations to build embankments for permanent protection from floods would begin soon. The administration would be given the necessary instructions in this regard.

stories.title: STP remains unchanged despite Governor’s reprimand:Students say it isn’t operational; VC claims STP is running
stories.summary: The status of the sewage treatment plant (STP) at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapeeth remains unclear. Around two months ago, on 28 July, Governor Anandiben Patel expressed displeasure at the fact that the STP had not been made operational despite being constructed during the convocation ceremony. She ordered the university to start the STP within a month. Despite this, students say they have not seen the STP operating even once. In response to an RTI query, the university had said that 90 per cent of the STP's work had been completed. It added that operation was not possible as the work was still in progress. The vice-chancellor, however, claims that the STP is operational. Students have demanded that if the STP is running, the university should provide details of how much water is being treated in it. Students said - They have never seen the STP operating, nor has the sewer line been dug Yuvraj Pandey, who has been studying at the university since 2020, said he had never seen the STP operating. He said that if the STP was functioning, its operation should be visible on the campus. He also said that it had been stated that a sewer line would be laid to carry sewage to the STP, but he had not seen any excavation or pipeline being laid on the campus for this purpose. Aakash, who has been studying at the university for around four years, also said he had never seen the STP operating. He said he had not seen any excavation work being carried out to lay the sewer line. Former student Aakash Rai, who filed the RTI application, said the RTI informed him that operating the STP is currently not possible because the work is still in progress. Students say that if the university claims the STP is operational, it should provide information on how much water is being treated, its daily treatment capacity and where the treated water is being used. Governor directed that the STP be made operational within a month On 28 July, Governor Anandiben Patel raised the issue of the STP at the convocation ceremony of Kashi Vidyapith. The Governor had said that the STP had been built but was not operational. She had directed that it be made operational within a month. Nearly two months have passed since the Governor's directive. Despite this, students claim they have not seen the STP being operated. Vice-Chancellor claims: STP is operational Meanwhile, the university vice-chancellor says that the STP is operational. This indicates a discrepancy between the claims of the university administration and the students regarding the operation of the STP. The students say that if the plant is actually operational, information related to its functioning and records of water treatment should be made public. Information provided under the RTI: 90% of work completed, 80% payment made Former student Aakash Rai had sought information about the STP from the university through an RTI application. In its RTI response issued in 2026, the university stated that work on the STP and sewer line had been carried out in 2023. The cost of the STP, which has a capacity of 250 KLD, was stated to be ₹154.12 lakh, while the cost of approximately 1,600 running metres of sewer line was stated to be ₹111.60 lakh. In response to the RTI, the university said that around 90 per cent of the work had been completed and around 80 per cent of the payment had been made. It also said that the remaining work was in progress. In another response, it was stated that the installation of the STP was in progress and that it had not been commissioned because the work was incomplete. ‘Documents that surfaced after the RTI raise questions about the situation’ Former student and RTI applicant Aakash Rai said he had filed an RTI application in 2025 seeking information related to the STP. Dissatisfied with the initial response, he appealed, and the matter reached the State Information Commission. Following the hearing on 14 September, he received information from documents related to the STP and sewer line. Aakash Rai said the documents state that the STP has a capacity of 250 KLD, cost ₹154.12 lakh and include details of around 1,600 metres of sewer line. He questioned the actual status of the sewer line, saying that its construction was also part of the project. He said that he and other students had not seen any excavation being carried out on the campus for laying the sewer line. STP work was to be completed within three months under the MOU The university and the CDS wing of Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam (Urban) signed an MOU for the STP on 25 March 2023. Under the MOU, the executing agency was required to begin construction by 15 April 2023. The MOU set a three-month deadline for completing the STP work. This meant the work was to be completed by July 2023, according to the agreed timeline. It is now October 2026, meaning around three years and three months have passed beyond the deadline. The MOU included the installation of a 250 KLD STP as well as around 1,600 running metres of sewer lines. Despite this, the RTI response stated that around 90 per cent of the work had been completed in 2026 and that the remaining work was in progress. On the one hand, students are refusing to accept that the STP is operational despite the governor's directive to start it within a month; on the other, the vice-chancellor claims that the STP is running. The students are therefore demanding that records of the STP's operation and the water treated there be made public.

stories.title: UP BJP replaces old faces, bets on new ones:Brahmins, OBCs and Dalits in Rajya Sabha picks; sets 2027 strategy
stories.summary: The BJP has laid the caste groundwork for Mission 2027 through its Rajya Sabha nominations. The party has relied on its traditional vote banks among Brahmins, Kshatriyas, OBCs and Dalits. However, instead of betting on old faces, it has given new faces an opportunity. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP took the risk of fielding industrialist Sanjay Seth as its ninth candidate. But with the Assembly elections approaching, the party has this time avoided giving a ticket to any industrialist or prominent face. Instead, it has promoted its grassroots workers and core cadre. Two women get tickets By giving tickets to two women, or 25% of its eight Rajya Sabha nominees, the BJP has sought to move closer to the commitment under the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. To consolidate its Dalit vote, the party has increased the number of Dalit nominees by one compared with 2020. It has specifically chosen candidates from the Pasi and Khatik communities, both considered BJP vote banks. The number of Brahmin nominees has been retained at two. Among OBCs, the Kurmi, Pal (Gadaria) and Lodhi communities are considered BJP vote banks. The party has fielded workers belonging to all three communities. Dharampal Singh's stature rises Uttar Pradesh livestock minister Dharampal Singh's stature is set to rise both in UP politics and among the Lodhi community. Singh was a strong contender for the BJP state president's post in 2016 and 2025. However, caste equations prevented him from getting the post. The party has now chosen to send him to the Rajya Sabha instead. Dharampal Singh could now be inducted into the Modi Cabinet at the Centre in the coming days. Singh is currently 73 and will remain a Rajya Sabha member for the next six years, until he turns 79. Singh is older than two other prominent Lodhi leaders, Rajbir Singh Raju Bhaiya and BL Verma. By elevating his stature, the party has also sent a clear message that Dharampal Singh is its face among the Lodhi community. Ram Pratap lives up to party's trust BJP state general secretary Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan had lost the 2022 Assembly election from Agra's Etmadpur seat. The party recently reappointed him as state general secretary and made him in-charge of western UP. His appointment as western UP in-charge ahead of the Assembly elections had made it clear that he would not contest the polls. Ram Pratap Singh, who is considered close to state organisation general secretary Dharampal Singh, has now been made a Rajya Sabha candidate for his continued activity at the party office and to establish him as a new Thakur face in the Braj region. No third chance for these leaders BJP office-bearers say the central leadership has decided that those who have been made Rajya Sabha members twice or more will no longer be sent to the Upper House. Instead, they will be given opportunities to contest Assembly or Lok Sabha elections. Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Union minister BL Verma, Rajya Sabha MP Neeraj Shekhar and Arun Singh have lost their tickets under this formula. Arun Singh was also not included in the BJP's national team recently. These leaders failed to make an impact Political analysts believe that in 2020, the BJP sent Brajlal from the Dalit community, Seema Dwivedi from the Brahmin community, Neeraj Shekhar and Arun Singh from the Thakur community, Geeta Shakya from the Shakya community and BL Verma from the Lodhi community to the Rajya Sabha. However, the results of the 2022 Assembly and 2024 Lok Sabha elections showed that these leaders failed to live up to the party's expectations in their respective regions and communities. Neeraj Shekhar himself lost the election from Ballia. Brajlal failed to make a significant impact among Dalits, with Dalit (Jatav) votes beginning to shift towards the Samajwadi Party. Seema Dwivedi became embroiled in factionalism and controversies in Jaunpur and surrounding areas. The BJP's position also did not strengthen significantly in Arun Singh's home district of Mirzapur. After assessing the 2022 and 2024 election results, the BJP decided to replace these faces with new ones. Thakur resentment remains a challenge The BJP has reduced the number of Thakur representatives in the Rajya Sabha from two to one. Earlier, Arun Singh and Neeraj Shekhar were the party's Rajya Sabha members from the Thakur community. This time, only Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan has been given a ticket. Meanwhile, in the Legislative Council elections, the BJP has fielded five Brahmin candidates for 11 seats. From the Thakur community, the BJP has fielded only Kedar Nath Singh from the Varanasi Graduates' constituency and Manvendra Singh from the Agra Graduates' constituency. Among BJP state spokespersons too, 10 of the 32 are Brahmins and four are Thakurs. However, of the 99 current members of the Legislative Council, 24 are Thakurs, including 22 from the BJP. Despite this, the reduced representation of Thakurs has led to resentment among leaders of the community.

stories.title: How did kebab-paratha seller Armaan become Atiq’s shooter?:Shaista’s bodyguard, helped Ashraf’s plan succeed; police to record his statement in jail
stories.summary: Mafia don Atiq Ahmed’s shooter Mohammad Armaan has been sent to Gaya jail, with the Uttar Pradesh Police set to approach the special SC-ST court on Tuesday for permission to record his statement. Once permission is granted, the police will visit Gaya jail and record Armaan’s statement. The police will then question Armaan about the Umesh Pal murder case. Based on Armaan’s answers, the police will prepare grounds for seeking his remand. Using these points as the basis, the police will file a remand application in court. In fact, in the Umesh Pal murder case, Prayagraj Police officially arrested Armaan on Monday. He was then produced before the Prayagraj court at around 4.15 pm. Special Judge SC-ST Mayank Kumar’s court ordered that Armaan be sent to jail for 14 days. According to government lawyer Manoj Pandey, all documents related to the charges in the case were provided to Armaan in court. The court asked him whether he needed a lawyer. After Armaan said yes, his application was taken to provide him with a free legal counsel. The next date in the case has been fixed after 14 days. How did Armaan travel from Gaya to Prayagraj? How did he become associated with Atiq’s gang? When and how did he become so close to the family? Why and how did he end up in Gaya Central Jail? Read the report… First, read what happened on Monday Police produced Armaan before the Prayagraj court at around 4.15 pm on Monday. Special Judge SC-ST Mayank Kumar’s court ordered that Armaan be sent to jail for 14 days. Prayagraj Police will now file an application in court seeking Armaan’s remand. In fact, Prayagraj Police officially arrested Armaan on Monday in the Umesh Pal murder case. Meanwhile, following the court’s order, Bihar Police will take Armaan with them and lodge him in Gaya jail. If the court grants Armaan’s remand, he will be handed over to Prayagraj Police. Before he was produced in court, 40 policemen accompanied him for security. Armaan’s face was covered with a white gamcha. The media asked Armaan, “Where are Shaista Parveen and Guddu Muslim?” However, Armaan did not react to these questions. More than 100 policemen were deployed in the court premises during Armaan’s appearance. They included women police personnel, PAC personnel, three ACPs and commandos from Bihar Police. Armaan carries a bounty of ₹5 lakh. He had been lodged in Gaya jail in Bihar for the past three years. He was brought to Prayagraj from there on transit remand. Prayagraj Police told the court that Armaan had got his bail cancelled and gone to a Bihar jail. His arrest had not been shown in this case until now. After learning that he was in jail, the Uttar Pradesh Police formally recorded his arrest in this case and produced him before the court. Jaya Pal’s testimony underway, trial to gain momentum The case in which shooter Armaan was produced before the court is the same case in which the trial of 12 other accused is underway. At present, the testimony of the complainant, Jaya Pal, wife of Umesh Pal, is being recorded. Following Armaan’s appearance in court, the investigation into the case and further judicial proceedings related to it are also expected to move faster. How Armaan became Atiq’s shooter, read Opened a kebab-paratha shop, entered Atiq’s family through Guddu Muslim Mohammad Armaan, also known as Armaan Bihari, is originally from Gaya in Bihar. He came to Prayagraj 11 years ago. There, Armaan opened a kebab-paratha shop in the Rajapur area under Cantt police station limits. Atiq’s shooter Guddu Muslim used to supply chickens wholesale. It was during this period that Armaan came into contact with Guddu Muslim. He handed over the kebab-paratha shop to his younger brother Imran. After that, Armaan began staying with Guddu Muslim and started accompanying him. Through Guddu Muslim, he entered Atiq’s family circle. Through Guddu, he was also introduced to Nafis Biryani, a businessman close to Ashraf. Nafis had a shop called Eateon in Civil Lines. Armaan spent most of his time sitting at this shop. It was here that he met Sabir. Sabir was closer to Atiq’s family. Mohammad Ghulam used to stay with Atiq’s son Asad. It was through Sabir that Armaan came into contact with members of the family. Meanwhile, as Atiq and Ashraf were in jail, other close associates moved away. Asad and Ghulam went to meet Atiq, who was lodged in a Gujarat jail, and Ashraf, who was in Bareilly jail, through FaceTime. Guddu Muslim, Armaan and Sabir also went with them. They began visiting the two brothers in jail and became close to them. Used to stay with Shaista Parveen and move around as part of her security cordon During this period, on January 5, 2023, mafia don Atiq’s wife Shaista Parveen joined the BSP. The BSP declared her its candidate for the Prayagraj mayoral post. Shaista began meeting people in the city’s West area. During this period, Sabir and Armaan started accompanying Shaista. Guddu Muslim also stayed with her. All of them moved around as a security cordon. After Shaista received the ticket, mafia don Atiq, who was lodged in Sabarmati Jail in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and Ashraf, who was in Bareilly jail, allegedly hatched a conspiracy to eliminate Umesh Pal. Asad and Ghulam then went to meet Ashraf in Bareilly jail. The plan to murder Umesh Pal was made. Asad then went to meet his father Atiq in jail. Atiq told him to speak to Guddu Muslim, Sabir and Armaan and decide what role each of them would play. Asad and Ghulam met the three men and finalised their respective roles. The same shooters then killed Umesh Pal and his gunner. After the murder, Guddu Muslim and Sabir fled together. Atiq’s son Asad and Ghulam also fled together. Armaan, meanwhile, escaped from Prayagraj alone. Two days after the murder, Armaan got his bail cancelled in Gaya and went to jail. Later, Atiq Ahmed’s son Asad Ahmed and Ghulam were killed in a police encounter in Jhansi on April 13, 2023. Armaan had surrendered in court After the Umesh Pal murder, Armaan came to Gaya to evade the Uttar Pradesh Police. Armaan had allegedly opened fire at ‘Bholu Anda Wale’ near Katari Talab. A case had been registered against him in connection with the incident. He surrendered before the court in this case. After that, Armaan was sent to Gaya Central Jail. Now, know how UP Police reached Gaya jail The Uttar Pradesh Police had been searching for Armaan for the past three years. During this period, they learnt that he was lodged in Gaya Central Jail. After receiving the information, police from Prayagraj’s Dhoomanganj police station reached Gaya jail on September 30. There, the police took Armaan’s latest photograph and obtained his thumb impressions on plain paper. After completing the paperwork, the police returned to Prayagraj. On October 1, they filed an application in the Gaya court seeking transit remand. Armaan was seen firing with Guddu Muslim On February 24, 2023, Umesh Pal and his two government gunners were shot dead in broad daylight in Prayagraj. CCTV footage of the incident also emerged. A man riding a motorcycle was seen in the footage. According to the police, Armaan was riding the motorcycle and Guddu Muslim was sitting behind him. Armaan had brought Guddu Muslim to the crime scene on the motorcycle. As soon as the motorcycle stopped, Guddu Muslim opened fire. Armaan also fired shots. After the incident, both fled the scene on the motorcycle. The two main shooters in the murder case, Guddu Muslim alias Guddu Bombaj and Sabir, both carrying a bounty of ₹5 lakh, are still absconding. Atiq’s wife Shaista Parveen, Ashraf’s wife Zainab Fatima and Atiq’s sister Ayesha Noori are on the list of most-wanted accused. Family fears encounter After learning that Armaan was being brought to Uttar Pradesh, his father Shamim and mother Asgari Khatoon feared that he could be killed in an encounter. Armaan’s father had filed an application in the Gaya court. He had requested that Armaan not be handed over to the Uttar Pradesh Police. He said that if the police wanted to question him, it should be done through video conferencing. Most of the accused in the Umesh Pal murder case have been killed in police encounters. He feared that Armaan could also be killed in an encounter in the name of recovering a weapon. Mother had said, “He is being made a scapegoat” Armaan’s mother Asgari Khatoon had said, “My son is being made a scapegoat. Our family is very poor. We do not even have our own permanent house to live in. Armaan used to live in Prayagraj and do small jobs. He is neither a professional criminal nor a big shooter. He has been in jail for the past three years.” Armaan’s younger brother Imran had said, “We had already expressed our fear that my brother’s life was in danger. Now the Uttar Pradesh Police has taken him to Prayagraj. We are afraid that something may happen to Armaan too. The family will accept whatever decision the court takes. But Armaan must not be harmed in any way.” Armaan’s lawyer alleges collusion between jail administration and police The application filed by Armaan’s parents was heard in the court of Gaya Magistrate Saurabh Kumar on October 1. The court rejected the application filed by Armaan’s family and lawyer. Armaan’s lawyer Lalit Kumar Gupta confirmed this. Alleging collusion between the police and jail administration, the lawyer had said, “Armaan’s life is in danger. Armaan could be killed in Uttar Pradesh. A conspiracy is being hatched to kill Mohammad Armaan through collusion between the Uttar Pradesh Police and the Gaya Central Jail administration. “We had sought his appearance through video conferencing, citing security concerns, but the court rejected it. Armaan has been lodged in Gaya jail since February 27, 2023. He is being deliberately implicated in the Uttar Pradesh case.”

stories.title: Floods under scorching sun:Where did so much water come from? Upper areas’ rainwater took 3 days to reach Lucknow; situation may last a week
stories.summary: It has been around seven days since it last rained in Lucknow, with the monsoon having completely withdrawn from Uttar Pradesh and people sweating under intense sunshine, yet around 40,000 houses in the Faizullaganj area are facing a serious flood situation. With the Gomti in spate despite no rain, residents are wondering where so much water is continuously coming into the river. Read the report… The Gomti, unlike the Ganga and Yamuna, is not a Himalayan mountain river. It originates from Gomti Tal or Fulhar Lake in Uttar Pradesh's Pilibhit district. Monsoon rainfall provides the water flow for this river. It travels around 960 km through Shahjahanpur, Hardoi, Sitapur and Lucknow before joining the Ganga near Kaithi village on the Ghazipur-Varanasi border. The Gomti also has 6 tributaries. Small rivers and water streams such as Kathina, Sukheta, Choha and Sarayan flow through the plains and increase the flow of the Gomti. However, because the Gomti is a river originating in the plains, its flow is quite slow. This is why no major dam has been built on it. Only one barrage, the Gomti Barrage, has been built in Lucknow to control the river's water level and supply drinking water to the city. Where does the river begin and end, and which rain-fed rivers join it? Understand it through the map Warm, humid winds brought rain to Pilibhit, Lakhimpur and Sitapur A deep depression (warm and extremely humid winds) that developed over the Bay of Bengal caused heavy rainfall in Pilibhit, Lakhimpur Kheri, Sitapur and Hardoi on September 26 and 27. According to the Meteorological Department, Shahjahanpur received 162.1 mm of rainfall on September 26. This was 100 times higher than the average rainfall for that day. Similarly, Pilibhit received 56.1 mm of rainfall on September 27, whereas the normal rainfall for the day is only 2.2 mm. This was around 25 times higher than normal. Due to the distance of these districts from Lucknow and their geographical location, the water from the Gomti gradually began reaching Lucknow. Mukesh Vaish, Executive Engineer of the Irrigation Department's Lucknow Division, says, “The gradient of the Gomti is also very low. As a result, its speed is around 1 km per hour during normal days. Besides this, the Gomti passes through highly winding routes.” A distance that appears to be 250 km on the map becomes a journey of more than 350 km because of the river's meandering course. Even when water pressure rises during a flood, the river's speed reaches only 2 to 3 km per hour. This is why it took 3 days for the floodwater to reach Lucknow. Its impact began to be seen by September 30 and October 1. Now understand how water from other districts reached Lucknow… 1. Sitapur and Hardoi (distance: 80 to 130 km): Water from rainfall in these areas entered the Lucknow border, including Bakshi Ka Talab and Itaunja, the fastest, within 36 to 48 hours, or 1.5 to 2 days. 2. Shahjahanpur (distance: 180 to 220 km): It took 3 to 4 days for water from here to reach Lucknow. 3. Pilibhit (distance: 350+ km): It takes 5 to 6 days for water from the plains of Pilibhit and Fulhar Lake to flow through the Gomti's winding course and reach Lucknow. River water entered the city through drains At the Kudiya Ghat Pumping Station at Lucknow's Gomti Barrage, the Gomti's water level is maintained at around 105.7 metres. This water is treated and supplied as drinking water to the entire capital. At the same time, during the rainy season, the barrage controls sudden increases in water flow through 10 gates and helps protect the city from flooding. However, the Gomti's water level has remained around 108.14 metres. Under normal circumstances, water from the city flows into the river through drains. But when the river's water level rises above the drains, the system starts working in the opposite direction. As a result, river water is flowing back through the drains and entering residential areas. Prabhakar Prasad, Chief Engineer of the Sharda Canal Project, says, “Illegal construction and encroachment in the river's floodplain and wetlands have reduced the river's natural capacity to absorb water.” All 10 gates of the Gomti Barrage have been fully opened to drain the water. Meanwhile, 48 drains that discharge into the Gomti have been sealed to prevent the river water from flowing back. The floodwater is expected to recede within 4 to 5 days.

stories.title: Hospital submerged in Faizullaganj, Gomti reaches Ekana Stadium:India-West Indies match; roads flooded before 35,000 fans arrive
stories.summary: The situation has gone out of control in Lucknow due to flooding in the Gomti River. The 100-bed, four-storey hospital in Faizullaganj has been submerged. Helpless doctors are treating infected patients while sitting beside a drain. Schools in the area are closed. Frightened residents have sent their families to relatives' homes and are staying back to guard their houses. People can be seen using boats to carry whatever food supplies and belongings remain in their homes from one place to another. The water of the Gomti river has reached Ekana Stadium, around 21 km from here. India and the West Indies are scheduled to play a match here today, with 30 to 35 thousand people expected to attend. The Lucknow administration appeared alert a day before the match regarding the arrangements. Water accumulated on the service lane was being drained throughout the day. Read the flood report… 2 scenes around Ekana Stadium The first T20 match between India and the West Indies is scheduled to be played at Ekana Stadium today, Tuesday. The river water has reached up to around 100 metres from Gate No. 1 of the stadium. A boundary had been built just a few days ago some distance from the stadium. The water is now touching that boundary. However, the stadium is located at a higher elevation, so there is currently little possibility of the water reaching it. But anticipating the threat, preparations are now underway for permanent construction along the riverbank. Large boulders have therefore been placed near Gate No. 1. Shaheed Path runs directly in front of Ekana Stadium, with the Uttar Pradesh Police headquarters on the other side. The service road in front of the headquarters is currently flooded with up to 1 foot of water. There is an underpass here, which has up to 2 feet of water inside it. Police personnel are stopping bikes from passing through it. According to local residents, this is not Gomti river water. They say the water that flows into the Gomti river has been blocked, causing it to spread onto the roads. Boats on roads, thefts reported from submerged houses In the Daudnagar intersection area of Faizullaganj, water could be seen everywhere. There is 6 to 8 feet of water on the road, and people are able to travel only by boat. A 100-bed community health centre was started here in 2022. The first floor of this four-storey hospital is now submerged. The doctors posted here have been assigned duties at different locations. Some other staff associated with the hospital are now sitting over a drain a short distance from the hospital and providing medicines to people. Ajay said, ‘The flood came in 2008, there was a field here then…’ It was here that we met Ajay Gupta. He says, “The last time a flood came was in 2008. At that time, there were not so many houses here. There was a village and open land, so the flood was not this dangerous. The situation is completely different today. One-storey houses of people have now been submerged.” People are now being forced to leave their homes. Since no one is staying in the houses, thefts have also increased. “Yesterday, we caught a person doing something similar. But what could we do? So we later let him go.” Shantidevi cried, 'My husband is trapped on the roof amid the flood…' Amid the flood, we met 60-year-old Shanti Devi, who began crying. She said, “We somehow managed to save half of our belongings and took them out. Now my husband is trapped on the roof amid the flood. Somehow, please take us to him. My husband is ill and it is necessary for me to reach him.” We took Shanti to the administrative officials, from where she travelled by boat to reach her husband. Built a house in 2011, now forced to leave it Sanjeev, who is from Gaya district in Bihar, works in Lucknow. In 2011, he bought land in the Daudnagar area and then built a house. He says, “When I was building the house in 2011, people had told me about the 2008 flood. However, nothing like this had happened since. In 2018, water had reached the road, but it did not enter the house. This time, water has entered the house, and now we are being forced to leave.” Sanjeev’s wife and daughter have left with suitcases. His wife says, “A lot of our belongings have been submerged. Now everything is in God’s hands. Even when it was raining, we did not think this would happen, but the situation has now become extremely bad.” Women said, 'Officials are helping those whose homes have not been affected' Here, we met a group of women who were extremely unhappy with the administration’s arrangements. The women alleged that the administration was providing help to those who had not been affected. “We are affected by the flood, but no one is asking about us. Our entire house is filled with water. An electric motor installed on the roof has also been stolen.” “The officials who come here take boats to the hospital and then return. They do not even come to our village. These women said no relief camp has been set up anywhere. “Where should we go? What should we eat? There are no arrangements for us.” Civil Defence said, 'People do not want to leave their submerged homes' At the relief camp, Sunil Tiwari of Civil Defence told us, “All our wardens are helping people amid this crisis. Our people are on every boat because at several places people are forcibly stopping the boats. We want to ensure that this does not happen.” “The situation inside the area has deteriorated at present, and there is a lot of water at several places. Even in this situation, people are not ready to leave their homes because they fear that if the area is vacated, their belongings kept on the upper floors of their houses will be stolen.” Sunil says, “The situation has worsened because of rainwater that has entered the tributaries of the Gomti. It will take time for this water to drain. It is believed that the water level will start falling after 5 days. Looking at the current situation, it appears that relief may come only after the next 7-8 days.” 'There is no preparation by the administration, they are not even providing boats to deliver water' Amid the flood, several social workers have reached the area and are providing help on their own. One of them is Ravikant, who is delivering drinking water to people using his tractor. He says, “There is no preparation by the administration here. The arrangement of boats is very limited. We asked them for a boat so that we could take water inside, but we received no response. Now we are using a tractor to reach wherever we can provide help. This is our schedule for the entire day.”

stories.title: UP BJP in-charge seeks winning plan for lost seats:Vinod Tawde asks regional presidents to suggest solutions; co-in-charges to get areas soon
stories.summary: On Thursday, BJP national general secretary and Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde asked the regional presidents several questions in Lucknow. He asked how the seats that the BJP lost in the 2022 Assembly and 2024 Lok Sabha elections could be won in 2027. He sought reports on three points. Tawde instructed the regional presidents to begin election preparations with their teams. At a meeting held at the BJP state headquarters in the evening, the regional presidents, state general secretaries, regional in-charges and state presidents of the party's frontal organisations were introduced to the co-in-charges in the presence of state president Pankaj Chaudhary and organisational general secretary Dharampal Singh. Reasons for Lost Seats and Solutions Must Be Stated Tawde told the regional presidents that the report must include possible solutions along with the reasons for the defeats. Based on this report, the party will prepare its future electoral strategy for these seats. Tawde said that in the coming days, state co-in-charges Anant Odha, Medha Kulkarni, Pradeep Verma and Jagdish Ishwarbhai Patel would be assigned responsibility for the assembly constituencies. The co-in-charges will visit their respective areas and review the election preparations. He said that the state teams of the frontal organisations had been announced. The district presidents should also be announced soon. Those present at the meeting included state general secretaries Abhijat Mishra, Dilip Patel, Shankar Lodhi, Ram Pratap Singh and Geeta Shakya; Awadh regional president Awadhesh Dwivedi; OBC Morcha state president Prakash Pal; SC Morcha state president Ashok Rawat; ST Morcha state president Vidyabhushan Gond; and Mahila Morcha state president Saroj Kushwaha. These leaders staked their claim for Rajya Sabha tickets The BJP is deliberating on the names of candidates for the eight Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh. Of the eight MPs whose terms are ending, two are Brahmins, two are Thakurs, one is a Lodhi, one is a Shakya, one is a Sikh Punjabi and one is a Dalit. From the Brahmin community, BJP national general secretary Harish Dwivedi, former MP Ramapati Ram Tripathi, poet Kumar Vishwas, Varun Gandhi and Subrat Tripathi are contenders. From the Kshatriya community, former minister and state vice-president Suresh Rana, state vice-president Kameshwar Singh, Rajya Sabha MP Neeraj Shekhar and Arun Singh have staked their claims. Former MPs Anil Agrawal and Rajendra Agrawal from the Vaishya community are also in the race for a ticket. From the backward classes, former MP and son of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh, Rajbir Singh alias Raju Bhaiya, Durvijay Shakya, Rajya Sabha MP and state general secretary Geeta Shakya, national vice-president Rekha Verma, state general secretary Dileep Patel, Mamtesh Shakya, former MP Sanjeev Balyan and Satyapal Singh are contenders. According to information, the BJP's core committee will prepare a panel of candidates' names. Vinod Tawde will take the panel to Delhi. The party's national leadership will then discuss the names with state president Pankaj Chaudhary and organisation general secretary Dharmapal Singh. The Rajya Sabha candidates may be announced on 3 or 4 October. Understand the arithmetic: Who will get which Rajya Sabha seat Seats in the Rajya Sabha election are allocated based on the number of legislators. In other words, the party or alliance with more legislators can send more candidates to the Rajya Sabha. The formula for calculating the votes required to win one Rajya Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh is: total MLAs ÷ (vacant seats + 1) + 1 Uttar Pradesh currently has 397 MLAs and 10 vacant Rajya Sabha seats. Therefore: 397 ÷ 11 + 1 = 37.09
