stories.title: Wife cries holding Subedar husband’s feet:Caresses son’s body, daughter faints crying; 3 funeral processions held together in Deoria
stories.summary: The bodies of the Army subedar, his son, brother and nephew reached Deoria on Monday morning. As all four bodies arrived at their ancestral village, the family was overwhelmed with grief. The subedar's wife clung to her husband's feet and wept uncontrollably. His daughter fainted while crying. After regaining consciousness, she insisted on seeing her father's face and repeatedly ran towards him, but family members restrained and comforted her. The entire village turned out to pay tribute to the subedar. People raised slogans of ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ and ‘May they remain immortal’. When the biers of the subedar, his son and brother were carried out of the house together, the entire village was moved to tears. After a funeral procession covering about 2 km, the bodies reached Baikunth Dham on the banks of the Bathua river in Rudrapur. Meanwhile, the nephew's body was also brought to Baikunth Dham from another village. The last rites of all four will be performed here. The incident took place in Gahila Dudhaiala village, under the jurisdiction of Rudrapur Kotwali, around 22 km from the district headquarters. On Sunday, Gaurav Singh (18), the only son of Subedar Major Satyawan Singh, his brother Ram Samujh (55) and his relative nephew Rajan Singh (35) died in a tragic accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur while bringing back Subedar Major Satyawan Singh's body. See the heartbreaking pictures Understand the entire matter in sequence- Look at the pictures from the accident... Wife seeks ₹5 crore compensation for family Sarojni Devi, the wife of martyred Subedar Satyawan Singh, wrote to DM Madhusudan Hulgi and SP Abhijeet, urging the Chief Minister to provide financial assistance of ₹5 crore to each family. She also demanded the construction of a grand entrance gate in the village in her martyred husband's name and the allocation of a petrol pump in his name. In addition, she appealed for one government job for each family member.

stories.title: Sisters run tea stall to become IAS officers:DM speaks to them over phone, promises all possible help; invites them to his residence
stories.summary: DM Deepak Meena spoke by phone on Sunday with the sisters in Gorakhpur who sell tea to prepare for the IAS examination and buy medicines for their paralysed father. He asked about the family and enquired about their father's condition. He then called them to his residence at 10 a.m. on Monday. The DM assured the sisters that he would provide all possible help. The three sisters run the shop together throughout the day and prepare for the examination on YouTube until 2 a.m. A short while ago, Dainik Bhaskar prominently published the story of the sisters' determination. Following this, the administration has stepped forward to help them. The eldest sister, Vartika Upadhyay, said, We received a call from the DM's office at around 9 p.m. The person speaking said that the DM wanted to meet us. Father paralysed, household responsibilities fall on the sisters Vandita Upadhyay, a resident of Maharajganj, said, I live with my family in a rented house in Bargadwa. My father, Ramsakal Upadhyay, was previously a branch manager at Reliance Life and Insurance Company in Maharajganj. The family's financial condition was stable. In 2017, her father became paralysed. He subsequently lost his job. The family's financial condition began to deteriorate. Her mother, Madhuri, is a housewife. There was no other permanent source of income in the household. Taught tuition and worked jobs, but still could not make ends meet Vandita said that, along with her father's medicines and household expenses, she was also worried about the future of the three sisters. She started tutoring young children and also took up odd jobs. But this was not enough to cover the family's expenses. About four years ago, the three sisters planned to open a tea shop. They thought it would be easy to start a tea stall on a small budget. However, their mother refused. She said, Our relatives are well-off. What will they think if they see us doing this? They will make fun of us. Saved ₹8,000, then opened a tea stall After that, we dropped the idea of opening a tea shop. But the family's financial condition gradually began to deteriorate. The financial strain also affected the education of the elder brother. Twenty-six-year-old Shivam Upadhyay studied up to Class 12, after which he had to discontinue his education. He currently works from home as a telecaller for a company. Four months ago, the three of us sisters revisited our old idea and started a tea stall opposite the DDU gate with ₹8,000. We named our stall Believer Bistro. It felt somewhat strange in the early days because we used to study there. But gradually, everything returned to normal. People started coming, and they liked the taste of our tea. When we began making some profit from the sales, I added Maggi to the menu along with tea. Elder sister Vartika is preparing for the IAS examination. She wants to become a DM in the future. Vandita and Avantika are still in college. As they also run the tea stall throughout the day, they have less time to prepare. However, they do study from 12 midnight to 2 a.m. Vandita wants to join the police department after becoming an IPS officer, while Avantika wants to become an IAS officer. Mother says-daughters are my strength Mother Madhuri says that her daughters have been her strength even during difficult times. Earlier, I was afraid of what people would think and refused to set up a stall, but now I am happy that they are doing their work. Their dream will certainly come true. Father Ramsakal, meanwhile, says that he is proud of his daughters. The way they have managed the entire family without anyone's support over the past few years is no small achievement. I am happy that they are doing for themselves what I could not do for them. They did not lose courage. ₹3 lakh to ₹4 lakh has been spent on treatment Vandita said that at least ₹3 lakh to ₹4 lakh has been spent on her father's treatment so far. More expenses continue to accrue. His medicines cost ₹5,000 to ₹6,000 a month. He was also taken to Nepal for treatment. During this period, all their savings were exhausted. There are a few decimals of farmland in the village, which are looked after by people living nearby.

stories.title: Kanpur govt doctor dies by suicide:Married 3 years ago; shoots himself with licensed revolver at 2 am
stories.summary: A government doctor in Kanpur allegedly died by suicide after shooting himself in the chest with his licensed revolver. His wife rushed into the room after hearing the gunshot and found him lying on the floor in a pool of blood. Family members took Dr Sandeep Singh (47) to Regency Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place around 2am on Sunday at Blossom Apartment in Nirala Nagar. Singh was a surgeon posted at a community health centre in Kanpur Dehat. Singh's father Raj Bahadur said his daughter-in-law Kanchan called him during the night and told him that Sandeep had shot himself and that she was taking him to hospital. DCP Dipendra Nath Chaudhary said the forensic team has seized the revolver. Dr Sandeep lived separately from parents Singh was a resident of Paradevanpurwa in Lal Bangla. His father Raj Bahadur Singh is a retired Army subedar. Sandeep had three brothers — Vishal, Vikram and Rahul. Vishal died after an illness, while Rahul died in a hit-and-run case in Noida. Raj Bahadur lives in Paradevanpurwa with his wife and younger son Vikram. Sandeep lived separately with his wife Kanchan, daughter and two-month-old son at Blossom Apartment in Nirala Nagar. Second marriage took place in 2019 His cousin Mohit said Sandeep's first marriage was in 2007 to Keerti Singh, an MBBS doctor from Kanpur. They had a 12-year-old son and divorced by mutual consent in 2018. Sandeep married Kanchan Singh, a resident of Kasganj, in 2019. Kanchan is a homemaker and they have two children — four-year-old Mahi and a two-month-old son. Raj Bahadur said disputes had started between Sandeep and Kanchan over minor issues soon after their marriage. He would often intervene and try to settle their differences. He said he last spoke to Sandeep around 9.30 pm on Sunday and asked about his well-being. According to the family, Sandeep later had an argument with his wife. Around 2am, he took out his licensed revolver, went to the prayer room, touched Laddu Gopal's feet and then sat before the temple and shot himself in the chest. Completed MS from GSVM Medical College in 2010 His cousin Rishabh Singh said Sandeep completed his MBBS from Jolly Grant Medical College in Dehradun in 2006 and MS from GSVM Medical College in Kanpur in 2010. He then joined Hallet Hospital and worked there for around nine years before being transferred to Kannauj. After working there for six years, he was posted at a CHC in Kanpur Dehat. He had been working there as a general surgeon for the past one-and-a-half years. Kidwai Nagar SHO Neeraj Dwivedi said, The case appeared to be one of suicide by shooting himself in the chest. He said a family dispute had emerged as a possible reason in the preliminary inquiry. The body has been sent for post-mortem, and the exact reason will be clear only after questioning.

stories.title: Severe floods hit Lucknow, water enters 40,000 homes:3 lakh people affected, forced to leave homes; expected to worsen further
stories.summary: The flood situation is worsening in Uttar Pradesh. Ten rivers are in spate after water was released from dams following heavy rainfall in the hills. Despite no rain for the past eight days, 11 districts, including Lucknow and Sitapur, remain affected by floods. In Lucknow, the water level of the Gomti river has been rising rapidly for the seventh consecutive day. Around 40,000 houses in the Faizullaganj area are submerged under 4-5 feet of water, affecting nearly 3 lakh people. Thousands have been forced to leave their homes, while boats are operating on the streets. Amid the floodwaters, a house wall suddenly collapsed. Hanumant Dham, the Lete Hue Hanuman Temple and Chandrika Devi Temple along the Gomti Riverfront have also been submerged. Dozens of villages in Ballia and Gonda have been cut off and turned into islands.

stories.title: Umesh Pal murder case:Atiq’s shooter Armaan brought to Prayagraj; to be produced in court today; was in Bihar jail for 3 years
stories.summary: Police brought Armaan, an accused in the murder of Prayagraj lawyer Umesh Pal, to Prayagraj on Monday morning. Armaan was a shooter for mafia don Atiq Ahmed. Armaan, who carried a bounty of ₹5 lakh, had been lodged in Bihar's Gayaji jail for three years, while the Uttar Pradesh Police had been searching for him across the state. Armaan was brought to Prayagraj on transit remand. The police have currently kept him at a secure location. Shortly, the Dhoomanganj police will produce Armaan before the ADJ SC-ST Court. The trial in the murder case of lawyer Umesh Pal and his two government gunmen is underway in the same court. Security has been tightened on the court premises ahead of the hearing. The police may also file an application seeking Armaan's custody. If custody is granted, the police will question him about the Umesh Pal murder case. Family fears an encounter Since the Umesh Pal murder case, Atiq Ahmed's wife, Shaista Parveen, and Ashraf's wife, Zainab Fatima, have been absconding. During Armaan's interrogation, the police will try to find out whether he has been in contact with them, identify their possible hideouts and gather any other information about them. After learning that Armaan was being brought to Uttar Pradesh, his father, Shamim, and mother, Asgari Khatoon, have been fearing a police encounter. Armaan's father had filed a petition in the Gaya court, demanding that Armaan not be handed over to the Uttar Pradesh Police. He had said that if the police wanted to question him, it should be done through video conferencing. Most of the accused in the Umesh Pal murder case have already been killed in police encounters. Armaan, too, could be killed in an encounter in the name of recovering a weapon. Mother had said - he was being made a scapegoat His mother, Asgari Khatun, had said that her son was being made a scapegoat. Our family is very poor. We do not even have a permanent house of our own to live in. She said that Armaan had earlier lived in Prayagraj and done odd jobs. He is neither a professional criminal nor a big-time shooter. He has been in jail for the past three years. Armaan's younger brother Imran had said that they had previously expressed apprehension that his brother's life was in danger. The Uttar Pradesh Police have now taken him to Prayagraj. The family fears that something untoward may happen to Armaan as well. The family will accept whatever the court decides. However, Armaan must not be harmed in any way. Armaan's lawyer says - collusion between prison authorities and police A hearing on the application filed by Armaan's parents was held on 1 October in the court of Gaya magistrate Saurabh Kumar. The court rejected the application filed by Armaan's family and lawyer. Armaan's lawyer, Lalit Kumar Gupta, confirmed this. The lawyer accused the police and jail administration. He said, "Armaan's life is in danger. He could be killed in Uttar Pradesh. A conspiracy is being hatched to kill Mohammad Armaan in collusion with the Uttar Pradesh Police and the Gaya Ji Central Jail administration." "We had sought Armaan's appearance through video conference, citing security reasons, but the court rejected it. Armaan has been lodged in Gaya jail since 27 February 2023. He is being deliberately framed in the Uttar Pradesh case." Find out how the Uttar Pradesh Police reached Gaya Ji jail Uttar Pradesh Police had been searching for Armaan for the past three years. During this time, they learnt that he was lodged in Gayaji Central Jail. After receiving the information, police from Prayagraj's Dhoomanganj police station reached Gayaji Jail on 30 September. There, they took Armaan's latest photograph and obtained his thumb impressions on plain paper. After completing the paperwork, the police returned to Prayagraj. They then filed an application for transit remand in the Gaya court on 1 October. Armaan was seen firing alongside Guddu Muslim Umesh Pal and his two government gunners were shot dead in broad daylight in Prayagraj on 24 February 2023. CCTV footage of the incident also emerged. A man on a motorcycle was seen in the footage. According to the police, Armaan was riding the motorcycle, while Guddu Muslim was seated behind him. Armaan had brought Guddu Muslim to the crime scene on the motorcycle. As soon as the motorcycle stopped, Guddu Muslim opened fire. Armaan also fired shots. After the crime, the two fled the scene on the motorcycle.

stories.summary: Police have arrested one accused in connection with the attack on a former district president during the Samajwadi Party's press conference at the Gorakhpur Press Club. Meanwhile, police are conducting raids in search of the expelled SP leader and his sons. Four police teams have been deployed to make the arrests. The arrested accused was identified as Ankit Kumar Gaur, a resident of Bichhiya Azad Nagar in Shahpur. Former Samajwadi Party district president Nageena Prasad Sahani filed a complaint following the assault at the Press Club on 3 October. He alleged that Samajwadi Party leaders Anshuman Singh, Kamlesh Singh and Vimlesh Singh, their associates Ankit Kumar Gaur and Shubham Rai, along with 10 other unidentified people, abused him and attacked him with the intention of killing him during the gathering. Kamlesh Singh and Vimlesh Singh fired firearms, but the shots missed. This saved his life. Based on the allegations, the police registered a case under serious sections. Report sent to DM for cancellation of arms licence The police have formed four teams and are conducting raids to arrest Anshuman Singh, his sons and the other accused. The police have also sent a report to the district magistrate seeking cancellation of Anshuman Singh's arms licence. They are also gathering information about the arms licences of the other accused. Dispute over a chair The Samajwadi Party's former district president has alleged that a dispute broke out over sitting on a chair during the press conference. When the argument escalated, Anshuman's son, Kamlesh Singh, slapped Ramnagina Prasad Sahni. The complaint also alleges that firearms were brandished and shots were fired. The police are investigating these allegations. A video of the incident had also begun to go viral on social media. Lawyers had also come out in support in the matter. Identifying Ramnagina as an advocate, the lawyers had demanded that a case be registered. Press club president lodges case Gorakhpur Journalists Press Club president Onkar Dhar Dwivedi has also lodged an FIR against 12 Samajwadi Party leaders. In a written complaint submitted to the Cantt station house officer, he said that a press conference by SP district president Brijesh Kumar Gautam had been scheduled at 2 p.m. on 3 October in the press club auditorium. It is alleged that during the press conference, district president Brijesh Kumar Gautam, former district president Nageena Prasad Sahani, Awadhesh Yadav, Prahlad Yadav, Mohsin Khan, Kajal Nishad, Sanjay Pehalwan, Shabbir Qureshi, Sanjay Nishad, Anshuman Singh, Kamlesh Singh, Vijay Bahadur Yadav and others entered the auditorium carrying weapons. During the press conference, they began assaulting one another over an issue. The journalists covering the event became uncomfortable and somehow moved aside to save themselves. City SP Nimish Patil said in this regard Both cases are being investigated. Four teams have been deployed to arrest the accused. The police are also examining videos and other evidence related to the incident.

Bulldozers to roll from October 11:Illegal lawyer chambers to be demolished; encroachments around Lucknow Collectorate
stories.summary: Bulldozers will be deployed against encroachments around government offices, courts, hospitals and bus stands in Lucknow from 11 October. Zone 1 of the Municipal Corporation has given encroachers a final opportunity to remove the structures themselves by 10 October. If the encroachments are not removed by the deadline, a joint team of the district administration, police and Municipal Corporation will carry out demolition action. The action is being taken under an order issued by the Allahabad High Court on 10 September. The court had directed that roads and footpaths be cleared of encroachments in view of the difficulties being faced by the public while commuting. The Municipal Corporation had earlier given encroachers until 3 October to remove the structures. They have now been given a final extension until 10 October. Areas where action will be taken The campaign covers the District and Sessions Court complex, the old High Court campus, the Collectorate, the Board of Revenue, the old Sadar Tehsil campus, the Sub-Registrar's Office, the Police Commissionerate office, the Residency power substation, Balarampur Hospital, Kaiserbagh bus station, the Transport Department's Tehri Kothi workshop and the area near the BSNL office. You will be responsible if you do not remove your belongings The Zonal Officer of Municipal Corporation Zone 1 has warned that if any belongings or structures are damaged during the removal of encroachments from 11 October, the concerned person will be responsible. The administration will not provide any compensation for this. Additional Municipal Commissioner Pankaj Srivastava said action to remove the encroachments was being taken following an order of the High Court.

stories.title: Arrest warrant issued for codeine syrup accused Shubham’s wife:Vaishali named accused after liquor contract, property probe; court directs police action
stories.summary: Interpol is searching for absconding codeine cough syrup mafia operator Shubham Jaiswal. Meanwhile, the court has issued an arrest warrant against his wife, Vishal Jaiswal alias Vaishali Poswani. The warrant was issued after Vaishali's name surfaced in connection with Shubham Jaiswal's properties and liquor shops. The court has directed the Kotwali police to arrest Vaishali, wife of Prahladghat resident Shubham Jaiswal, and produce her before the court. Sigra property and liquor shop in wife's name Amid the ongoing cross-examination in the case linked to mafia figure Shubham Jaiswal, the police investigation has revealed that Shubham used money earned from codeine cough syrup to acquire several properties. He also opened liquor shops, which are in his wife's name. The police had therefore filed an application in court seeking an arrest warrant against Vaishali. The court has issued this direction. Vaishali Jaiswal is absconding Kotwali Station House Officer Dayashankar Singh said that Vaishali had been absconding since after Shubham Jaiswal. Raids are being conducted to arrest the accused who are absconding in the case. The court has issued a warrant against Vaishali, following which the search for her has been intensified. Besides her house in Jagatganj, her neighbours and relatives are also being questioned, and raids are being conducted at possible hideouts. Interpol searching for absconding Shubham Codeine cough syrup mafia figure Shubham Jaiswal, a resident of Kayastha Tola Prahlad Ghat in Varanasi, is now being traced with Interpol's assistance. No one has had any information about his location since November 2025. Varanasi Police have declared him a fugitive and also issued a Red Corner Notice against him. A reward of ₹50,000 has been announced for information leading to his arrest. After the Varanasi and Sonbhadra police, the SIT (Special Investigation Team) will now initiate action to seize the accused's properties in the case.

Akhilesh may deny tickets to Muslim leaders:Owaisi to field them; no alliance, plans candidates for 200 seats
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi had given the SP-Congress alliance time until October 2 to reach an agreement. The deadline has now expired. The party is preparing to contest the election on its own. Owaisi is preparing to field candidates on at least 200 Assembly seats. Of these, 100 will be Muslim-dominated seats, where the party wants to field strong candidates with a high chance of winning. Owaisi is particularly eyeing Muslim leaders who want to contest the election but are being denied tickets by Akhilesh Yadav. Owaisi is preparing to field such leaders on AIMIM tickets. The question is whether Owaisi still hopes for an alliance with the SP-Congress or whether, like in 2022, he will move ahead with smaller and regional parties. Read the full report… AIMIM claims, ‘SP leaders are in touch…’ AIMIM is entering the fray with a changed strategy this time. The party is looking at leaders who have worked on the ground in their constituencies for a long time but are now facing the possibility of being denied tickets by the SP or other opposition parties at the last minute. The figures from previous elections also indicate that the SP may give fewer tickets to Muslim candidates this time. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the SP fielded 64 Muslim candidates, around 15.88% of its candidates. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, however, it gave tickets to only four Muslim candidates, accounting for just 5% of the total seats. AIMIM expects the SP to field fewer Muslim candidates in the 2027 election as well, as it did in the Lok Sabha election. If tickets are denied to prominent and influential Muslim leaders, AIMIM will bring them into its fold and field them. For this, party workers are conducting ground-level surveys and reaching out to potential candidates. These leaders claim that several SP leaders are in touch with AIMIM. Owaisi’s rallies planned from Purvanchal to western UP AIMIM has planned Owaisi’s Uttar Pradesh tour from Purvanchal to western UP, with a particular focus on Muslim-dominated districts. Asaduddin Owaisi held a public meeting on October 4 at Rajapur Rani in the Bhinga Assembly constituency of Shravasti in Purvanchal. On October 11, he will hold a public meeting in Azamgarh, an important district in eastern UP in terms of its Muslim population. The SP holds all 10 Assembly seats here. Owaisi will visit Rampur on October 18. Rampur has also been an SP stronghold, although the party’s position has weakened here since Azam Khan was jailed. On October 25, Owaisi will address a major public meeting in the Kairana area of Shamli district. Kairana is the Lok Sabha constituency of SP MP Iqra Hasan. He will then hold a major public meeting in Meerut on November 7. Before this, Owaisi has also held public meetings in Matera in Bahraich, Najibabad in Bijnor, Moradabad Rural, Saharanpur and Kanpur. Where did AIMIM hurt the SP in 2022? Of Uttar Pradesh’s 403 Assembly seats, Muslim voters play a major role in the electoral outcome on 120 to 143 seats. In around 73 seats in western UP, the Muslim population is above 30%. These include Rampur, Moradabad, Sambhal, Saharanpur, Bijnor, Amroha and Muzaffarnagar. On around 70 seats, Muslims account for between 20% and 30% of the population. In 2022, AIMIM fielded candidates on around 97 seats. Although it did not win a single seat and its vote share was just 0.49%, it cut into votes by 2,000 to 8,000 in the seats it targeted. On these seats, the victory margin was smaller than the number of votes AIMIM received. Alliance with smaller parties possible With the possibility of an alliance with the SP-Congress appearing to have ended, Owaisi may form an alliance with smaller parties. These could include the Azad Samaj Party, Peace Party and Rashtriya Ulama Council. To send a message to Muslims, Owaisi has already said that if they want to stop the BJP, they should come together with respect; otherwise, AIMIM will fight its own battle.

stories.title: Bihar’s JDU, LJP seek seats in UP:If no NDA deal, who will they hurt by contesting alone?
stories.summary: Two key BJP allies in Bihar, the Janata Dal United (JDU) and Lok Janshakti Party-Ram Vilas (LJP-R), are preparing to enter the electoral fray in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, with both parties stepping up their organisational preparations. While LJP national president Chirag Paswan is reaching out to the state’s youth through programmes such as ‘Youth Bole Toh’ in Prayagraj, Nishant Kumar, son of former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, has visited Varanasi for two days to gauge the political mood, with the party also organising a major gathering there on October 25. The question is, how many seats do the NDA allies JDU and LJP-R want to contest in Uttar Pradesh? Is an alliance with the BJP possible for both parties? If the two parties contest the elections separately, which party will be affected? Read the full report... In Bihar, Janata Dal United and Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) are counted among the BJP’s two strong allies. The two parties have 85 and 19 MLAs, respectively, in the Bihar Assembly. In the Lok Sabha, the two parties have 17 MPs, including 12 from JDU and five from LJP (Ram Vilas). This gives an indication of the importance of both parties to the BJP in Bihar. Now, both parties are looking towards the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections as part of their expansion plans. JDU wants seats in Uttar Pradesh in return for allowing the BJP to have its Chief Minister in Bihar. Chirag Paswan, meanwhile, also wants to expand his party and is trying to give it an all-India identity. What is JDU’s plan for Uttar Pradesh? Keeping the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in mind, JDU has appointed Bihar government minister Shravan Kumar as the state in-charge. The party’s Uttar Pradesh president, Anup Singh Patel, says the party is preparing to contest 60 seats under the leadership of the state in-charge. These seats are spread across eastern, central and western Uttar Pradesh. This means the party does not want to focus only on eastern Uttar Pradesh, which borders Bihar. The seriousness with which the party is preparing to contest the elections can be gauged from the fact that Nishant Kumar, son of former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, himself stayed in Varanasi for two days. He offered prayers at the Baba Vishwanath temple and also attended the Ganga Aarti. Speaking to the media at the Circuit House in Varanasi, Nishant Kumar said, “It is my good fortune that I have come to the sacred land of Varanasi. Guruvadi Baba is the deity of our family, so I sought his blessings.” JDU has called a meeting of its state executive in Varanasi on October 25. The state executive will also be reconstituted during the meeting. The party will present its blueprint for Uttar Pradesh before its office-bearers at the meeting. It will also make its position clear on seat-sharing and an alliance. How strong is JDU’s claim in Uttar Pradesh? JDU is focusing on districts such as Varanasi, Mirzapur, Jaunpur, Ghazipur and Deoria in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Kurmi, Patel and other OBC voters are considered to have a significant presence in these areas. In Bihar, Nitish Kumar’s main support base has been among the Kurmi and extremely backward classes. Therefore, JDU hopes that contesting the election along with the BJP and Apna Dal (S) can prevent the OBC vote from getting divided. Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal says, “The real strength of any alliance is its support base. The extent of JDU’s support base in Uttar Pradesh can be gauged from the results of the last two Assembly elections. JDU contested the elections alone in 2017 and 2022. In 2022, the party fielded candidates on 27 seats but could not save its deposit on any seat. The party received a total of 0.05% of the votes.” LJP has also announced plans to contest UP elections The Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), the BJP’s second major ally in Bihar, has also announced that it will contest the Uttar Pradesh elections. On July 6, LJP (R) held a meeting of its national executive at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow. Chirag Paswan himself attended the meeting. At the time, he said that his party would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. He reiterated this on September 27 during the ‘Youth Bole Toh’ programme in Prayagraj. After returning to Delhi from Prayagraj, Chirag Paswan also said, “The kind of support we received from the youth of Uttar Pradesh in Prayagraj strengthens my belief in the thinking with which my party is planning to contest the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.” How many seats is LJP preparing to contest? During the Lucknow programme, LJP had claimed that it was preparing to contest all 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. Arun Bharti, who has been appointed the party’s in-charge for the Uttar Pradesh elections, says that the party is fully prepared. “We have already held two major events in Uttar Pradesh. Chirag Paswan himself attended both events. We are part of the NDA. If we receive a respectable offer of seats from the BJP, LJP will consider it." He added, “Our alliance with the NDA is in Bihar. In elections in other states outside Bihar, every party has the right to expand its support base. LJP is also doing the same. A large number of voters from our community are also in Uttar Pradesh. We will move forward by taking the Paswan community and other sections of society along with us.” Can BJP form an alliance with JDU and LJP in Uttar Pradesh? Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh answers this in the negative. He says, “There are already four regional parties in the NDA alliance in Uttar Pradesh. Among the four parties, RLD has a presence among Jat voters, Apna Dal (S) among Kurmi-Kushwaha voters, SBSP among the Rajbhar community and Nishad Party among the Nishad community." He added, "This time, the BJP has to resolve the seat-sharing equation with all four of its allies. In such a situation, it will not increase its problems by bringing two more parties into the alliance.” JDU’s core vote base in Bihar is among Kurmi-Kushwaha voters. Apna Dal (S) follows the politics of the same core vote base in Uttar Pradesh. LJP’s core vote base in Bihar is among the Paswan community. In Uttar Pradesh, this community has traditionally been with the BJP. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, however, this community did show a shift towards the Samajwadi Party. LJP could potentially make up for this. If both parties contest separately, who will be affected? In every election, a large number of smaller parties with influence in different districts and among different castes enter the electoral fray. Although they may not win many seats, even 1,000-2,000 votes can change the result on several seats. Political analyst Prof. Sanjay Kumar says, “Many times, larger parties also use smaller parties for their own benefit. Big parties ask smaller parties to field candidates who can divide the voters in order to defeat their opponents. Smaller parties cut into the valuable votes of the main candidate and change the equation of victory and defeat.” JDU and LJP are both BJP allies in Bihar. In Uttar Pradesh too, they would want to move forward by consolidating their core voters. Therefore, if contesting separately causes even a slight loss, the BJP would be affected. However, the performance of both parties in the last two elections in Uttar Pradesh was not very strong. When were they together in Uttar Pradesh? Before merging with JDU in 2003, the Samata Party contested elections in Uttar Pradesh as part of the NDA alliance. In 1996, the Samata Party won two seats and managed to win one of them. In 1998, the Samata Party won both seats allotted to it. In 2003, the Samata Party merged with JDU. However, the Samata Party never contested the Assembly elections.

stories.title: ‘DM uncle, I can’t talk to Papa, please install tower':5-year-old folds hands in Sonbhadra; walks 1km to make calls
stories.summary: A video of a girl appealing to Sonbhadra DM Charchit Gaud to provide mobile network in her village surfaced at 4 p.m. on Friday. In the video, the girl is seen folding her hands and requesting the DM to make mobile network available in the village. The girl says that her father lives away from home. There is no mobile network in the village, so she is unable to speak to her father properly over the phone. After the video surfaced, officials said the mobile network would be upgraded from 2G to 4G. The matter concerns the Nagwan development block. Now read the full story... The girl seen in the video is named Aanvi Patel. She is a UKG student at Hello Kids School in Robertsganj. Aanvi's entire family lives in Robertsganj. Her father, Vikas Patel, is a teacher at a school in Robertsganj. Her mother, Renu Priya Patel, is a homemaker. During the holidays, the family travels from Robertsganj to their ancestral village, Saraigarh, 60 km away. Aanvi is currently in the village with her family. Because there is no mobile network there, she has difficulty speaking to her father. In view of this problem, Aanvi's family members made the video. In the video, Aanvi is seen folding her hands and appealing to District Magistrate Charchit Gaur to have a mobile network installed in the village. The girl says, "Uncle DM, please arrange for a mobile network in my village, Saraigarh. My father lives away from us, and we are unable to call him. Please, Uncle DM!" 2G network available, preparations now under way for 4G BSNL SDO Dharmendra Kumar Singh said, "On the DM's instructions, a survey has been conducted in Saraigarh village. A 2G network is currently available in the village. Preparations are now under way to upgrade the network to 4G. A letter has been sent to senior officials for this. Work on the project is expected to begin soon." District Magistrate Charchit Gaur said, "A survey is being conducted in Saraigarh village. There is a network problem in rural areas. The problem will be resolved soon."

stories.title: Aradhana Misra becomes UP Congress chief:Ajay Rai removed; Imran Masood made working president, Devendra Nishad and Alok Prasad vice-presidents
stories.summary: Congress leadership has removed Ajay Rai as Uttar Pradesh Congress president and appointed Aradhana Misra, MLA from Pratapgarh’s Rampur Khas seat and leader of the Congress Legislature Party, as the new state unit chief. Saharanpur Congress MP Imran Masood has been appointed working president of the Uttar Pradesh Congress. Aradhana Misra ‘Mona’ is a three-time MLA from Rampur Khas and the leader of the Congress Legislature Party. She is the daughter of senior Congress leader Pramod Tiwari. Active in politics for more than two decades, she has also worked with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra during the Congress’ ‘Ladki Hoon, Lad Sakti Hoon’ campaign. The party has appointed Devendra Nishad and Alok Prasad as state vice-presidents. Around three months before the Assembly elections, the Congress has made a major organisational change in its Uttar Pradesh unit. The party has sought to focus on Brahmins, minorities (Muslims), OBCs and Dalits ahead of the Assembly polls. Imran Masood is an aggressive leader, known for outspoken views Imran Masood has a strong hold among Muslim and OBC voters in Saharanpur and adjoining areas. He is known for his sharp and outspoken statements. Despite becoming an MP in 2024 with the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance, Masood has openly spoken about differences within the alliance. He publicly claimed that the Samajwadi Party won 37 seats in 2024 only because of its alliance with the Congress. Masood wants the Congress to finalise an alliance with the Samajwadi Party soon for the 2027 elections. During the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, a controversial remark he made about Narendra Modi made headlines across the country. He was also jailed over the remark. At an election rally, Masood had said that if Narendra Modi tried to turn Uttar Pradesh into Gujarat, his “boti-boti” would be cut into pieces.

stories.title: Teacher says ‘Don’t touch me, I’ll kill you’:School manager misbehaves; arrested in Kushinagar; victim asks, ‘What would you do if this happened to your daughter?’
stories.summary: A school manager in Kushinagar sexually harassed a female teacher and threatened to kill her when she objected. A 5-minute 47-second video linked to the incident has surfaced. In it, the manager can be seen making inappropriate advances towards the teacher and making obscene remarks. In the video, the teacher can be heard warning the manager, "Stay away. Don't touch me. I will kill you." She also says that anyone would understand how it would feel if the same thing happened to their daughter. The incident is said to have taken place on Thursday, 1 October. The manager allegedly called the teacher to his office after school hours on the pretext of preparing her transfer certificate (TC). He then allegedly harassed her. The victim lodged a complaint with the police on Thursday night. The police arrested the accused at around 1 p.m. on Friday. He was sent to jail after being produced in court at 5 p.m. This case concerns The Rainbow Loreto School in Kushinagar. The school, located at Saraswati Chowk in the Ravindranagar police station area, provides education up to class eight. The accused school manager, Dinesh Rai, is a resident of Motichhapar village (Bhiswa) in Ravindra Nagar, Kushinagar. His wife is ill. He has a daughter and a son in the family. Manager said, "My wife is ill; I want to have sexual relations with you" The manager asked the female teacher to have sexual relations with him. During the conversation, he cited his wife's ill health and said, "My wife is ill... so I want to have sexual relations with you." The female teacher objected to what the manager was saying. She questioned how he could speak to her in that manner. In the video, the female teacher can be seen repeatedly telling him to stay away. The manager also appears to be trying to move closer to the woman and touch her. It is being reported that the female teacher recorded the conversation on her mobile phone. Now read the conversation between the school manager and the female teacher Female teacher: Sir, whatever you are doing is wrong. You are taking wrongful advantage of this. You are doing something very wrong. School manager: Wrong? Female teacher: Your mind has become polluted. You are a very dirty-minded man. Don't you have a wife? School manager: She is ill. Female teacher: Then get married again. Would you do things like this? I am also someone's daughter and sister. You cannot do this. How old is your daughter? School manager: She is 18 years old. Female Teacher: What would you do if someone did this to your daughter? Answer me. School Manager: I sit down after eating, which is why I have developed a protruding stomach. Female Teacher: Of course it will, when you do not do any work. Look, sir, it is absolutely not the way you think it is. School Manager: Are you mad? Female Teacher: If you want it that badly, get married again. Tell your wife that we are going to get married again. If you need it so badly, go somewhere else, but do not do this at school. School Manager: I will be disgraced there. Female Teacher: So you will not be disgraced at school? Do you do this with every female member of staff who comes here? Your intentions are not right. After this, the female teacher asks why she was called after school hours. She tells the manager to speak clearly instead of making gestures. Female teacher: Sir, you cannot touch me at all. Absolutely not. School manager: Wait for a while, we only want what is best for you. Female teacher: If I were another girl, I would beat you badly at this moment. Stay away from me. According to the video, the female teacher begins to leave the place. During this, she tells the manager to move away from her and leaves while protesting. Police register case under serious sections According to the police, a case has been registered against the accused, Dinesh Rai, under Sections 75, 115(2) and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). These sections relate to sexual harassment, voluntarily causing hurt and criminal intimidation. Find out what punishment may be imposed- BNS Section 75 (sexual harassment): Depending on the sub-section involved, the punishment may be imprisonment for one to three years and/or a fine. BNS Section 115(2): Imprisonment for up to one year, or a fine of up to ₹10,000, or both. BNS Section 351(3): Threatening someone with serious harm, such as death or grievous injury, is punishable by up to 7 years in prison, a fine, or both.

stories.title: Bodies thrown from moving car after murder in Lucknow:Lured on pretext of showing property; held hostage, ₹50 lakh demanded
stories.summary: The KGMU nursing officer and his friend, who had been missing in Lucknow for five days, had been murdered. The killers called them on the pretext of showing them a property. They then held them hostage and demanded a ransom of ₹50 lakh. When the money was not paid, they killed both men. They then threw the bodies from a moving Thar into the Ghaghra river. The police solved the case on Friday evening, relating to the incident on 28 September. The five accused involved in the murders had held the two friends hostage in separate rooms. To avoid suspicion, they parked Pawan's car in Sitapur. Pawan Kumar Garg was an Assistant Nursing Superintendent. He had gone to view a property with his friend Sachin. The killers strangled Pawan and Sachin with a rope The accused strangled Pawan and Sachin with a rope. To destroy the evidence, they threw the bodies into the Ghaghara river from Chalhari Ghat near Mahmoodabad. Madiyaon police and the Crime Branch (North Zone) have arrested all five accused. The accused have been identified as Nitin Mishra alias W (38), a sweet-shop owner from Lodhauli, Itaunja; auto-rickshaw driver Prakash Singh alias Pुद्दी (24); tea-shop owner Suraj Singh (32); commission-agent's accountant Mohit Singh (26); and Avneesh Kumar Maurya (38) of Ajit Puliya, Mall Road, Itaunja. Police recovered the deceased's gold chains and ring, driving licence (DL), Aadhaar card and photocopies of bank statements from the accused. They also seized the Thar and Hyundai cars used to dispose of the bodies. Land purchase plan turned deadly DCP North Amit Kumar Anand said that during police questioning, the main accused, Nitin Mishra alias W Mahraj, said he already knew Pawan Kumar Garg. Pawan had told him that he had ₹50-60 lakh set aside to buy land. He had asked him to show him a good property. After learning that a large sum of money was involved, Nitin conspired with his associates to carry out a kidnapping and extort ransom. On the night of 27 September, Nitin called Pawan to Bhithouli Crossing. Pawan arrived with his friend Sachin Vishwakarma. The accused took both of them to New Fauji Dhaba in Itaunja, where an argument broke out while they were drinking. Held hostage in a house under construction The accused took both men to Nitin's house under construction in Annamau, held them hostage in separate rooms and demanded a ransom of ₹50 lakh. To mislead the police, Nitin took Pawan's Brezza car from the dhaba and left it parked in Sitapur. Around noon on 28 September, after Pawan refused to pay the money, the accused began fearing that they would be caught. At around 12 noon, the accused strangled Pawan and Sachin with a rope and killed them. At around 5:30 p.m. on 28 September, the accused loaded both bodies into a Thar vehicle, took them to Chalhari Ghat and threw them into the Ghaghra river from the bridge. Missing person report filed on 29 September On 29 September, Pawan's nephew Sanjay Garg, a resident of Keshav Nagar, Madiyaon, reported his uncle missing at the Madiyaon police station. The police then began examining CCTV footage and toll plaza records. On 2 October, a case was registered under Section 140(2) of the BNS on the complaint filed by Pawan's brother, Manoj Kumar, and all five accused were arrested based on information provided by an informant near Bhithouli Tiraha. Pawan had recently sold a plot According to members associated with the KGMU Nursing Association, Pawan Garg had been posted as an assistant nursing superintendent at KGMU since 2011. He was currently posted in the orthopaedics department. He spent most of his time in the operation theatre. He left home on the night of 27 September. A few days earlier, he had sold a plot in the Kalli Paschimi area. Subsequently, reports emerged of a transaction with someone regarding the investment of the proceeds. However, this has not been confirmed. He left home at around 8 p.m. on Sunday, initially saying that he was going to Dubagga. It was learnt that he then travelled towards Madiaon in an Innova car. A property dealer friend was with him. When the friend's brother called to ask about his location, he said that he had reached Prerna Sthal. Subsequently, information emerged that Pawan's location had been detected near the Itaunja crossing at around 11 p.m. The police found his car in CCTV footage from the Itaunja toll plaza, and it was later recovered abandoned in Sitapur. The police are investigating the case from several angles. Had been embroiled in a dispute with his wife for several years Pawan Garg had been embroiled in a dispute with his wife for around 10 years. The two had been living separately. Their son lived with his wife. Around three years ago, the couple began living together following a court order. His wife stayed with him for around a year. During this period, they had another son. After two or three months, a dispute broke out between them again. After that, around two years ago, his wife's family took her with them to Rajasthan. Had also been involved in minor disputes According to people associated with the Nursing Association, complaints about Pawan Garg would also come in from time to time in the department. He was somewhat short-tempered and would often speak his mind openly in the heat of the moment. However, he was sociable and helped others when needed. His relations were also normal at the Nursing Association level. He would regularly have disputes over certain matters while working in the department. Family was originally from Rajasthan Pawan Garg's father previously owned a gold and silver shop in Rajasthan. Later, the family shifted to Uttar Pradesh. Pawan Garg joined KGMU in February 2011. He had been living in Lucknow ever since. His wife is said to be originally from Karauli in Rajasthan. Karauli is also said to be Pawan's native place.

stories.title: Anupriya Patel stays silent on Divya Mittal’s questions:Reviews organisation in Lucknow; says NDA will score hat-trick in 2027
stories.summary: Apna Dal (S) chief Anupriya Patel held an organisation review meeting at the party's camp office in Lucknow on Friday, 2 October. The meeting discussed preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, booth management and strategies to strengthen the organisation. After the meeting, a Bhaskar reporter asked Anupriya Patel about the challenge posed by former IAS officer Divya Mittal. Even after being asked the question nine times, Anupriya did not give a direct answer. She preferred to talk about other issues. Claim of an NDA 'hat-trick' in 2027 Speaking to journalists, Anupriya Patel said that Apna Dal (S) is a strong and reliable ally of the NDA. The NDA will secure a major victory in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election, just as it did in 2017 and 2022. She said- Our goal is to form an NDA government in Uttar Pradesh again in 2027. The NDA will have a candidate in every seat, whether the seat is allotted to Apna Dal or to another alliance partner. We will try to ensure the victory of the alliance candidate in every seat. To achieve this, every party worker will work on the ground with full strength. 'Opposition should stop making excuses after defeat' Anupriya Patel took a strong stance over the opposition's repeated questioning of the Election Commission, electoral rolls and the election process. She said that when the opposition loses an election, it tries to blame one institution or another instead of analysing its own failures. Dismissing the Opposition's allegations, he asked directly, "If the country's electoral process is completely tainted and flawed, then let the Opposition explain: whose governments are in power in Kerala, Karnataka, Punjab, Tamil Nadu and Himachal Pradesh? When Opposition parties win in these states, the entire electoral process suddenly becomes completely transparent and sound, but when the NDA wins the people's mandate and forms the government, questions begin to be raised about the process. If the Opposition's argument is correct, should the governments of all these states also be dissolved?" He further said that the Opposition had gained some electoral advantage in the 2024 election by creating an atmosphere of lies and confusion, but the people had now understood this tactic. The Opposition would face defeat once again in 2027. 'A 100% strike rate is our sole target' Addressing party office-bearers and workers during the review meeting, the Union minister put forward her views in a highly aggressive yet positive manner. After conducting a detailed review of the organisation, she assigned several important responsibilities to the workers- 1. Resolve to achieve a 100% strike rate: Anupriya Patel gave workers clear instructions that the party's goal in the upcoming election should not merely be to contest, but to ensure the victory of every candidate it fields - a 100% strike rate. She said the main purpose of the organisation's review meetings was to ensure that not the slightest shortcoming remained in its structure. 2. Let the flag fly at every doorstep and hut: Supporting the campaigns announced by the state president, she said, 'The time has come for workers to take the Apna Dal flag in their hands and set out from village to village and street to street. Not a single village or booth in Uttar Pradesh should remain where the Apna Dal flag is not seen flying over a house, doorway or hut. When the party flag is visible everywhere, the workers' morale and confidence will increase many times over.' 3. If opponents attack you, know that you are on the right path: Encouraging the workers, he said that when opponents feel threatened by your existence, they resort to abusive language and criticism out of frustration and desperation. He told the workers, "If you are being targeted from all sides, it simply means that you are at the centre of the entire discussion and are receiving plenty of attention. Learn to enjoy the desperation of your opponents and keep your eyes fixed solely on your goal, like a fish's eye." 4. Pay special attention to maintaining linguistic propriety: He strictly instructed all party workers and the social media team that linguistic propriety must not be violated under any circumstances on public platforms, at meetings or on social media. The party's identity must remain that of a disciplined and positive organisation. Major Announcement of Upcoming Programmes The dates of major programmes to be held in the coming days were also announced to further broaden the party's support base. stories.title: 16-year-old boy goes missing after taking initiation from Sant Premanand:Parents protest outside Vrindavan ashram, plead ‘Give our son back’
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy from Hathras has been missing for three months. His parents and other family members arrived in Vrindavan on Friday. They claim that their son was initiated by Sant Premanand Maharaj at the Kelikunj ashram three months ago. He has not returned home since then. The boy has been identified as Anuj Chaudhary. He is a resident of Baramai Kheda village in Hathras. His family members have been staging a sit-in outside the ashram since 11 a.m. Those taking part include Anuj's father, Rajveer Singh, his mother, grandmother, four sisters, uncle and other villagers. The family members said they would not leave the area outside the ashram until Anuj was found. See 4 pictures from outside the ashram : Father said, "Give me my son back. We will leave from here." Father Rajveer Singh said that Anuj's maternal grandparents' home is in Panigaon, near Vrindavan. During this time, he started visiting Keli Kunj Ashram to seek the blessings of Sant Premanand Maharaj. After some time, he decided to take initiation and, after persuading his mother, received initiation from Premanand Maharaj around three months ago. After taking initiation, he stayed at home for five days. He then said that he was going to seek Maharaj's blessings. He left home carrying the kanthi mala given to him by Premanand Maharaj and three books. Three months have passed since then, but to this day, the family has neither seen his face nor spoken to him. Rajveer Singh said that Anuj is his only son among four daughters. He was studying and was in intermediate this year. He is around 16-17 years old. Rajveer is a farmer. He said, "Give me my son back. We will leave from here." Grandmother alleges: Ashram staff pushed them out Anuj's grandmother, Munni, said, "On the 25th, it had been three months since he received initiation. He came home after receiving initiation. After that, he said he was going to seek Premanand Maharaj's blessings. He went to the Keli Kunj Ashram. Since then, we have received no information about him." She alleged that the family went to the ashram to seek information about Anuj, but the people there did not listen to them and pushed them out. According to Munni, the family also asked to see the recordings from the cameras installed at the ashram, but they were not allowed to check the cameras. Munni said the ashram only told them that Anuj was engaged in spiritual practice and would return. She said the family had filed complaints at the Sadabad and Bisawar police stations. The police also visited the ashram, but the family has still received no information about Anuj. Anuj's grandmother, Munni, said there was still no trace of the child. She said, "There is a saint at the ashram. He told us on Thursday that he would hand over the child within two hours, but there is still no sign of those two hours either. We spoke to him yesterday." According to Munni, the family last spoke to Anuj by phone on the morning of 3. They have been unable to contact him since. She said, "Our only demand is that we want our child. We have not met our child for three months. We have not been sitting here since yesterday, but for three months, yet we still have not been given our child." Police arrive outside the ashram Vrindavan police arrived after receiving information about the sit-in outside the ashram. Vrindavan Circle Officer Sandeep Singh and Kotwali in-charge Ashwani Kumar spoke to the family members and gathered information about the entire matter. The police team then went inside the ashram and sought information about Anuj. Ashram management says-Anuj is not here A seeker from the ashram came out with the police. He told the family members that Anuj's photograph had been sent to the group of the ashram's volunteers. Thousands of disciples had visited the ashram during Guru Purnima. Information about Anuj was sought at that time as well, but he could not be traced. The ashram management is ready to provide all possible assistance to the family. However, the family members were not satisfied with this response. Case already registered in Sadabad Vrindavan Circle Officer Sandeep Singh said that a case has been registered in Sadabad in connection with Anuj's disappearance. Records related to his initiation at the ashram are also being checked. Police are investigating the matter. The family alleges that no one from the ashram had been willing to speak to them directly for so many days and that they had not been given clear information about Anuj. -------------------- ... CCTV footage of Premanandji's disciple jumping from the 4th floor: Sat on the boundary for 6 seconds, lay on the floor, then suddenly got up and jumped CCTV footage has emerged showing Premanand Maharaj's 25-year-old disciple, Rasik Dulari Sharan, jumping from the fourth floor in Vrindavan. It shows him sitting on the terrace boundary wall. Six seconds later, he lies down on the floor. He suddenly gets up and jumps over the boundary wall. Seeing this, the second disciple arrives running. He looks down and sees that Rasik Dulari Sharan had died by suicide at 10:35 a.m. on 25 September. The CCTV camera installed on the roof recorded the entire incident.Read the full story...

stories.title: SP workers, police clash during symbolic ashes procession:Police carry protesters away in Lucknow; SP stages protest
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party workers held a symbolic funeral urn procession for the Election Commission in Lucknow on Friday. Carrying the urn and raising slogans against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft, the workers clashed with police when they were stopped. When police tried to take them into custody, dozens of women and police personnel lay down on the ground. Police officers were seen carrying some protesters by their legs and dragging them towards the van. In one instance, a police officer lifted a worker with both hands, carried him to the van and put him down near it. The police later took the protesters to Eco Garden. The Samajwadi Party workers had gathered near Janpath Market at around 12 noon on Monday and started moving towards the state assembly to protest. However, police stopped them in Hazratganj. The protesters accused the police of misbehaving with them and tearing their clothes. Police tried to stop the protesters at the spot, leading to a long commotion between the two sides. Watch the visuals below : Now read what the activists said... Abhishek Yadav, who had come from Barabanki to take part in the protest, said that Gyanesh Kumar had murdered democracy. "We will remain on the streets until he resigns," he said. He alleged that more than 35 crore votes had been stolen to help form BJP governments in different states and at the Centre. He alleged that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the entire Election Commission, acting at his direction, were working for the BJP. He said they would fight to save democracy, from the streets to Parliament. 'We set out to immerse the Election Commission's ashes' Arriving with an urn containing ashes, Chhotu said they were going to immerse the Election Commission's ashes. They said, "The Election Commission is dead, and this urn contains its ashes." They alleged that the Election Commission was favouring the BJP and that cheating was being carried out continuously. Chhotu alleged that after Bihar and West Bengal, preparations were now under way to influence Uttar Pradesh as well. They said elections would not be allowed to take place in Uttar Pradesh until Gyanesh Kumar was removed as Chief Election Commissioner. According to them, the Election Commission's functioning had weakened democracy. 'The Opposition has been raising the issue of vote theft from the outset' Rinki Singh, who took part in the protest, said that Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had been raising the issue of vote theft for a long time. She claimed that evidence had also been presented several times, but the Election Commission had taken no action. Rinki said that questions had once again been raised over the Election Commission's role following a report published in an English newspaper. She alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party was benefiting from the Election Commission's collusion.

stories.title: Ordered wrench, pepper spray online to kill mother:Lucknow son used AI to plan murder in diary; loved dressing like girls
stories.summary: A 17-year-old boy was detained by Lucknow police in connection with the murder of his mother on Friday. The investigation found that he had planned the murder in advance. He had ordered a master wrench and pepper spray online and had also written the murder plan in a diary with the help of AI. The diary also contained details of the items to be used in the murder and instructions to keep hot water ready to destroy evidence after the incident. Police have taken the diary, mobile phone, wrench and the clothes worn during the incident into custody and sent them for forensic examination. According to the police investigation, the boy did not like his parents’ restrictions. He would become aggressive when anyone touched his body. He also liked dressing and grooming himself like girls. Police are including these aspects in their investigation. See pictures of the crime scene : Reached home on the pretext of meeting his mother, committed the crime within 15 minutes The incident took place on the night of 1 October in a flat at Vision Apartment. According to the police, the boy had reached home on the pretext of meeting his mother. He told her that he would make tea. The room door then remained closed for around 15 minutes. During this time, he struck his mother several times on the head with a wrench. After the incident, the boy himself called his father and the police to inform them about what had happened. As soon as they received the information, police officers, including DCP West Jitendra Srivastava, reached the spot. The forensic team collected evidence from the scene. The boy began living separately in Ganeshganj four months ago A close family member, Naresh, said the boy had been troubled by his gender identity since he was around 10 or 11 years old. His behaviour began to change as he grew older. After disputes and physical altercations began occurring at home, the family rented a separate flat for him in Ganeshganj around four months ago. He then began living there alone. Father says his son was undergoing treatment According to the boy's father, his son had been receiving treatment at different hospitals for mental health problems. Naka police station in-charge Vivek Chaudhary said the teenager had been taken into police custody and was being questioned. All aspects, including the reason for the murder and the dispute within the family, are being investigated. Naka police station in-charge Vivek Chaudhary said- Information related to the incident may be stored on the mobile phone. However, the accused is not revealing the phone's password. Action is currently being taken.

stories.title: CM Yogi spins charkha on Gandhi Jayanti:Children sing ‘Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye’ in Lucknow; says, 'charkha symbolises self-reliance'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath spun a Charkha at Gandhi Ashram in Lucknow on Gandhi Jayanti. He urged people to follow Mahatma Gandhi’s message of Swadeshi and self-reliance in their daily lives. Children also sang ‘Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye’ during the programme. Yogi said Gandhi led movements peacefully and transformed them into mass movements. He recalled his childhood association with the clothes and charkha at Gandhi Ashram. “The Charkha is not just a charkha; it is a symbol of India’s self-reliance and self-sufficiency,” he said. See the pictures... Swadeshi message turned freedom movement into mass movement The CM said Gandhi’s message of moving from Swadeshi to self-reliance became one of the foundations of India’s freedom movement. He said the freedom struggle, which was initially fragmented, became a mass movement under Gandhi’s leadership. Gandhi also encouraged people to embrace Swadeshi and self-reliance. Yogi urged citizens to make Swadeshi, cleanliness and self-reliance part of their daily lives, saying Gandhi’s messages continue to inspire people. He said the Uttar Pradesh government had announced a 25% discount on khadi products until January 30, 2027, on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. He urged people to make khadi part of their lives and respect the skills of artisans, craftsmen and weavers. He said the ‘Local to Global’ approach could provide them with a larger platform. Yogi said Gandhi’s message of self-reliance would form a foundation for Viksit Bharat. Yogi recalls Shastri's simplicity and ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’ Yogi also remembered former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, describing him as known for his simplicity and good nature. He said Shastri’s personality was simple yet firm and resilient, and that he demonstrated through his actions what he said. Yogi recalled Shastri’s slogan ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’, saying it became a guiding message for independent India. He said soldiers were protecting the country’s borders while farmers were working hard to meet its food requirements. Shastri’s appeal strengthened the sense of respect for both soldiers and farmers, he added. India self-reliant in food production The Chief Minister said India is now self-reliant in foodgrain production. He said the country can meet the needs of its large population and also has the capacity to supply foodgrains to several other countries. Yogi said soldiers guarding the country’s borders also represent the same resolve that Shastri placed before the nation in 1965. Yogi mentions Swachh Bharat campaign Yogi also referred to Gandhi’s emphasis on cleanliness, saying Prime Minister Narendra Modi carried forward the message through the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan. He said the campaign laid the foundation for a cleaner and healthier India and also helped raise awareness about women’s dignity.

stories.title: MP Chandrashekhar rides on Fortuner bonnet at high speed:5 cops cling to vehicle; returning from Sambhal
stories.summary: A video has surfaced showing MP Chandrashekhar Azad travelling seated on the bonnet of a speeding Fortuner. In the 15-second video, Azad can be seen sitting on the bonnet and leaning against the front windscreen, while five police personnel are hanging from the car’s doors. Several vehicles from his convoy can also be seen speeding ahead of and behind the Fortuner. However, Azad’s security personnel are seen signalling the other vehicles to slow down. The video is reportedly from September 29 and was recorded while Chandrashekhar was returning from a public meeting in Chandausi, Sambhal. After the video surfaced, the MP issued a clarification on Thursday. Chandrashekhar said, “There was a large crowd in the convoy and a traffic jam was forming. The police were unable to control the crowd. Therefore, I had to violate security protocols, sit on top of the vehicle myself and explain the situation to the people.” Check out the VISUALS below : Read the full story below : Azad Samaj Party national president and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad held a public meeting in Chandausi, Sambhal, on 29 September. Hundreds of supporters were present in the event. It is reported that after leaving Chandausi, the supporters' vehicles began travelling with his convoy. The MP said that the large number of vehicles travelling with his convoy caused a traffic jam on the road. To get the jam cleared, he had to climb onto the vehicle himself and appeal to his supporters to clear the way. On Thursday, MP Chandrashekhar clarified the matter in Bijnor. He said a traffic jam had formed in front of the vehicle after the rally in Chandausi. The police were trying to clear the jam but were unable to move the crowd. The police could not even use batons because of him, as a large number of women were present there. He was forced to climb onto the vehicle to remove them and clear the way. The jam was cleared only after he folded his hands and appealed to the people. He added that he could not tolerate traffic jams on the road putting the lives of his workers at risk. If someone who is ill is on the way to hospital and gets stuck in a traffic jam, their life should not be at risk. SP said-Sambhal police can take action When told that the video was from Bijnor, SP KK Vishnoi said the matter was not from Bijnor district. The video is reportedly from Chandausi.

stories.title: Akash Anand apologises to Mayawati:Says won’t join another party; calls her decision to expel father-in-law right
stories.summary: Akash Anand apologised to his aunt Mayawati on Friday, saying she is his political mentor, inspiration and like a mother to him. He said, "Whatever I have learnt in politics, I have learnt from you. Whatever I have done, I have done under your guidance." He said his silence was misunderstood and led to rumours. "If this has hurt you, I apologise to you for it. I only want the opportunity to serve the party and the mission again under your leadership," he said. Akash wrote on X, “Whatever I have learnt in politics, I have learnt from you. Whatever I have done, I have done under your guidance. My silence was misunderstood. If this has hurt you, I apologise to you for it. I only want the opportunity to serve the party and the mission again under your leadership.” Akash also rejected speculation that he may join another party. He said, “I am not joining any other political party—not today, nor ever. The BSP is not just a party for me; it is my family.” After Akash was expelled from the party, Chandrashekhar and Akhilesh had offered him to join their parties. Since then, there had been speculation that he could join another political party. He said Mayawati was right to expel father-in-law from party Akash said Mayawati’s decision to expel Ashok Siddharth, his father-in-law, from the party and his decision to retire from politics was completely right. “I stand with that decision. Relationships have their place, but the mission is bigger than them. It is my responsibility to put the interests of the party and the movement above personal and family interests,” he said. Akash’s post has led to speculation that Mayawati may take him back into the party. There is also speculation that he could be given an important post ahead of the UP Assembly elections.

stories.title: School bus crash in Kanpur kills woman teacher:3 students injured, glass shards pierce heads and faces; they were heading for Gandhi Jayanti event
stories.summary: A school teacher died and half a dozen people were injured after a speeding dumper collided head-on with a school bus in Kanpur on Friday morning. Three children were among the injured, and two of them were referred to Hallet Hospital in critical condition. The accident took place around 8 a.m. near Harbaspur village on the Kanpur-Sagar Highway. At the time of the accident, 35 people, including five students, were travelling on the bus. The impact was so severe that the bus windows shattered, and broken glass scattered inside the vehicle. The incident triggered panic and screams among those travelling on the bus. The bus was carrying people who were on their way to attend a Gandhi Jayanti programme at China Public School in Ghatampur. After receiving information about the accident, police reached the spot and took the injured to Bidhnu CHC for treatment. Watch the visuals below : Story being updated...

stories.title: Two BHU women professors cheated:Fraudsters took ₹30 lakh promising flats; gave cheque under pressure, bounced twice
stories.summary: Two female professors from Banaras Hindu University (BHU) were duped of ₹30 lakh on the pretext of providing flats in Sunderpur on Friday. They booked one flat each at Brij Enclave but did not receive possession even after the promised deadline. Police have registered an FIR against builder Avinash Upadhyay, his brother Kalindi Upadhyay, Rishikesh Upadhyay and their mother after cheques issued to refund the money bounced. Dr Shabnam, one of the BHU teachers, had also lodged an FIR on September 23. Flats booked in May 2021 According to Dr Rita Singh's complaint, she and Dr Shabnam booked one flat each in a project by Sunderpur-based builder Avinash Upadhyay in May 2021. They each paid ₹15 lakh for the flats. The builder had promised to construct the flats and hand over possession by June 2022. The agreement also stated that if the flats were not handed over within the given period, the entire amount would be refunded with interest. However, the flats were not handed over even after the deadline. Flats booked on second floor still incomplete According to the complaint, both professors had booked flats on the second floor of the building. However, construction of the flats is still incomplete. The complaint alleges that the builder's phone has also been switched off for nearly two years. After considerable pressure, the builder gave both professors cheques for ₹15 lakh each, but the cheques bounced when deposited in the bank. About a month later, the builder issued cheques again, but bounced again. Chitaipur police have registered an FIR against four people, including the builder, and started an investigation. Station House Officer Rakesh Gautam said the documents related to the case were being examined. Further action will be taken based on the allegations in the complaint and the transaction documents.

stories.title: ‘Akhilesh divorced us, we accepted’:Minister Rajbhar calls SP sinking boat; says ‘Those who want to die can go there’
stories.summary: Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar lashed out at SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, saying, “Akhilesh Yadav has divorced us. We have accepted it too. We said, ‘Accepted, accepted, accepted’ three times. Why are you shouting now? The SP is a sinking boat; whoever wants to die should go there.” Rajbhar made the remarks on Friday in response to Akhilesh Yadav’s statement during a press conference on Thursday. Akhilesh had said, “You bring Rajbhar to us, and we will take him. We are waiting. He won with the SP’s votes; how will he win on his own again?” Rajbhar said, “What regard is there for party workers in the Samajwadi Party? Is any leader valued there? Muslims are treated as slaves there. The extremely backward classes are treated as slaves there. The party is dominated by the family, criminals and wealthy people.” He also targeted the SP’s PDA formula, saying that until recently the party talked about PDA — backward classes, Dalits and minorities. He said that now the family and wealthy people such as Dhanraj and Parimal Nathwani had entered the picture. Rajbhar added that the party was now looking for a criminal so that it could complete its PDA formula. Mayawati also lashes out at Akhilesh, saying, PDA is just a sham; tickets go to family members and wealthy businessmen Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati targeted Akhilesh Yadav over giving a ticket to Dhanraj Parmal Nathwani. She posted on X on Friday morning, saying, "The SP's PDA and socialism are a sham. Akhilesh has fielded his relative Ram Gopal Yadav in the Rajya Sabha election. The second candidate is Dhanraj Parmal Nathwani, who comes from a major industrial house." "The third candidate is only for face-saving. The SP needs PDA votes, but wants to make family members and capitalists MPs and MLAs. This is the SP's double standard. The poor, Dalits, Adivasis, extremely backward classes, Muslims and minority communities should become aware before the election. Their interests are safe only in the Ambedkarite BSP; everything else is a deception." About Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, whom Akhilesh gave a ticket
