stories.title: CCTV captures Premanandji’s disciple jumping from fourth floor:Sat on boundary for 6 seconds, lay on floor, suddenly got up and jumped
stories.summary: A CCTV video showing the moments before the death of 25-year-old Rasik Dulari Sharan, a disciple of spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj in Vrindavan, has surfaced. The footage shows Rasik sitting on the boundary wall of the fourth-floor terrace. After about six seconds, he lies down on the floor. He then suddenly gets up, climbs onto the boundary and jumps. A sadhu is seen rushing towards the spot after noticing what happened. He then looks down from the terrace. Rasik Dulari Sharan died after falling from the building at around 10.35 am on September 25. Dainik Bhaskar received this exclusive video today. He was cremated on the banks of the Yamuna on 26 September. Police have questioned more than 30 people linked to the Keli Kunj Ashram in the case. Watch the CCTV footage- Earlier CCTV footage showed him falling from the building A video showing Rasik falling from the fourth floor had surfaced five days ago. The footage showed him suddenly falling from a height of around 40 feet and landing on the road. Two cyclists were passing by at the time, while a water-supply vehicle also reached the area. One of the cyclists was reportedly a disciple. Rasik had been staying for around three months at the four-storey Guru Kripa Kunj building in the Varah Ghat area. The building belongs to Keli Kunj, a trust associated with Premanand Maharaj. More than 50 disciples and sevadars associated with the ashram reportedly live in the building, which is around 500 metres from Premanand Maharaj’s old Keli Kunj Ashram. Police investigating circumstances surrounding death According to police, Rasik went to the fourth floor of the building at around 11 am on September 25. He reportedly remained there for some time before falling from the terrace. He was taken to Sarvodaya Hospital in a serious condition, where he later died. Witnesses reportedly noticed injuries and bleeding. Police also found a grinder with blood stains inside his room. Investigators are looking into whether the injuries were self-inflicted. Post-mortem found multiple injuries The post-mortem examination of Rasik Dulari Sharan Das was conducted on September 26 by a two-doctor panel. The procedure was also videographed. According to the preliminary report, injuries were found on his head, legs and waist. The report also noted injuries to his private parts. The body was subsequently handed over to his family. After the post-mortem, it was taken by ambulance to the banks of the Yamuna for the last rites. His mother Laung Devi, sister Machhla, brother Manish and brother-in-law Sonu Patel reached the spot. More than 10 people associated with the ashram also attended the cremation before returning to the Ashram. Took initiation from Premanand Maharaj two years ago Rasik Dulari Sharan was originally from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh. He came to Vrindavan two years ago and took initiation from Premanand Maharaj. He subsequently changed his name from Deepak Lodhi to Rasik Dulari Sharan. Since he had experience in electrical work, he was assigned electrical-related duties at the ashram. Deepak was the second of three siblings. He had an elder sister and a younger brother, Manish. His mother, Laung Bai, had visited Vrindavan about a year ago and stayed at another place for five days. During that period, she reportedly met Deepak regularly. He was also reportedly said to have completed a 3,000-km Narmada Parikrama. Mother alleged she was not allowed to meet him Rasik’s mother reached the spot after being informed about the incident. She said she had last spoken to her son two years ago and was informed that he had fallen from a building. She said the family rushed to Vrindavan after receiving the information. She also alleged that the family had visited him earlier but was not allowed to meet him. “God will take action against those responsible,” she said. Questions remain over circumstances of death Several questions surrounding Rasik’s death remain unanswered. Police are investigating the circumstances leading up to the incident, while people associated with the ashram have not publicly commented on the reasons behind his death. A blood-stained grinder was reportedly found in his room, while the post-mortem recorded injuries to his private parts. Investigators are examining whether these injuries were self-inflicted and, if so, what led to them. The circumstances preceding his death, including his movements inside the building and the events captured in the CCTV footage, are part of the ongoing investigation.

stories.title: Killed by woman he loved:Siddharthnagar mother says, ‘Thought daughter-in-law would bring happiness, never knew she’d become his killer’
stories.summary: A Class 11 student from Siddharthnagar fell in love with a Class 12 girl after they met on Instagram. Within months, the two decided they could not live without each other. Their families eventually accepted the relationship and got them married. But around six months after their marriage, the relationship ended in tragedy. The wife, Jyoti, strangled her husband, Amit Chaudhary, with his old school tie on the night of October 2, 2024. On September 30, 2026, a court sentenced Jyoti to life imprisonment and imposed a fine of ₹10,000. The case is from the Chilhya area, around 18 km from Siddharthnagar district headquarters. What led to the growing differences between the couple, who had once been deeply in love? Why did they frequently argue? And what happened that night? To find answers to such questions, Dainik Bhaskar visited the home of Amit Chaudhary in Santori village-the boy who was murdered. What his family revealed was shocking… Their story began on Instagram In December 2023, Amit Chaudhary, then 22, and Jyoti, 21, met through Instagram. Amit was from Santori village in the Chilhya area, while Jyoti was from Budhnaiya Pakdi village under Shohratgarh police station. Their conversations gradually turned into a relationship. On March 12, 2024, the two left their homes together. Their families were initially upset but later accepted the relationship. Both belonged to the same caste. On March 19, 2024, they got married in a court ceremony. A reception was later held in the village, with the entire community invited. Amit's mother, Vindhyavasini, believed her son had found the partner he wanted and that his life would now be settled. Six months later, a night changed everything On the night of October 2, 2024, Amit and Jyoti went to their room after dinner. At around 11.30 pm, Jyoti allegedly tied Amit's hands with a dupatta and then tightened his old school tie around his neck, killing him. After the incident, Jyoti herself called the emergency number 112 and told the police that she had killed her husband and was still inside the room. When Chilhya police and PRV personnel reached the house, the room was locked from inside. Jyoti opened the door herself. Amit was found lying lifeless on the bed, with marks around his neck. Family says arguments had increased During questioning, several details emerged. Jyoti alleged that Amit used to ask her for money. His family, however, said Amit had stopped her from using Instagram after their marriage. They claimed this had become a frequent source of arguments between the couple. The same social media platform through which they had met had reportedly become a source of conflict in their marriage. Father: “Everything ended for us” Amit was the only son of Santosh Chaudhary and Vindhyavasini. He had three sisters and was the family's only son. His mother still breaks down when she sees the room where her son died. Trial lasted nearly two years After Jyoti was sent to jail on October 3, 2024, the case was heard in the Siddharthnagar District and Sessions Court for nearly two years. A total of 24 witnesses, including doctors, police personnel and family members, were listed. Nine gave key testimony during the trial. On September 30, Judge Ajay Kumar Srivastava convicted Jyoti Chaudhary of murder based on the evidence and witness statements and sentenced her to life imprisonment with a ₹10,000 fine. Father told court how police informed him Amit's father, Santosh Chaudhary, told the court that relatives had gathered at their home for the brahmabhoj ceremony of his mother on October 3, 2024. He said relatives were sleeping in the veranda, while he and his wife were downstairs. His three daughters and some children were sleeping upstairs, while Amit and Jyoti were in their room. At around midnight, UP-112 police arrived and called out his name. When he came outside, officers asked whether Amit Chaudhary was his son. Santosh said the police then told him that his daughter-in-law Jyoti had killed Amit. He went upstairs with the police. Jyoti opened the room's door from inside and walked towards the police. Santosh told the court that Amit was lying inside with blood coming from his mouth. His hands were tied with a dupatta and his neck was tightened with his old school tie. Mother: “My son was lying lifeless” Vindhyavasini told the court that there had been considerable activity at home because of the family ceremony. She said she and her husband were sleeping downstairs, while Amit and Jyoti were upstairs. When she heard the police calling around midnight, she followed her husband upstairs. She said the sight inside the room left everyone screaming. Sister saw Amit's body Amit's sister Anuradha was among the first and key witnesses in the case. She told the court that she woke up after hearing the police arrive and the commotion around midnight. She saw her parents going upstairs with the police. When she looked inside the room, she saw her brother Amit lying lifeless.

stories.title: AC bus-trailer collide on expressway, 4 killed:One side of 40-ft bus blown off; driver dozed off
stories.summary: Four passengers were killed and four others seriously injured after an AC bus collided with a trailer on the Gorakhpur Link Expressway in Ambedkarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, on Friday morning. The bus was carrying around 50 passengers from Delhi to Darbhanga in Bihar when the accident occurred at around 5 am. The collision was so severe that the left side of the nearly 40-foot-long bus was completely damaged, trapping several passengers inside. Most of the passengers were asleep when the crash occurred. Police reached the spot and, with the help of passers-by, cut open the damaged bus to rescue those trapped inside. The rescue operation continued for around 40 minutes, after which the injured were taken to hospital. Bus driver allegedly dozed off The bus was reportedly travelling at nearly 100 kmph when the accident occurred. The bus driver, conductor and trailer driver fled the scene after the crash. ASP Dr Tejveer Singh said the bus belonged to the Tighra Express travel service. A preliminary investigation suggests that the bus driver may have dozed off, leading to the collision. The accident took place in the Jaitpur police station area, around 50 km from the district headquarters. Pictures of the accident One victim identified Most of the passengers were from Bihar. One of the four deceased has been identified as Sachin Kumar (30), a Bihar resident. Police are working to identify the other three victims. The injured passengers include Sumit Mishra (33), Sumit Anand (40) and Rinku Kumari (45). The trailer was carrying tiles from Rajasthan to Bihar when the accident occurred.

Readers want Divya Mittal to contest polls on SP ticket:Prepare from Mirzapur; know what Bhaskar poll says
stories.summary: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal is set to enter politics. Since her announcement, there has been discussion about which party she will join and where she could contest an election. Dainik Bhaskar asked its readers two questions on the issue. Which party could give Divya Mittal the most success in politics? Four options were given, BJP, SP, Raja Bhaiya’s party and Independent. The SP received the highest share, with 30% of readers choosing the option. This means nearly three out of every 10 readers felt Divya Mittal could find the most success by joining the SP. The BJP came second with 28% of the votes. The option of contesting as an Independent also received 28% of the votes. Meanwhile, 14% of readers chose to join Raja Bhaiya’s party. This means the difference between the SP and BJP was just 2 percentage points. The Independent option also received the same share of votes as the BJP. Interestingly, instead of joining a political party, Divya Mittal has said she wants to enter politics as the ‘voice of the people’. She has said she will decide her political path in consultation with the people. From which Assembly seat should Divya Mittal contest the election? The options were Mirzapur, Chunar, Lucknow and Varanasi. Mirzapur emerged far ahead of the other options in the readers’ response. As many as 81% said Divya Mittal should contest from Mirzapur. Chunar received 8% of the votes, while Lucknow was chosen by 6% and Varanasi by just 5%. In other words, the votes for Mirzapur were several times higher than the combined votes for the other three options. Her administrative tenure in Mirzapur could be one of the reasons behind this response. Divya Mittal became the DM of Mirzapur in September 2022. She was widely discussed for her work involving public outreach programmes in rural areas and drinking water initiatives. An initiative to supply piped water to Lahuriyadah village was also undertaken during her tenure. Even after her transfer from Mirzapur, her farewell remained a talking point. She was given a farewell in the presence of local residents. Later, her tenure in Deoria also attracted attention. A debate over powers between elected representatives and the administration once again brought her into the spotlight. A 2013-batch IAS officer, Divya Mittal resigned from service on August 30, 2026. On September 29, she made it clear that she was entering politics.

stories.title: Blue drum case:Muskaan-Sahil’s lives to change after sentence; husband’s killer may wear white sari or suit, lover kurta-pyjama; diet to increase 1.5 times
stories.summary: The court will announce its sentence on October 14 in Meerut's high-profile blue drum murder case. Muskan, along with her lover Sahil, had murdered her husband Saurabh. District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra will pronounce the sentence for Muskan and Sahil. As soon as the sentence is announced, the lives of Sahil and Muskan in prison will also change. Both have been living as undertrial prisoners in jail for the past 17 months, but now they will become convicted inmates. Upon conviction, as per the UP Jail Manual, various aspects of their living conditions will change. For instance, Muskan will wear a white or cream-colored saree or suit, while Sahil will wear a white kurta and trousers. Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Dr. Viresh Raj Sharma, Senior Jail Superintendent of Meerut District Jail. Read on to find out how Muskan and Sahil's lives will change and what those changes will be… Sahil and Muskan will be seen in uniform Dr. Viresh Raj Sharma said, “As soon as they are sentenced, Muskan and Sahil will now have to wear prisoner clothing in jail. The uniform rule will apply to them. Under this rule, Muskan will be given a white or light cream-colored saree or suit. Sahil will be given the uniform for male prisoners: a white kurta and trousers.” “Both will have to wear these clothes so that they can be identified separately in prison. Undertrial prisoners can wear their own clothes, but after conviction, uniforms must be worn according to prison rules.” Sahil will be assigned hard labour Work will also be assigned to Sahil and Muskan. Since Muskan currently has a young child with her, she will not be made to work. However, Sahil will have to work. He may also be assigned hard labour. Along with this, files will be prepared to transfer both to the central jail. If either of them wants their family to appeal or wishes to appeal themselves, they can file an appeal in the High Court through the prison administration. As per the rules, family visitations will also be allowed. Diet to be increased by 1.5 times from normal After sentencing, prisoners' diets also change. Since convicted prisoners are made to do hard labour and more work in jail, which requires more energy, their diet is adjusted accordingly. Therefore, the diet for both will be increased. Additionally, their surveillance will also be heightened. Muskan and Sahil to be shifted to another jail After conviction, prisoners are also shifted to other jails. However, this transfer depends on seat vacancies in other prisons. Thus, Muskan and Sahil will be transferred to other jails based on the availability of vacant seats across state prisons. Male prisoners are often sent to the Central Jail in Agra. Female prisoners are sent to Nari Niketan in Lucknow. However, these transfers occur strictly on the basis of seat availability. Currently, the transfer of 300 male prisoners and 17–18 female prisoners is already pending. When seats become available, older inmates must be sent first, and only after that can Muskan and Sahil be shifted. Until then, both will be kept here in the Meerut District Jail. Wherever Muskan goes, her daughter will go with her. Since the daughter is under one year old, prison rules state that a child remains with the mother in jail up to the age of 6. Consequently, the child will stay with her mother until she turns 6. Not a name, but a prisoner number: A new identity for both Muskan and Sahil will receive their prisoner numbers only after sentencing. Muskan is currently in women's barrack 12A, while Sahil is in the men's barrack. Sahil's barrack might change, but since there are only two women's barracks in total, changing Muskan's barrack is unlikely. Both will be counted daily by their prisoner numbers, and their identity inside the jail will no longer be their names, but this very prisoner number. This number will be assigned according to the serial sequence on the day of sentencing. After October 14, Muskan and Sahil will not be able to see each other's faces October 14 will be the final date when Muskan and Sahil see each other for the last time. They will come face to face. Both Muskan and Sahil have been lodged in the district jail since March 19, 2025. During this period, they came face to face with each other on court hearing dates. On March 19, 2025, while going to jail, both saw each other. After that, on April 21, 2026, when Muskan and Sahil were brought to the District Judge's court for proceedings under Section 313, both saw each other upon coming out of jail. Apart from this, they occasionally saw each other during hearings via video conferencing. On September 30, 2026, both also joined together from the jail's video conferencing room and were able to see each other. Now, October 14 will be the final date when both will be able to see each other during the pronouncing of the sentence. After this, not only will meeting each other be impossible for Muskan and Sahil, but even seeing each other's faces will not be possible. Because Muskan and Sahil are neither husband and wife nor blood relatives, they cannot meet in jail. After sentencing, Muskan will serve her sentence in the women's barrack and Sahil in the men's barrack as per regulations. Their jails will also be changed in the future. Sahil's brother hires lawyer in High Court After sentence is pronounced in Meerut District Court, Muskan and Sahil can challenge it in the High Court through their lawyer. It is reported that a private lawyer has already been hired by Sahil's brother in the Allahabad High Court. The lawyer will file an appeal in the High Court for Sahil's bail and release. However, currently, there is no one from Muskan's side to secure her bail or contest her case.

stories.title: ‘Bharat Taxi 11% cheaper than Ola-Uber:Passengers happy, drivers unhappy; say saving ₹4-5 per km isn’t enough to run homes
stories.summary: The government-backed cab service ‘Bharat Taxi’ has been launched in Uttar Pradesh. It is currently operational in five cities — Lucknow, Prayagraj, Gorakhpur, Kanpur and Varanasi. In the coming days, the service will also be launched in the remaining 70 districts of the state. ‘Bharat Taxi’ is considerably cheaper for passengers compared to Ola and Uber. The Bharat Taxi app claims to increase drivers’ earnings as well. The company will not deduct any commission from drivers. Drivers joining the platform will also get insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh. However, despite these benefits, cab drivers are not happy. They say Bharat Taxi charges Rs 50 every day as a subscription fee. Fuel costs around Rs 5.50 per km, while the app pays Rs 10-11 per km. This leaves them with only Rs 4-5 per km. They question how they are expected to run their households on such earnings. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to cab drivers in Lucknow to understand their experiences and expectations after joining Bharat Taxi. Here is what they said… Know how Bharat Taxi is different from Ola and Uber Cab services such as Ola, Uber and Rapido are run by private companies in India. Bharat Taxi, on the other hand, is operated by a cooperative company, Sahakari Taxi Cooperative Limited. After trials in Delhi, Gujarat, Mumbai and Pune, Bharat Taxi has now been launched in Uttar Pradesh. So far, around 8.5 lakh cab drivers across the country and around 40,000 in UP have registered with the platform. Private cab companies such as Ola, Uber and Rapido increase fares during peak hours, such as during rain, festivals or office hours. Bharat Taxi, however, has been designed around a model of keeping fares stable. This means passengers will pay the normal fare even during peak hours. Private companies charge cab drivers around 25-30% commission on every ride. For example, if a driver gets a ride worth Rs 100, the company takes Rs 25-30, leaving the driver with only Rs 70-75. Passengers benefit, but we are bearing the losses When Dainik Bhaskar spoke to drivers on the ground, they listed 10 complaints about the Bharat Taxi app. Ramroop Verma, who has been driving a cab in Lucknow’s Lalbagh for eight years, says, ‘Bharat Taxi is completely useless. It is paying Rs 10 per km. CNG costs Rs 105 per kg in Lucknow. The fuel alone costs us around Rs 5.50 per km. What remains, Rs 4.50 to Rs 5, has to cover the vehicle EMI, maintenance and tyre expenses. How are we supposed to run our households?’ Ramroop further says, ‘Five years ago, we used to get Rs 200 for a 10-km ride. Today, we are getting Rs 100. Ola, Uber and Rapido are all the same. Uber gives us rides at Rs 8-9 per km, and on top of that, we have to pay a daily recharge of Rs 164, including GST. The recharge expires after 24 hours.’ The situation for drivers on Ola and Uber is generally similar. These cab service providers offer rides within cities at a base fare of around Rs 9-12 per km. In addition, they either charge drivers a commission of 25-30% or a fixed daily subscription fee of around Rs 150-160. Amid this entire calculation of earnings and expenses, drivers ultimately bear the pressure. ‘Rs 20,000 spent on panic button’ Durgesh Kumar, a cab driver from Amethi, met in Hazratganj, says, I have been driving a cab since 2023. I have also downloaded the Bharat Taxi app. I had heard that we would get the entire fare. But the reality is that I am not getting rides on the app yet. The app shows Rs 140-145 for a 10-km ride. There is so much traffic that only Rs 50-60 is left. I recently paid Rs 57,000 in road tax alone. Durgesh also highlighted another major problem. He says, The government has now made a panic button mandatory in all cabs. It costs around Rs 18,000-20,000. Those who have installed it say it is of no use. If it is not being used, why put a burden of Rs 20,000 on poor drivers? Downloaded the app, but still not getting rides We met Surendra at Polytechnic Chauraha. He drives his auto through different apps. Surendra says, Rapido works fine, while the other apps are behind it. We have downloaded Bharat Taxi, but we are not getting rides on it yet. If it works the way we have heard it will, then it will be good. Whose fare is how much? Know the rate list The Dainik Bhaskar team checked fares simultaneously on different apps at 6 pm for two routes, Kamta to Lucknow Airport and Kamta to Lulu Mall. Bharat Taxi currently has the cheapest subscription Cab drivers take subscriptions from different companies, after which they get rides more quickly. For example, Uber’s 24-hour pass costs Rs 139 plus 18% GST, taking the total to Rs 164. Ola’s pass is also priced at around the same rate. Rapido follows a slightly different model. Under its Rs 590 pass, drivers can earn up to Rs 10,000. Bharat Taxi, meanwhile, currently charges around Rs 50 for a one-day pass. Drivers joining the app in the initial phase are also being offered additional discounts under special offers. Therefore, the subscription charge may vary for different drivers. Eight major organisations invested ₹80 crore to set up Bharat Taxi The organisation operating Bharat Taxi is called ‘Sahakari Taxi Cooperative Limited’. It was launched jointly by eight major cooperative and financial institutions in the country. These include NCDC, IFFCO, NAFED, Amul, KRIBHCO, NDDB, NCEL and NABARD. Initially, each of the eight institutions invested Rs 10 crore. This means a total initial capital of Rs 80 crore was raised to start the company. Bharat Taxi will now compete with major cab companies such as Ola and Uber. For this, the company is preparing to raise around Rs 300 crore in funding. The money may be used to provide better offers to passengers and strengthen the company’s position in the market. Drivers to get Rs 5 lakh insurance cover The cooperative company also provides insurance to cab and bike drivers joining Bharat Taxi.

stories.title: Constable skips duty, enters poll fray on SP ticket:Says ‘Make Akhilesh Yadav CM’; alleges BJP backs those seeking to end reservation
stories.summary: A constable posted with Dial-112 in Gorakhpur has reportedly left his duty and is preparing to contest the Assembly election on a Samajwadi Party (SP) ticket. Sources claim that the constable remained absent from duty for nearly a year by allegedly managing the system, while his attendance continued to be marked. About three months ago, senior officers came to know about it and suspended him. Even after that, he did not report to the police lines. At times, he has been issuing posters welcoming senior SP leaders, while on other occasions, he has been appealing to people to join the party through slogan-based posters. In other words, he has been trying to build support among voters. In a photo wearing a red cap, he wrote: “Wear the red cap and move forward with socialism.” About a month ago, at an SP review meeting in Dhanghata, Sant Kabir Nagar, the constable said, “I belong to the Scheduled Caste, the Dalit community. The Dalit MLAs and MPs currently with the BJP are taking Dalit votes and supporting those who want to end reservation. Akhilesh Yadav is saying that this will be the last election. If you and I do not wake up, the elections and the Constitution will come to an end. Come together and make Akhilesh Yadav the Chief Minister.” Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar over the phone, the constable said, “I have been inspired by the policies of the Samajwadi Party from the beginning. While being in the police department, I was unable to deliver justice to the public. That is why I thought of becoming an MLA. For the past three years, I have been actively working in the area and helping people.” Know the full matter in detail, Seeking ticket from SP for Sant Kabir Nagar’s Dhanghata seat Constable Shyam Sundar Chauhan is originally from Naina Jhala village under Mahuli police station in Sant Kabir Nagar. He has three children—one son and two daughters. He joined the police as part of the 1994 batch of constables and has been posted in 11 districts. In 2023, he was transferred from Kushinagar to Gorakhpur, where he was posted with Dial-112. It is being reported that during his posting in Gorakhpur, he began preparing to contest the election from the Dhanghata Assembly constituency in Sant Kabir Nagar. His oldest social media post dates back to 2023, when he wished the people of the Dhanghata Assembly constituency a Happy New Year. Since then, he has regularly posted about activities in the area and his political involvement. Photo on SP banners, ‘constable’ written alongside his name Shyam Sundar has reportedly been campaigning in the area while remaining absent from duty for a long time. During this period, he has been visiting villages in the Dhanghata Assembly constituency and meeting people. Several photos and videos of him campaigning can be seen on social media. However, it has not been clarified at the departmental level how his attendance was marked while he remained absent. Shyam Sundar has used Samajwadi Party banners in his social media posts and campaign material. His photograph appears on the posters, with the word ‘constable’ written alongside his name. In one poster, he is seen wearing a red cap. Photos of senior Samajwadi Party leaders have also been placed alongside his. Shyam Sundar has staked his claim for an SP ticket from the Dhanghata Assembly seat. He has said that he will contest the election if the party leadership gives him the ticket. Trying to strengthen his claim ahead of the 2027 election The Uttar Pradesh Assembly election is scheduled for 2027. With this in mind, the activities of political parties and potential candidates have increased in the Dhanghata seat as well. Shyam Sundar is also attending party programmes and trying to strengthen his claim for the ticket. Says from the stage, ‘I, Shyam Sundar Chauhan, constable, welcome you all’ About a month ago, a review meeting of booth presidents, zone in-charges and sector in-charges was held in Lohreya in the Dhanghata Assembly constituency. Shyam Sundar addressed the meeting. He said, “I, Shyam Sundar Chauhan, constable, welcome you all.” He added, “On the instructions of the national president, this conference of booth presidents is being held across the state. Detailed discussions are taking place on how to strengthen the party. Whoever wins the booth will be the winner. Whoever wins their booth will help us form the government.” ‘A government employee cannot contest elections while in service’ The constable has not resigned from his job. According to sources, the reason is that he allegedly wants the police department to dismiss him. This, the sources claim, would allow him to approach the court and potentially seek reinstatement if he loses the election or something goes wrong. There are clear provisions under the Uttar Pradesh Government Servants’ Conduct Rules regarding government employees actively participating in the activities of a political party and contesting elections. The rules prohibit government employees from joining political parties and from contesting, interfering in or using their influence in Assembly or local-body elections. Retired police Circle Officer Shiv Pujan Singh said, “No employee can contest an election while holding a government job. If a government employee engages in political activities in violation of the rules, departmental action can be taken against them, which may even include dismissal from service.” Gorakhpur SP Crime Ayodhya Singh said, “Shyam Sundar Chauhan has been under suspension for quite some time. He is not reporting for attendance either. We are trying to contact him and find out the reason for his continued absence.”

The Congress leader , declaring to launch a fresh protest from Jantar Mantar, said, "Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," and called him an “illegitimate” poll body chief.

stories.title: 'Truly historic milestone': Leaders hail PM Modi as he completes 25 years in government
CM Yogi Adityanath hails PM Modi on 25 years as head of govt, says he presented Gujarat as model State
The loss of Jeffrey Archer feels personal because we miss the India of the 1980s – the India of simple pleasures
stories.summary: The novelist who became family to Indians

stories.title: DMK’s mixed signals on Rahul: Ex-ally backs Cong MP’s anti-CEC protest day after questioning silence on Tamil Nadu SIR
'You have failed Bengal': Mamata's TMC claims 2,400+ rape cases in 5 months under BJP
Hugh Jackman joins charity-focused ticketing platform Humanitix
Wyoming Army veteran fought mountain lion bare-handed to save dog
Supreme Court to examine plea seeking recall of split verdict on CEC, EC appointment law
Meet Kimberley Christopher, FSU doctoral candidate developing plasma technology to destroy ‘forever chemicals’
stories.summary: Kimberley Christopher, pursuing her doctorate, is innovating a patented plasma technology designed to eliminate PFAS contaminants effectively. This groundbreaking approach aims not merely to relocate these stubborn chemicals but to transform them into non-toxic byproducts. Recently, she triumphed in a pitch competition, propelling her research into a stage backed by the National Science Foundation.

stories.title: NASA sent 10 million basil seeds to space, inspiring nearly 1 million students
Ron Burkle bought Frank Lloyd Wright’s Ennis House for $4.5M, restored it, then sold it for $18M
stories.summary: Billionaire investor Ron Burkle acquired the iconic Ennis House, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, at a bargain due to its deteriorated state. After pouring approximately $17 million into comprehensive renovations, the property was exquisitely restored and listed for $18 million in 2024. This impressive sale established a new benchmark for architecturally significant homes, underscoring the importance of conserving historic structures for future appreciation.

stories.title: 'Like your movie, money is Ata Pata Laapata': SC directs Rajpal to pay Rs 2 crore by Oct 13
'SIR —Shahenshah Instigated Removal': Congress takes jibe at 'diabolical duo' over Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi FIR
Scientists breed rare rattlesnake for first time, six babies born to aid recovery
'Inflation man Modi's reign of terror continues': Congress on repo rate hike
Opposition seeks President Murmu's appointment over CEC Gyanesh Kumar issue
'Those who opposed me taught me power of democracy': PM Modi on completing 25 years in public service - top quotes
'Roll no. 1, resigned sir, roll no. 2, behind sir!': CJP takes jibe at Pradhan amid anti-Gyanesh stir
A 1920-era American elm survived a 4,000-pound bomb in Oklahoma City
stories.summary: An American elm in Oklahoma City known as the Survivor Tree has observed many changes since its likely planting in 1920. The tree was growing in a family backyard before commercial development removed surrounding trees and structures. In 1995, the elm endured significant damage from the bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building while remaining standing.

stories.title: Kharge to host INDIA bloc lunch as opposition plans next move after ‘vote chori’ protest
After Delhi and Mumbai, Bengaluru to protest against SIR on Thursday - all you need to know
'Unable to distinguish between victim & perpetrator': India tears into OIC over J&K remarks at UN
FIR registered against Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi over entry into Akashvani Bhawan during protest
Ashok Chakra for flydubai pilot Smit Machchar? Rajya Sabha MP Kartikeya Sharma urges PM Modi
KPSC recruitment case: Suspended chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar, member BV Geetha detained
Three new SC judges take oath, all in the name of God; number of women judges in SC – three out of 37
PM Modi offers prayers at Delhi temple as he completes 25 years in public office
‘This is merely the beginning’: Congress warns Gyanesh Kumar after INDIA bloc protest
'Congress loses even on ballot papers': Himanta hails NDA's Silchar civic polls victory
'Against all odds': Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike awake after failed execution
stories.summary: Christa Pike, a death row inmate in Tennessee, is recovering at a hospital following a failed execution attempt. Her lawyers reported that she is awake and speaking after being unconscious for several days. Doctors say the extent of her recovery remains uncertain, and she might face a long rehabilitation process. Legal questions arise about whether Tennessee can execute her again after the failed lethal injection.

stories.title: African park once called a “silent graveyard” now has 37 rhinos and seven calves
stories.summary: Zinave National Park in Mozambique experienced severe wildlife loss during a 16-year civil war, which impacted biodiversity. Rewilding efforts initiated in 2016 have since introduced several species, including rhinos and lions. The introduction of 250 elephants has helped restore the park's ecosystem and enhance habitats for various species. Conservation programs and anti-poaching strategies have also been implemented to protect newly introduced wildlife.

stories.title: Ludwig Shares MrBeast Request: streamer says YouTuber sought honest video feedback; jokes off paid promo
stories.summary: Ludwig Ahgren revealed that MrBeast contacted him after several months without speaking, sending a link to his latest video and asking for his thoughts. Ludwig said he agreed to watch it and promised to share his “unadulterated thoughts.” He also joked about whether he should get paid for the promotion. Separately, Ludwig struggled with the difficult Geometry Dash level “GRIEF” during a recent stream.

stories.title: Gabe Newell’s Inkfish builds a $816 million, 162-metre deep-sea research vessel
80% vote in West Bengal bypolls amid rigging, intimidation charges
stories.summary: Bypolls across Nandigram and Rejinagar saw an 80% turnout despite allegations of rigging and voter intimidation. In Tamil Nadu, turnout dipped compared to previous elections, with results showing 86% and 80% participation. Assam's Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency recorded 76% turnout during the bypolls, while Puducherry's Thattanchavady seat had a turnout of 78% by 5pm. Various candidates and parties reported incidents of interference and blocked agents during the polling process.

stories.title: Modi's 25 years in office: A study in seva and action
stories.summary: Narendra Modi has completed 25 years of service as the head of government in various capacities. His commitment to service is evident from his early experiences in disasters and personal encounters. Modi's journey reflects the importance of courage and conviction in the face of uncertainty as he navigated numerous challenges. Spiritual principles have shaped his leadership style and influenced his decision-making processes.

stories.title: From Gujarat CM to India's PM: Modi's 25 years in office
stories.summary: Narendra Modi's journey began with his role as Gujarat Chief Minister, addressing state issues and implementing reforms. His tenure included launching significant initiatives like the Jan Dhan Yojana and Swachh Bharat Mission, aimed at improving welfare. The BJP's political maneuvers led to Modi becoming Prime Minister in 2014, marking a significant shift in governance.

stories.title: 3,000-year-old horse buried inside ancient Egyptian fortress may have been a chariot animal
stories.summary: Archaeologists have uncovered the remains of a 3,000-year-old young male horse inside Egypt’s ancient Abqaa’ fortress, suggesting it may have been used to pull a chariot. Nearby harness fittings point to its military role. Excavations also uncovered tablets bearing the names of Ramesses II and Merneptah, along with a depiction of a captured Libyan prisoner from the Meshwesh tribe.

stories.title: ED summons Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann kin in 5 crore graft case
stories.summary: Bhagwant Mann's wife Gurpreet Kaur faces a bribery allegation of Rs 5 crore related to a rape case. The Enforcement Directorate has summoned Amardeep Singh Grewal, Kaur's brother-in-law, for questioning. Grewal had requested an adjournment but is now expected to appear for statements. A high court has ordered a CBI investigation concerning allegations against Mann’s Officer on Special Duty.

stories.title: Congress itself, not EC, responsible for its losses: BJP
stories.summary: BJP has dismissed the march demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar as a sign of opposition frustration. During the protests, BJP representatives criticized Rahul Gandhi and questioned the credibility of his claims about member attendance. Union ministers expressed that the Election Commission is not responsible for Congress's electoral failures. BJP spokespersons emphasized the party's continued success and the opposition’s inability to connect with voters.

stories.title: Lake Hartwell Shoreline Cleanup: Drought exposes long-hidden trash; volunteers pull record 36 tires
stories.summary: In a remarkable display of community spirit, volunteers have gathered over 8,300 pounds of litter from the shores of Lake Hartwell, driven by an ongoing drought that has unveiled hidden debris. Amid concerns regarding the Clemson Lower Diversion Dam Saddle Dike, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has enforced specific restrictions.

stories.title: In 2021, Georgia police destroyed $37,000 hemp; 6 years later, Supreme Court revives grower’s claim
stories.summary: In 2021, Georgia police aircraft allegedly destroyed $37,000 worth of legally grown hemp during a drug-suppression operation. Six years later, the Georgia Supreme Court revived the grower’s compensation claim, overturning a 60-year-old precedent that broadly shielded government agencies from property-damage claims when acting under police powers. The ruling allows the lawsuit to proceed, though damages have not yet been awarded.

stories.title: Meet Shrikari Punjala, the student who turned eggshells into crystals
Amid Canada trade talks, NSAs discuss security coop
stories.summary: India and Canada are engaged in a security dialogue to strengthen their bilateral relations. NSA Ajit Doval hosted his Canadian counterpart David Morrison for discussions on security issues. Both nations reviewed their progress in law enforcement cooperation and identified areas for further collaboration. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand is also scheduled to visit India later this month.

stories.title: Flydubai flight incident: Cockpit attack left Captain Smit Machchhar with 'depressed skull fracture'
stories.summary: Captain Smit Machchhar faced serious injuries from his co-pilot during the flight's crisis situation. The co-pilot attacked him with an axe, resulting in a skull fracture that required emergency surgery. Doctors monitored his recovery closely and assisted him for further treatment in the UAE. The Indian embassy is providing support to Captain Machchhar and his family during this challenging time.

stories.title: Chang’e-6 soil reveals metallic iron in lunar samples; it may preserve clues to Moon’s lost magnetic field
stories.summary: Recent analysis of lunar soil samples returned by China's Chang’e-6 mission revealed a unique form of iron. This iron, γ-Fe, exhibits exceptional magnetic properties, which could provide insights into the Moon's ancient magnetic field. Researchers suggest that extreme impacts on the lunar surface caused the formation and preservation of this unusual iron. The findings could enhance our understanding of the Moon's geological history and its evolution over time.

stories.title: Punjab government moves Supreme Court against CBI probe into 'bribe syndicate' linked to CM Bhagwant Mann's OSD
stories.summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's government has approached the Supreme Court for an urgent hearing. They aim to challenge a High Court order that mandated a CBI investigation into corruption allegations. The High Court's concerns include alleged coercive actions by the Central Bureau of Investigation in the state. The Punjab government argues that the orders violate governance principles outlined in the Constitution.

stories.title: ED unearths bribe racket involving top executives of 40 PSUs, banks & companies
stories.summary: Enforcement Directorate has uncovered a bribery racket involving executives from at least 40 public sector undertakings and banks. This scheme involved laundering corporate social responsibility funds through multiple trusts operated by a fake doctor. The fake doctor has been impersonating a medical professional for nearly three decades while receiving substantial donations. Investigations revealed kickbacks were paid, with funds returned to donors after deducting commissions.

stories.title: Streamer Alleges Racial Profiling: Beard plans legal action; police deny claims
stories.summary: BenDaDonnn has broken his silence after being arrested in College Station and charged with evading arrest or detention. He says he was racially profiled and wrongfully detained and plans legal action. Police say he refused commands and tried to get away. His bond was $7,000, while his security guard Kenny Carter’s bond was $4,000.

stories.title: A storm stranded an Outer Banks couple from most of their wedding guests. Then hundreds of strangers showed up
stories.summary: Amidst the storm, Kimberly Laprad and Jayden Sink transformed their wedding on Hatteras Island into a community affair when their guests were unable to make it. Inviting locals resulted in an impressive turnout of 500 to 800 attendees who came together to support the couple. Local businesses generously provided food and services while the couple looks forward to returning every year to contribute to community initiatives.

stories.title: Election Commission: Was ready to meet 240 opposition MPs but not at their chosen venue
stories.summary: Election Commission declined a meeting with opposition MPs led by Rahul Gandhi at Parliament House annexe. The commission emphasized meetings should occur on its premises and through authorized representatives. Despite being offered a chance to submit a memorandum, the MPs rejected this proposal. The Commission stated it had not received prior appointment requests from the parties until late in the day.

stories.title: Wisconsin homeowner fights data-center power line over land and $81K offer
Cabinet adopts resolution hailing achievements of PM Modi
stories.summary: Cabinet has adopted a resolution recognizing Narendra Modi's 25 years of public service as Chief Minister and Prime Minister. This resolution highlights various policies that benefited the common man, showcasing Modi's governance style. It mentions key initiatives like SWAGAT and PRAGATI that improved governance and service delivery. Additionally, it discusses welfare schemes that helped millions escape poverty and empowered women in society.

stories.title: New dating rewrites history of Oklahoma meteor crater
stories.summary: Researchers from the University of Texas at Austin have traced the Ames meteor impact to approximately 370 million years ago, presenting a significant revision to the previously accepted estimate of 467 million years. This research connects the impact with the Frasnian-Famennian mass extinction event, employing zircon crystals to establish a more precise timeline, thus providing deeper insights into pivotal moments in Earth's geological history.

stories.title: Opposition's anti-SIR-CEC march turns into INDIA bloc-government face-off
stories.summary: Opposition members from the INDIA bloc, led by Rahul Gandhi, organized a protest march to the Election Commission. The police stopped their march just before reaching Akashvani Bhavan, leading to a lengthy dharna by the MPs. Despite police attempts to remove the protesters, several MPs entered the Akashvani premises and continued their demonstration. Rahul Gandhi criticized Prime Minister Modi and accused his government of treasonous actions against the country.

stories.title: CBI raids CM Bhagwant Mann’s camp office, his OSD’s home in graft probe
stories.summary: CBI conducted raids on multiple locations including the camp office of Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann. The investigation stems from a High Court order based on allegations from the Enforcement Directorate. Various individuals are named in the FIR for their alleged involvement in corruption and manipulation of government processes. Mann criticized the timing of the raids as politically motivated amid upcoming elections.

stories.title: In 1987, ancient glass sponge reefs were found alive off Canada's Pacific coast after 40 million years
stories.summary: In 1987, Canadian scientists discovered ancient glass sponge reefs alive in British Columbia’s Hecate Strait, overturning the belief that these reef-building animals had vanished 40 million years ago. More than 9,000 years old, the reefs survive today in Hecate Strait, Queen Charlotte Sound and Howe Sound, creating a rare underwater ecosystem often called the “Sea of Glass.”

stories.title: Cheetahs return to Zambia's Greater Luangwa after nearly 30 years
Maryland manure-lagoon overflow kills nearly 11,000 fish across 25 species, officials say
stories.summary: A tragic incident has unfolded at Basin Run, where nearly 11,000 fish have succumbed to the consequences of a manure lagoon overflow from Kilby Farms. The Maryland Department of the Environment has traced the source of this discharge back to a series of ongoing pollution violations. Local residents, frustrated with the recurring environmental harm, are demanding accountability.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Arms & drugs seized in cross-border smuggling case; 4 held
stories.summary: J&K Police arrested four suspects linked to cross-border drug and arms smuggling. The police seized a Beretta pistol, magazines, live rounds, and narcotics during this operation. Initial arrests occurred when two men were stopped at a checkpoint and found with heroin and a firearm. This investigation revealed connections with handlers based in Pakistan and previous air-dropped consignments. The case has been registered under relevant laws with further investigation ongoing.

stories.title: Kirk Douglas’ Beverly Hills home with 40+ celebrity autographs sells for $9M
Two sisters turned their childhood love of the ocean into a 65-foot research yacht
stories.summary: Angela Rosenberg and her sister took a significant step by establishing the ANGARI Foundation to fill the void in marine science education. Collaborating with Florida International University, they facilitate student participation in real-world expeditions aboard the research vessel R/V ANGARI. These experiences, including shark tagging and plankton exploration, aim to ignite students' passion for marine science, fostering a connection between youth and the ocean.

stories.title: A Costa Rican cattle ranch became a wildlife haven with 440 bird species
Fort Cronkhite: The abandoned WWII fort near San Francisco where giant 16-inch guns once shook the city
stories.summary: Fort Cronkhite, a former WWII military post in California’s Marin Headlands, once helped protect San Francisco Bay with massive 16-inch guns. Now part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area, the historic site preserves wartime buildings and military defenses alongside beaches, trails and Pacific views. Visitors can explore Battery Townsley and discover the area’s WWII and Cold War history.

stories.title: Scientists found a new magnetic mineral in Chang’e-6 Moon samples, preserved inside impact-glass particles
stories.summary: A groundbreaking discovery by researchers has unveiled a new magnetic mineral, γ-Fe, found in lunar samples from the Chang'e-6 mission. This remarkable find sheds light on the ancient magnetic environment of the Moon, now long lost. Detailed analysis of tiny iron particles within lunar impact glasses reveals that γ-Fe can maintain stable magnetic signals, potentially serving as a record of the Moon's magnetic history.

stories.title: Cabinet okays new body to bring roads, rail, ports, aviation under one planning framework
stories.summary: India's government has approved the creation of the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority for better planning. This new agency will oversee projects exceeding Rs 500 crore in various sectors. ITLA aims to improve coordination among transport ministries and ensure multi-modal integration. It will develop a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a ten-year horizon for effective planning. The authority will also establish a unified transport data repository for project assessment.

stories.title: 'CBI raid at Punjab CM's office result of BJP's frustration': AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal
stories.summary: In a post on X, Kejriwal said the CBI raid was an attempt to target Punjab's elected Chief Minister and alleged that the BJP had consistently "pushed Punjabis around" since coming to power at the Centre, citing the farmers' movement, the issue of Punjab's water and the Punjab University issue.

stories.title: Focus must now be on taking digital literacy, financial literacy to every citizen: Uttarakhand CM
stories.summary: The Chief Minister said the achievement was the result of the hard work and collective participation of teachers, students, neo-literates, volunteers and everyone associated with the campaign while congratulating the people of Uttarakhand on the state becoming the sixth fully literate state in the country.

stories.title: California schoolgirl's sewing project grows into nonprofit with 5,000+ care bags for women
stories.summary: Khloe Thompson, a California teenager, started making care bags for women in need after seeing homelessness. She founded the nonprofit Khloe Kares, which has distributed over 5,000 handmade bags containing personal-care items. The organization collaborates with local businesses and community groups to expand its outreach efforts. Thompson's initiatives have also included supporting children in Ghana and youth workshops on various topics. She received the George H.W.

stories.title: 'Expert in theatrics': BJP hits out at Rahul Gandhi over protest 'drama', row over meeting EC
CM Samrat Choudhary reviews Bihar flood situation, seeks damage report
stories.summary: Bihar has been hit hard by severe floods caused by unprecedented water levels in rivers, leading Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to assess the situation closely. Several districts reported significant destruction, and immediate relief efforts were set in motion. The Indian Air Force played a vital role by air-dropping food supplies to areas cut off from road access.

stories.title: City-wide low-emission zone for Delhi realistic near-term goal: CAQM official
Barricade stunt, chips, 9-hour dharna and detentions: All that happened at Rahul Gandhi-led CEC protest
4.9-magnitude earthquake hits Uttarakhand's Chamoli, tremors felt in Delhi-NCR
stories.summary: Earthquake tremors felt in Delhi-NCR

stories.title: Miami Beach’s historic Savoy Hotel could face demolition for a 38-story tower
stories.summary: Plans have been submitted to demolish much of the historic Savoy Hotel to construct a new 38-story tower. This project will utilize Florida's Live Local Act to overcome local zoning regulations and historic preservation concerns. The developer aims to retain a small section of the Savoy's facade and lobby in a nod to history. Local officials and preservationists have expressed strong opposition due to potential loss of cultural heritage.

stories.title: Trump says Iran taking out LA and San Diego would be 'small price to pay'
Lithuania ready to cover cost if US establishes military base
stories.summary: Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius has declared his willingness to finance the establishment of a permanent US military base in Lithuania. Since 2019, Lithuania has been hosting a rotating US battalion and is eager for a long-term military presence. Concurrently, the Lithuanian parliament is considering lifting constitutional prohibitions on nuclear weapons, a move that has drawn sharp criticism from Russia, citing heightened regional tensions.

stories.title: 'Unusual request': EC explains why it could not meet Rahul Gandhi-led opposition MPs
stories.summary: The Election Commission of India stated that no political party formally requested a meeting as protests occurred. Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, attempted to march towards the Election Commission to submit a memorandum. The Commission emphasized the need for parties to follow prescribed procedures when seeking meetings. After an unusual request from 240 MPs to meet at Parliament House Annexe, the Commission offered an alternative.

stories.title: FIR against BJP BLA over 'false' Form-7 applications, first such case in Telangana
stories.summary: An FIR has been lodged against BJP Booth Level Agent S Balachander for allegedly filing false voter deletion requests. The complaint, initiated by an election official, triggered a police inquiry. Congress leaders claim these submissions aim to unjustly disenfranchise valid voters from the electoral list. In response, Telangana’s Chief Electoral Officer has ordered District Election Officers to take action against these fraudulent applications.

stories.title: 'Making steady progress, regaining health': Indian embassy in UAE updates on flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar
Jack Dorsey’s Bitchat taken off Indian app stores over law-and-order concerns: Report
stories.summary: Bitchat, a decentralized messaging app by Jack Dorsey, has been removed from Indian app stores. The government cited concerns over potential law and order issues associated with the app’s functionality. Both Apple and Google complied with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology's request for the app's removal.

stories.title: US House passes resolution honouring Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar, condemns 'act of terrorism'
stories.summary: The US House of Representatives has honored Captain Smit Machchhar through a formal resolution, celebrating his courageous defense of the aircraft against a treacherous act by his co-pilot that placed all lives at risk. The flight safely reached Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, ensuring the passengers' safety. This resolution also acknowledged the vital contributions of off-duty pilots and crew members during the incident.

stories.title: 'Everything will be remembered': Rahul and Priyanka removed from protest site after high drama - watch
150 years, 6 generations and 650 protected acres: The story of a Colorado ranch
stories.summary: Hutchinson Ranch, the oldest family-owned ranch in Colorado’s Upper Arkansas Valley, spans 700 acres along Highway 50. The Hutchinson family has maintained ownership for six generations, successfully implementing conservation agreements protecting 650 acres. These agreements prevent the land from being subdivided for development while allowing the family to continue ranching. Notable historic recognition occurred in 2003 when the ranch was identified among the top endangered properties in Colorado.

stories.title: Pak, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agree to deploy forces in Gulf country amid Houthi attacks
stories.summary: Pakistan and Turkiye have agreed to provide military support to Saudi Arabia following regional security threats from Houthi rebels. Representatives from the three countries held an emergency meeting to reinforce their Mecca defense agreement. This agreement establishes collective defense provisions that aim for a rapid military deployment if any country is attacked. Additionally, the committee appointed a retired Pakistani General as secretary-general to oversee defense strategies.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: MEA condemns attacks on seafarers, IAF gets new chief, opposition steps up protest against CEC and more
In 2014, a Tennessee couple paid 58 cents for Vince Lombardi’s sweater; it later sold for $43,020
stories.summary: In an incredible find, a couple bought a sweater for just 58 cents at a Goodwill store in North Carolina back in 2014. While viewing a documentary, they learned that it had ties to famed football coach Vince Lombardi, as a tag revealed its association with his tenure at West Point. Eventually, it fetched an astonishing $43,020 at auction after being consigned by Lombardi's colleague's widow.

stories.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger donated $250,000 for shelters for homeless veterans before Christmas
stories.summary: In 2021, Arnold Schwarzenegger donated $250,000 to Village for Vets to help provide temporary shelters for homeless veterans in Los Angeles. Before Christmas, 25 tiny shelters were installed at the VA campus in West Los Angeles. Each provided a bed, climate control, electricity and a locking door, giving veterans who had been living on the streets a safer place to stay while moving towards stable housing.

stories.title: Florida couple saves colorful Sarasota cottage village housing 17 small businesses from demolition
stories.summary: The anticipated transfer of the Historic Downtown Village in Sarasota to a developer has been called off. The cottages, which accommodate various local enterprises, will remain in the care of Alex and Marlene Lancaster. While business owners faced uncertainty regarding relocation and the emotional fallout of potential displacement, they now breathe a sigh of relief.

stories.title: 'Efforts to hide Iran war costs': US senator alleges denial of access to Al Udeid base in Qatar
'No meeting request received from any party': EC officials as Rahul, Priyanka refuse to leave 'protest site'
stories.summary: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra staged a protest near the Election Commission's office, even as the EC said it had received no request from any political party seeking a meeting. Cong said they demanded a meeting to discuss alleged electoral irregularities and questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The police intervened and detained several opposition leaders as the protest escalated.

stories.title: Patrick Swayze’s former California ranch with a dance studio listed for $4.5 million after $2.9 million sale
stories.summary: Rancho Bizarro, an extraordinary estate crafted by the artistic duo Patrick Swayze and Lisa Niemi, has hit the market once again. This idyllic ranch boasts state-of-the-art equestrian amenities, a vibrant dance studio, and a cozy main residence. After its acquisition by Aileen Getty in 2015 for $2.9 million, it is now available for $4.5 million.

stories.title: The India mood: Confidence in the country, anxiety about careers
stories.summary: India leads in consumer confidence, yet respondents express significant worries about unemployment and education quality. Many Indians believe the country is on the right track, despite job market uncertainties. The disconnect between economic optimism and job security highlights ongoing issues affecting connected consumers.

stories.title: New Hampshire groundskeeper left $3.8m to his town after living simply
Jharkhand protest: Congress workers scuffle with police outside CEO office
stories.summary: In Ranchi, Congress workers in Jharkhand rallied outside the Chief Electoral Officer's office to protest against Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstration escalated as protestors clashed with police while attempting to breach barriers and defaced the commission's nameplate. Their aim was to draw attention to the challenges citizens face with the electoral roll.

stories.title: 'Once a skunk, always a skunk': DMK questions Rahul Gandhi's stand on Tamil Nadu SIR deletions amid anti-CEC protest
From hunted-out woods to a deer refuge: How a Missouri couple transformed their 300-acre property
stories.summary: Mike and Dana Blevins turned their 300-acre property in Missouri into a thriving habitat for white-tailed deer. After purchasing the land, they implemented habitat management practices supported by the Missouri Department of Conservation. Their efforts contributed to the significant recovery of deer populations in the region, which faced near extinction in the past. As chronic wasting disease poses new challenges, they took part in management efforts to control infections.

stories.title: Wisconsin bargain hunter paid $29 for painting; later identified as Heade, sold for $882,500
stories.summary: In a remarkable turn of events, a man from Wisconsin stumbled upon a magnolia painting for just $29 at a rummage sale in the 1990s. A decade later, the artwork was authenticated as the work of esteemed American artist Martin Johnson Heade. Auctioned at Christie’s, it fetched an astonishing $882,500, shattering initial estimates of $300,000 to $500,000.

stories.title: Andrew Sun-Zhuang built a $260 AI pitching machine with 94% strike accuracy
'Dhappa': Cops tried to stop INDIA bloc's march to EC; Rahul Gandhi pulled a surprise
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra gave the INDIA bloc protest against the Election Commission an unexpected second act after police tried to stop INDIA bloc march against Gyanesh Kumar and began detaining opposition MPs.

stories.title: George Lucas’ sprawling Skywalker Ranch in California
stories.summary: Nestled in Marin County, Skywalker Ranch is a vast 4,700-acre creative sanctuary brought to life by filmmaker George Lucas. This enchanting retreat features a Victorian-style main house used for professional gatherings and boasts Skywalker Sound, operating since 1987. With amenities like themed guest rooms, diverse dining options, and a health club, the ranch remains a unique filmmaking destination, nearly fifty years after its inception.

stories.title: Mayawati says no more expulsions for nephew Akash after father-in-law’s political ‘sanyas’
'Grave concern': MEA condemns attack on MV Royad Mammadov that killed 2 foreign seafarers, injured Indian nationals
US, China in talks for reciprocal visits to nuclear sites in bid to build trust
stories.summary: The United States intends to begin reciprocal visits to nuclear facilities in China, aiming to strengthen trust between the two nations. This proactive initiative seeks to avert a possible arms race amidst escalating worries over China's expanding nuclear arsenal. Currently, officials from both sides are engaging in preliminary talks. A pivotal meeting between US and Chinese leaders is expected later this year to enhance dialogue surrounding nuclear risks and capabilities.

stories.title: Ancient DNA reveals an unknown extinct bovine related to modern yaks
'Learn to serve selflessly from PM Modi': Kiren Rijiju targets Rahul Gandhi over anti-CEC protest
Montana student compares banana and plantain starch to make stronger bioplastic
stories.summary: Rye Lynn Rost, a seventh grader from Montana, created bioplastics using starch from plantains and bananas. She discovered that plantains have more starch and higher tensile strength than bananas. Rye performed tests by comparing both bioplastics against plastic parafilm to evaluate their strength. Her project focuses on making sustainable bioplastics that are durable in environmental conditions over time.

stories.title: 'Attacks must end': MEA says 11 Indian crew members injured in Hormuz vessel strike
Punjab DA case: HC asks chief secretary why criminal contempt proceedings shouldn't begin
stories.summary: Punjab's Chief Secretary, KAP Sinha, faces a contempt notice for allegedly providing misleading statements about the pending dearness allowance. The Punjab and Haryana High Court is scrutinizing his assertions regarding the resolution of issues related to the state's appeal in the Supreme Court. Previously, the court ordered the government to settle overdue dearness allowance for both employees and pensioners.

stories.title: Nintendo destroyed its 1991 Campus Challenge cartridges; one surfaced at a 2006 garage sale, sold for $20,100
stories.summary: In an astounding find, video game enthusiast Rob Walters stumbled upon a rare Nintendo Campus Challenge cartridge at a garage sale back in 2006. This unique cartridge was made for a competitive gaming event in 1991 and hosted modified versions of beloved titles, allowing players to achieve high scores during tournaments.

stories.title: Drones strike two vessels in Bulgaria's economic zone; one ship sinks
stories.summary: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev revealed that drones targeted two commercial ships in Bulgaria's Exclusive Economic Zone, leading to alarming consequences. The Togo-flagged Alfa Watan sank after critical damage, while the Able vessel from Palau caught fire. Remarkably, a Bulgarian ferry was able to rescue all 18 crew members, with two suffering serious injuries.

stories.title: 1928 LA manor once owned by Gene Hackman asks $5.995M
stories.summary: A nearly 100-year-old English-style manor in Woodland Hills is listed for sale at $5.995 million. Originally built in 1928, the property has hosted notable owners like Michael Curtiz and Gene Hackman. The manor features a cobblestone driveway, extensive gardens, and original architectural details that reflect its rich history. Since its last sale in 1994 for $1.71 million, the property's value has significantly increased.

stories.title: Street politics
Andy Roddick and Brooklyn Decker’s Austin estate sells for $4.65M after $3.7M purchase
stories.summary: After extensive renovations, Andy Roddick and Brooklyn Decker sold their sprawling 15-acre estate in Austin, Texas. They bought the property in 2013 for about $3.7 million, and in 2019 sold it for approximately $4.65 million. The property showcased their tastes and aimed to be a family-friendly haven. The couple continues to hold several properties nationwide, including in North Carolina, while still thinking of Austin as home.

stories.title: Dentist recalls crucial 45 minutes that helped save flydubai hero Captain Smit Machchhar
Jeffrey Archer: The Brit author who made Indians fall in love with English writing
stories.summary: Archer spent half a century writing about conmen, politicians, tycoons, rogues and impossible comebacks. In the end, none of his protagonists was quite as improbable, indefatigable or entertaining as Jeffrey Archer himself.

stories.title: MrBeast breaks personal YouTube record as $1 million grocery store video hits 125 million views
stories.summary: MrBeast recently shattered YouTube viewership records with his newest video, which has captivated audiences by amassing over 70 million views. In this thrilling grocery store challenge, contestants lived in the store for an astounding 202 days, consuming almost all 4.3 million calories of food and ultimately winning $1 million. The enthusiastic response highlights MrBeast's magnetic content, and he remains optimistic that his most impressive work is yet to come.

stories.title: INDIA bloc protest: Scrap SIR, restore deleted names, sack CEC Gyanesh Kumar - key demands
Fastest-growing Ebola outbreak: Kenya reports first case, patient dies
A 103-year-old World War II veteran has been tending the same basement bar in Maryland since 1963
stories.summary: Irv Koch, a 103-year-old World War II veteran, has tended the bar in the basement of his Pasadena, Maryland, home since 1963. More than six decades later, the cash-only tavern still has no fixed opening hours, with Irv starting the day when his first customer arrives and closing when patrons leave or he gets tired.

stories.title: From climbing barricades to Akashvani Bhawan twist: High drama at Rahul-led CEC protest - how it unfolded
FlyDubai flight incident: Did aviation miss the insider-threat warning?
13 insects in 99-million-year-old amber reveal new species with mouthpart nearly twice its body length
stories.summary: A remarkable new insect species, Cretodorus noonoo, has been unearthed from 99 million-year-old amber found in Myanmar. This intriguing species is linked to the Neazoniidae family, renowned for its extraordinary mouthparts. These long and flexible adaptations reveal specialized feeding behaviors on tree sap. This discovery sheds light on the ecological interactions within Cretaceous forests, illustrating the diverse evolutionary strategies that shaped ancient ecosystems.

stories.title: Delaware homeowner wins part of default judgment; court orders pond work, loan records in HOA case
stories.summary: In a noteworthy court case, Gwendolyn Colston took on her community developer without legal representation and secured a favorable ruling. The Delaware Court of Chancery instructed the developer to ensure the upkeep of ponds and drainage systems in the area. Additionally, Colston gained access to insights on a contentious $44,329.

stories.title: 'We are going to destroy BJP': Rahul Gandhi's big declaration as opposition sits in to protest against CEC
Is Reggie joining Cuffem’s Sinister Six after leaving Kai Cenat’s Clover Boys
stories.summary: Cuffem is assembling an exciting new creator collective called the Sinister Six, marking his departure from the Clover Boys. Recently parted member Reggie is being considered for this dynamic group. Among other potential candidates is Adin Ross, with a keen eye on brand implications. After fruitful discussions, tensions between Cuffem and Reggie appear resolved, fostering an environment for this fresh collaboration.

stories.title: Ford’s Mexico factory hired a hawk to cut pigeon activity by 80%
In 1934, America created a $1 duck stamp; it has protected 6 million acres
Two Saudi airports in Jazan and Najran targeted as tension with Yemen's Houthis escalates
Florida woman rides 7,000 miles, raises $17,560 for charity that helped her two decades ago
stories.summary: A Florida woman completed a 7,000-mile motorcycle journey across 48 states in six days. She raised $17,560 for Quantum House, an organization that supported her during her daughter’s hospital stay. The ride attracted attention, allowing her to create awareness about the organization. Jess's daughter, who benefitted from Quantum House, joined her when she presented the raised funds.

stories.title: 'Wanted to tarnish image': Delhi Police on man held over alleged AI poster showing cop sexually assaulting woman
stories.summary: Delhi Police arrested a 24-year-old man named Nadeem Ahmed for creating a fake poster featuring a police officer. Police said the poster falsely depicted the officer sexually assaulting a woman during a protest, intending to damage police credibility. Investigators said Nadeem claimed to be an independent journalist and used AI tools for his misleading content.

stories.title: South African tycoon to spend $402M turning 600-hectare farm into F1 circuit by 2031
stories.summary: Neal Froneman leads a consortium aiming to construct a $402 million Formula 1 circuit near Cape Town, marking a potential revival of South African motorsport after nearly 40 years. Currently in the pre-feasibility phase, the circuit is designed to accommodate 125,000 fans and will include a media complex and entertainment spots. If the endeavor succeeds, it could generate over 15,000 local jobs, enhancing tourism and the economy.

stories.title: 'Acted of his own volition': ACP Bhagat steps aside from Addl DCP charge amid harassment probe
'Largely irrelevant': Jaishankar says UN failing on Gulf, Ukraine, Africa and Covid
Abhijeet Dipke claims CJP activists receiving police notices threatening October 10 protest 'could turn violent'
Meet Sartaj Singh Gandhi, the student who built a sensor to detect spoiled meat
stories.summary: Sartaj Singh Gandhi, a brilliant seventh grader, has innovatively developed a device that monitors the freshness of various meats by tracking ammonia gas released during decay. His research revealed that peak ammonia levels were detected on day six of testing turkey, chicken, pork, and beef. With plans to broaden the device's capabilities to other food types, Sartaj dreams of a future in cardiothoracic surgery.

stories.title: 'Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, time to resign': Rahul Gandhi as INDIA bloc march to EC stopped
‘Unacceptable’: India reacts after Russian strike injures Indian sailor on Black Sea ship
stories.summary: India has strongly condemned the attack on the MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea, which tragically resulted in the deaths of two foreign nationals. Among the injured was an Indian sailor, prompting the Indian Embassy in Romania to act swiftly. They assured that all Indian crew members are safe and receiving medical care. External affairs minister S Jaishankar raised maritime safety issues at the United Nations General Assembly.

stories.title: 'Creating anarchy to relaunch Rahul': BJP on Congress's Form 6 claims
Delhi court grants bail to 17 students, journalists arrested during CEC protest
Case against Bhagwant Mann's OSD: Punjab govt to move SC against HC order for CBI probe into ED's graft allegations
'More skeletons are tumbling out': Congress trains guns at EC over new report on Bengal polls
New York declares disaster emergency over measles, 108 cases reported
Bengal bypolls: AJUP chief Humayun Kabir detained in Murshidabad after casting vote
'9/11-style scare': How Israel nearly 'shot down' flydubai jet with 170 aboard
Trump blames Iran for flydubai incident, Vance 'defers', says 'nothing conclusively yet'
Native plants are helping restore habitat in Florida's Saint Sebastian River
Jeffrey Archer, author and former British politician, dies at 86
'Tarique hasn't ruled out India visit': Dhaka
stories.summary: Bangladesh has highlighted the importance of trust and bilateral engagement for future relations with India. State Minister Humaiun Kobir stated that preventing extremists in India from making destabilizing statements is necessary. He mentioned that mutual respect is required for maintaining good relations between the two countries. A potential visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to India is under consideration, emphasizing direct dialogue.

stories.title: US nuke test detection experiment bid to assert its hegemony: Ex-nuclear chief
stories.summary: Anil Kakodkar commented on the US conducting a non-proliferation experiment to enhance detection capabilities of nuclear explosions. This experiment aims to ensure the US maintains its nuclear hegemony and deters other nations from nuclear tests. The Federation of American Scientists reported India's nuclear warhead status and capabilities. The National Nuclear Security Administration explained that the experiment involved advanced sensor measurements for better detection.

stories.title: National Commission for Women seeks gender-neutral childcare leave, shared caregiving by parents
stories.summary: National Commission for Women has proposed several recommendations to improve maternity and childcare laws in India. The commission advocates for gender-neutral childcare leave to be extended to the private sector. It also suggests increasing leave for adoptive mothers from 12 weeks to 26 weeks. Recommendations include creating more childcare facilities and offering maternity benefits to informal workers. The focus is on shared parenting and establishing family-friendly workplaces throughout the country.

stories.title: Delhi Police ACP Vivek Bhagat’s additional DCP charge withheld amid harassment inquiry
stories.summary: Delhi government modified an order regarding duty charges of 12 police officers after harassment allegations surfaced. Assistant Commissioner of Police Vivek Bhagat voluntarily stepped aside from his additional charge as the inquiry continues. The CDC assignment began prior to the allegations, ensuring it does not indicate a promotion. The complaints have been transferred to the Crime Branch for a detailed investigation and fair inquiry.
