stories.title: Police Report Details Gun Threat: Doherty’s girlfriend alleges armed breakup fight; case yet to reach court
stories.summary: Jack Doherty’s girlfriend allegedly pulled a firearm during an argument over their breakup before his September arrest, according to a Fort Lauderdale police report obtained by TMZ. She told officers she feared Doherty and had warned she would shoot him if he came closer. Doherty denied touching her and showed officers security footage that he said supported his account.

stories.title: Nepal ends flood search with over 5,000 still missing, including 189 Indians
stories.summary: Nepal has suspended non-essential search operations after the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods that occurred on August 26. The floods resulted in 1,455 deaths, with 5,285 people still unaccounted for, including many foreign tourists. Among the missing individuals are 189 Indians, along with tourists from various other countries. The government has shifted its focus towards reconstruction and rehabilitation efforts rather than continuing search operations.

stories.title: Supreme Court agreed to meet, then changed mind: ONOE panel chief
stories.summary: The Supreme Court initially planned an informal meeting with the parliamentary committee on simultaneous elections. However, the meeting was canceled after opposition MPs raised concerns about the appropriateness of the interaction. The Supreme Court expressed that discussing the matter could lead to future judicial review. The proposal for the meeting was suggested by DMK MP P Wilson.

stories.title: Lakhimpur Kheri case: UP changes public prosecutor; Supreme Court asks Allahabad High Court chief justice to decide on trial judge
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government informed the Supreme Court about replacing the public prosecutor in the Lakhimpur Kheri case. This decision was made in response to allegations raised against the outgoing prosecutor by a witness involved in the case. As the Supreme Court monitors the trial's progress, it was noted that 86 witnesses have been examined thus far.

stories.title: Visa doesn't create absolute right to enter India, says Delhi High Court
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court emphasized that foreign nationals do not have an inherent right to enter India. Justice Amit Mahajan pointed out that holding a visa does not ensure unconditional admission. The court noted various factors that could lead to denial of entry, including national security and public health. A plea by a Turkmenistan woman for reasons regarding her entry refusal was dismissed.

stories.title: Only 15% going to work use public transport: NSO
stories.summary: The National Household Travel Survey indicates that only 15% of workers use public transport for commuting. It reveals that 46% of workers rely on two-wheelers and cars, leading to traffic congestion. Walking is the second most common commute mode, with 28.3% of workers traveling on foot. Student commuting patterns differ significantly, with 37% walking to educational institutions.

stories.title: D’Arros shearwater colony grew nearly 10-fold after rats were eradicated
stories.summary: D'Arros Island's Wedge-tailed Shearwater population rose dramatically after rats were eradicated in 2003. Researchers recorded 2,768 breeding pairs in 2016 and 2,406 pairs in 2021. The colony spread across a larger area and exhibited higher breeding burrow density during later surveys. The study utilized direct counts and area-based estimates to determine breeding pair numbers. Identifying the peak incubation period in November was crucial for future population comparisons.

stories.title: In a record, over 10,000 women clear JEE-Advanced
stories.summary: Women's success rate in JEE-Advanced achieved a record high in 2026 while their IIT seat share remained mostly unchanged. A total of 10,107 women qualified, reflecting a 7.5% increase in their qualifying count. Admissions across IITs reached 18,861, with 20% allocated to female candidates. Significant gains were reported for SC and ST candidates in qualification rates.

stories.title: Pahalgam handler rallies LeT support via anti-Israel rhetoric
stories.summary: Saifullah Kasuri made controversial remarks regarding the Pakistan army's role in regional conflicts. He threatened to erase Israel from the world map and defend Saudi holy sites. After the Pahalgam attack, he has been active in public events to raise support. High-level meetings between Lashkar-e-Taiba and Hamas have been reported, indicating growing connections. Kasuri's actions reflect an increasing boldness post-attack, as he recruits youth and gathers funds.

stories.title: Elvis Presley raised $65,000 for USS Arizona Memorial; crewmen remain entombed in Pearl Harbor wreck
stories.summary: Elvis Presley raised $65,000 towards the USS Arizona Memorial in 1961. Completed that year and dedicated in 1962, the 184-foot memorial spans the sunken battleship at Pearl Harbor, where more than 900 crewmen remain entombed.

stories.title: Legislative privilege vs free speech: Supreme Court 7-judge bench may close case
stories.summary: Nearly 23 years after the Tamil Nadu assembly's breach of privilege resolution, a Supreme Court hearing is scheduled. The resolution imposed a 15-day sentence on some journalists but has since been withdrawn. Senior advocates claimed that the writ petition's cause of action no longer exists and argued the matter has become academic. As a result, the Supreme Court is expected to dispose of the petitions.

stories.title: World entering age of flux, India will rise to challenges: EAM S Jaishankar
stories.summary: S Jaishankar emphasized the uncertainties facing the world during his speech at the Kautilya Economic Conclave. He expressed confidence in India's ability to navigate challenges such as conflicts and economic volatility. The minister highlighted India's proactive stance during crises, including the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing geopolitical tensions. Jaishankar called for diplomacy to resolve the Russia-Ukraine conflict, particularly concerning maritime security.

stories.title: Supreme Court may get 3 judges today, to be one short of full strength
stories.summary: The Union law ministry has announced the appointment of three judges to the Supreme Court. Justice Sunita Agarwal, Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh have been elevated. These judges were previously chief justices of their respective high courts and will be sworn in soon. With these appointments, the Supreme Court remains one judge short of its sanctioned strength.

stories.title: Form 6 not modified, only declaration added: Election Commission
stories.summary: Election Commission officials clarified that there was no change to Form 6, only an additional declaration form was introduced. This statement followed CJI Surya Kant's observation regarding the approval of modified Form 6. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi accused the Chief Election Commissioner of making illegal changes to the form. The Election Commission denied these accusations and referred to a previous press note for clarification.

stories.title: Rawat seeks meet with Congress brass as Kumari Selja slams his yatra plan
stories.summary: Harish Rawat's thanksgiving yatra has prompted a strong response from AICC, emphasizing the need for party unity. Kumari Selja has criticized the yatra as a parallel program that undermines Congress interests. The party leadership has expressed concern regarding Rawat's controversial statements and the potential division of support. A meeting between Rawat and Selja is expected to take place later this week.

stories.title: 'Judicial impropriety': Ex-CJI Gavai on sitting SC judge Bhuyan's remarks criticising SIR
stories.summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan raised concerns regarding the deletion of voters through special intensive revision, facing criticism from former CJI BR Gavai. While Bhuyan emphasized that disenfranchising citizens violates constitutional rights, Gavai expressed reservations about commenting on ongoing legal matters. Former Supreme Court judge Rohinton Fali Nariman also voiced concerns about the democratic implications of voters being removed from lists.

stories.title: California family’s 6,625-acre ranch is now protected forever
stories.summary: The Kinsey family has strategically safeguarded their vast 6,625-acre ranch in Benbow, California, by implementing a conservation easement. This crucial step preserves the land's agricultural, forest, and wildlife values, ensuring the ranch's ongoing functionality while protecting vital habitats for endangered species. David Johnson, a family member, was instrumental in this initiative, with the Northcoast Regional Land Trust planning to acknowledge their dedication to conservation this coming October.

stories.title: Probe sex assault case against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad, court directs Delhi cops
stories.summary: A Delhi court has ordered the completion of an inquiry into a sexual assault complaint against Chandrashekhar Azad. The complainant accused Azad of raping her under the pretext of marriage and claimed the police did not register an FIR. The police sought additional time for the inquiry, but the complainant opposed this request. The court rejected the police's plea and emphasized that the alleged offence is punishable with life imprisonment.

stories.title: India & Switzerland deepen ties across trade, mobility, tech and defence; sign 5 pacts
stories.summary: India and Switzerland have signed five agreements to strengthen cooperation in trade and mobility. The two countries aim to enhance market access for Indian exports and attract Swiss investments in key sectors. A new mobility agreement will facilitate easier access for Indian professionals and students to Switzerland. Both leaders discussed global conflicts and emphasized the importance of dialogue for peace.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha polls: 8 fresh BJP faces for UP, Hardeep Puri among 2 ministers dropped
stories.summary: BJP has chosen not to renominate Union ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma for Rajya Sabha. This decision raises speculation about a possible reshuffle of the council of ministers by PM Narendra Modi. Since several ministers have been given organization roles, it indicates their continuation in government may be unlikely. Puri's term ends in November, and he may be reassigned for the Punjab assembly polls.

stories.title: SIR row: Will annul Election Commission orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has asked the Election Commission to clarify decision-making processes related to voter roll revisions. It emphasized that decisions should be taken unanimously or by majority among commission members only. Senior advocate Vikas Singh argued for preserving records and scrutiny of the commission's actions. The court will examine allegations of unilateral actions against the Chief Election Commissioner.

stories.title: Couple turns 2 garden plots into 50-acre farm; 2.5 acres hit $200K in sales
stories.summary: Shane and Emma Rozeveld's journey from hobby gardeners in British Columbia to running a thriving 50-acre organic farm in Ontario is inspiring. Founders of Aslan Organics since 2017, they navigated challenges at the Sarnia Farmers' Market, eventually boosting their revenue to over $200,000 in a single year with weekly sales hitting $10,000.

stories.title: US F-1 visa: Indian student claims October interview date got canceled for refusing to pay agent extra ₹20,000
National Commission for Women issues safety guidelines to step-up monitoring of app-based and digital transport services
stories.summary: The National Commission for Women has released guidelines aimed at improving safety for women passengers using app-based transport services. These measures include verifying the background of drivers and ensuring proper identification matches. Additionally, the guidelines address issues related to late-night travel and unauthorized changes in drivers or vehicles. Aggregators are encouraged to create a verified pool of women drivers to enhance safety.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: High court quashes PSA detention of Shopian man for ‘showing anti-national tendencies’
stories.summary: Jammu & Kashmir high court has quashed the preventive detention of Mashooq Ahmad Shah under the Public Safety Act. The court found the allegations against him to be vague and lacking necessary details. Justice Rajnesh Oswal ruled that his detention violated constitutional guarantees under Article 22(5). Shah had been accused of anti-national activities without sufficient evidence. Consequently, the court directed his immediate release if not wanted in other cases.

stories.title: After losing her mother to MS, J.K. Rowling gave £10m to research
stories.summary: J.K. Rowling opened the Anne Rowling Regenerative Neurology Clinic in memory of her mother, who died of multiple sclerosis. The clinic focuses on research and treatment of various neurological diseases, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease. The funding aims to attract world-class researchers to develop new therapies and potentially find a cure. It has already hosted numerous clinical appointments and research projects since its inception.

stories.title: Montana meltdown: MAGA attacks Indians teaching at Montana State University. Turns out they are the 'best of the best'
Two killed, Indian among injured after Russian drone hits Turkish cargo ship
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck the MV Royad Mammadov cargo vessel in the Black Sea, resulting in two fatalities. Among the crew were three Indian nationals, one of whom sustained injuries and received medical care. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy confirmed that the ship's captain was killed in the attack and expressed condolences. Romanian authorities responded to the incident by rescuing 11 crew members and recovering two deceased individuals.

stories.title: Man pays $15, finds 6.03-carat diamond worth $1M
stories.summary: Jack Pearadin, a dedicated Navy reservist from Missouri, has transformed his passion into a treasure hunt since 2013 at Arkansas's Crater of Diamonds State Park. Recently, his persistence paid off when he discovered a stunning 6.03-carat yellow diamond he estimates could be worth $1 million. Throughout his adventurous quest, Pearadin has unearthed over 300 gems, sharing the profits from his latest find, aptly named the 'American Dream,' with a friend.

stories.title: 'Montana will never be the same': Who is Governor Greg Gianforte, the new target of MAGA's anti-India hatred?
Pakistan, Saudi, Turkiye activate Mecca defence pact as Yemen war escalates
stories.summary: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to enhance military cooperation to address regional security threats. Following recent attacks by Yemen's Houthi group, the three countries will activate collective deterrence measures. The emergency meeting of the Mecca Defence Alliance in Riyadh led to this commitment. Saudi-backed forces are also launching an offensive against the Houthis in Yemen to regain control.

stories.title: Scientists found at least 10 likely new species of bizarre branching worms inside sea sponges
stories.summary: Researchers have identified ten likely new species of branching marine worms found within sea sponges. These unusual worms exhibit a unique tree-like body structure, which has evolved over time. Genetic analysis and museum specimens helped resolve the long-standing classification issues of these marine organisms. The study indicates these worms' diversification relates closely to their sponge hosts and geographic locations.

stories.title: Not now daal-ing, says MAGA, as Montana governor comes to India to sell pulses
stories.summary: Montana's Governor Greg Gianforte is heading a delegation to India to promote agricultural exports. The focus is on selling lentils, peas, and chickpeas to the world's largest consumer of pulses. This trip highlights the growing tension within the Republican party regarding international trade and immigration. Many in the GOP criticize Gianforte's outreach to India amidst concerns about jobs for Americans.

stories.title: Dad built a backyard coaster, now selling it for NZ$4,500
stories.summary: In the midst of the COVID-19 lockdown, inspired by a flurry of YouTube tutorials, Bjorn Burton took on an exciting challenge—he built a roller coaster in his backyard. With his father’s help, he engineered this thrilling ride after rigorous safety trials with concrete bags. Now that the neighborhood kids have outgrown it, Bjorn is ready to sell the coaster, already envisioning a future project for when he welcomes grandchildren.

stories.title: 'Story matters, so does how you get it': Delhi Police lays down rules for scribes covering protests
Simon Andriesz: UK whistleblower who flagged Howard Lutnick’s alleged Epstein links dies by suicide, friend sets up fundraiser for son
Uttarakhand CM Dhami hands over appointment letters to 332 recruits under ESI scheme
stories.summary: Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday distributed appointment letters to 332 newly recruited personnel, including 271 appointees in the AYUSH Department and 61 Allopathic Pharmacy Officers under the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Scheme, at an event held at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan at the Chief Minister's Camp Office.

stories.title: American chestnut returns to Bronx Zoo after 120 years; 25 saplings planted in NYC
stories.summary: The American chestnut is returning to the Bronx Zoo more than 120 years after blight was first documented there. The zoo and New York Restoration Project planted 25 hybrid saplings as part of a restoration effort. Once abundant across eastern North America, the tree was devastated by disease that killed nearly 4 billion trees.

stories.title: Muslim outreach or message to Akhilesh? How Imran Masood's 'elevation' will test Congress-SP alliance in UP
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, Congress is setting the stage for the 2027 assembly elections amidst complicated alliance dynamics with the Samajwadi Party. The selection of Imran Masood as state chief has ignited concerns about Congress's approach to the alliance and the contentious seat-sharing talks. Masood's clear statements on the party's electoral strategy suggest underlying tensions that might define their coalition's effectiveness in challenging the BJP.

stories.title: Bypolls in 5 assembly constituencies, 1 Lok Sabha seat tomorrow: Key contests to watch
Taylor Sheridan bought a 600-acre Texas ranch as a family home; it is now a film set, horse hub and concert venue
stories.summary: Taylor Sheridan's Bosque Ranch in Weatherford, Texas, has transformed into a prominent site for film and TV productions. Originally intended as a family residence, it now generates substantial income through shows like Yellowstone and 1883. The ranch doubles as an equine center, celebrating Western culture with competitions and housing over 150 horses, making it a hotspot for equestrian training. Sheridan's strategic expansions have added to his impressive property portfolio.

stories.title: 'Misled the public': BJP rejects Rahul Gandhi’s 'illegal' claims on Form 6 and SIR
Supreme Court pauses coercive action against Tata Chemicals in marine sanctuary case
stories.summary: A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice on Tata Chemicals' plea against the high court's May 25 judgment. The bench asked the Gujarat government to respond by November 2. "Meanwhile, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners," the Supreme Court said.

stories.title: ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’: Congress announces nationwide campaign against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Five adopted Black children abused by white parents awarded $4.4 million settlement after CPS failures
stories.summary: Five adopted Black children who endured horrific abuse and neglect at the hands of their white adoptive parents have been awarded a $4.4 million settlement from West Virginia following alleged CPS failures. Some children were forced to live in a shed without running water or a bathroom before authorities discovered them in 2023.

stories.title: What Fox News CEO said on Karoline Leavitt joining the channel as a contributor from November 1
Tennessee estate returns at $19.9M after $6.8M sale and massive build-out
Indian man on a spouse visa convicted of money laundering in Austin, worked as a coordinator for India-based call center scammers
Workers cut 30 trees on wrong New Hampshire property; $100,000 settlement
'World is an age of flux, but India will rise to challenges': S Jaishankar
‘Police can’t remain mute spectators’: Delhi HC dismisses pleas for fresh probe into 2019 Jamia violence
MIT revives Bill Freeman's three-sided zipper after 40 years in a garage
'Fear of losing minority votes': MP CM slams Congress for silence on pilot Smit Machchhar
'Misleading': EC fact-checks Rahul Gandhi's 'CEC changed Form 6 illegally' post
Pakistani man in Florida creates website to sell fake US postage labels; $100K reward announced for his information
Florida woman inherited her father's home and now faces HOA lawsuit
‘No need to go to media’: SP MP urges Congress to raise seat-sharing demands directly with Akhilesh Yadav
Pennsylvania couple accidentally bought an 1830s house for $460,000; 5 years and $300,000 later, it is 85% complete
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania couple, Tyler and Lauren Bouldin, bought an abandoned stone house at an auction for $460,000. They faced numerous challenges during renovations, including structural issues and rising costs due to the pandemic. The couple decided to shift their approach to reuse materials and take on more work themselves. After about five years of work, the renovations are approximately 85% complete, although challenges remain.

stories.title: ‘Gyanesh Kumar must go’: Opposition turns up heat on CEC after SC Form 6 clarification
Jelly Roll and Bunnie Xo list $7M Tennessee home after divorce
stories.summary: Country singer Jelly Roll, whose real name is Jason DeFord, and Bunnie Xo are selling their Tennessee home. They finalized their divorce settlement earlier this year, transferring ownership of the property to Bunnie Xo. The mansion sits on nearly 10 acres and was built in 2022, with an asking price of around $7 million.

stories.title: 'What's the purpose of SIR if citizens are removed?' Bombay high court's Goa bench raps EC
stories.summary: The HC's remarks came while examining concerns over voter deletions during the SIR exercise. The bench referred to observations made by the Supreme Court that ensuring the inclusion of Indian citizens in the final voter list is the ECI's responsibility. The comments was in the backdrop of the wider legal challenge to the voter revision exercise, with concerns being raised over the manner in which names could be excluded from electoral rolls.

stories.title: Wild blacktip sharks can hear sounds from nearly 250 feet away underwater
'Beyond limits': Ex-CJI Gavai, former judges slam SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks amid EC-SIR row
Evening news wrap: SC refuses to pass interim order to suspend CEC; Trio win Nobel Prize in medicine for research on how brain forms memories
Chirag Paswan's UP gamble: Why PM Modi's 'Hanuman' is flexing his muscle against allies
stories.summary: Chirag Paswan's decision to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election marks an expansion of LJP (Ram Vilas). With plans to prepare for all 403 seats, the move could test the party's ability to build a Dalit vote base, influence close BJP-SP contests and strengthen its bargaining power within the NDA. His political journey from the 2020 Bihar split to a 19-seat win in 2025 provides the backdrop.

stories.title: 'Fighting this battle in our own way': AAP to skip opposition march to EC office over SIR row
stories.summary: Aam Aadmi Party announced they will not participate in the upcoming INDIA bloc protest at the Election Commission. Senior leader Sanjay Singh stated their ongoing protests concerning electoral roll issues are independent. Singh said the party perceives the matter as a people's movement, encouraging citizen participation without AAP's branding. AAP and DMK, previously aligned with the INDIA bloc, have also opted out of its recent meetings.

stories.title: In 1925, a Yellowstone explosion reshaped Biscuit Basin; 101 years later, USGS found a sign mix-up
stories.summary: A captivating century-old enigma surrounds Yellowstone's Biscuit Basin, centering on the misplacement of Black Pearl Geyser. The confusion stemmed from a hydrothermal explosion in 1925, which not only reshaped the landscape but also displaced a key sign. Correspondence from 1926 highlighted the depth of this perplexity related to the geyser's position.

stories.title: ‘SC itself scheduled, then cancelled meeting’: One Nation, One Election JPC chief PP Chaudhary amid controversy
stories.summary: PP Chaudhary provided clarification about the cancelled meeting set between the parliamentary panel and Supreme Court judges. He stated that the Supreme Court had initially scheduled the meeting for October 6 and later cancelled it. Chaudhary emphasized that previous interactions between parliamentary committees and the judiciary are not without precedent. Former Union minister Kapil Sibal criticized the meeting's constitutionality, arguing it undermined the separation of powers.

stories.title: BJP drops all 8 Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha members, including Hardeep Puri - what it means
stories.summary: The outgoing BJP members, apart from Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma, are Arun Singh, Neeraj Shekhar, Geeta Shakya, Brijlal and Seema Dwivedi. The eighth seat belonged to former deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma, who resigned on September 11 after being appointed lieutenant governor (LG) of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. His term was due to end on November 25, like those of the others.

stories.title: California scientists grow kelp in labs at 74,000 spores per millilitre
Pregnant mum won £1m lottery, then welcomed her baby four days later
stories.summary: In February 2019, Natalie and Andrew Symes unexpectedly won £1 million in the EuroMillions lottery. Shortly after their win, they welcomed their daughter Poppy a month earlier than expected. The couple used their winnings to buy a home and relieve financial pressure during lockdowns. Natalie's ability to stay home with the children has been a significant change in their lives.

stories.title: Kansas neighbour cut 133 trees, some 70 feet onto adjoining land; court upholds $6,500 award
stories.summary: A Kansas appeals court has upheld a $6,500 damages award against a man whose neighbour’s fence project led to 133 trees being cut on adjoining land in 2015. The court found the landowner filed his trespass case within the legal time limit and that there was enough evidence to hold Douglas Black responsible for the tree damage.

stories.title: New light-powered material could make clean hydrogen cheaper to produce
Florida's Burmese pythons are carrying three previously unknown RNA viruses
'CEC changed Form 6 illegally, unilaterally': Rahul Gandhi ups the ante after SC's clarification
Seven charged with setting fire to 13 rented Louisiana homes for insurance claims
stories.summary: Seven people have been charged in Louisiana over an alleged insurance fraud scheme involving 13 residential fires between 2019 and 2026. Prosecutors say the group rented homes, took out insurance, allegedly set fires and then submitted false claims for property losses, hotel stays and disaster relief payments.

stories.title: Texas man used Civil War relic as paperweight; later found it was a live explosive
Klein Curaçao restored native plants after removing goats and cats, aiding nine bird species
Kris Jenner relists Hidden Hills mansion at $11.25M after $2M price cut
PM Modi meets Swiss president Parmelin in Delhi; trade, investment on agenda
Koyel Mallick joins BJP a day after being nominated for Rajya Sabha seat
NASA spacecraft gains 3.5 km/s speed from Earth’s gravity assist without major engine burn
stories.summary: On September 28, 2026, Juice, the Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer, accomplished a successful gravity assist flyby of Earth. This maneuver was pivotal in adjusting the spacecraft's trajectory and significantly boosting its speed without the need for extensive engine thrust. Throughout its mission, Juice has strategically employed gravity assists, effectively conserving fuel.

stories.title: Rare 1982 Atari game found in box donated to Texas Goodwill sold for $10,590
stories.summary: A rare 1982 Atari 2600 game found among donated video games at a Texas Goodwill store sold for $10,590.79 in 2021. Goodwill said only 13 known copies of Air Raid existed at the time. The game was spotted by an employee, who confirmed its rarity with his father before the seven-day auction drew 34 bids.

stories.title: Minnesota farmers grazed sheep under solar panels; flock covered 6,500 acres
California thieves stole $80K statue of 1886 Kentucky Derby winner
Delhi Police detain protesters over demonstration against alleged sexual misconduct of three women journalists
stories.summary: Delhi Police on Monday detained protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating against an alleged incident of sexual misconduct against three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.

stories.title: ‘Comment on Smit’s bravery also’: Piyush Mishra questions Naseeruddin for attending Mumbai CJP protest
'Ensure women safety, even at 10pm': SC tells Delhi authorities to be 'very harsh' in rape crackdown
Antarctica’s 2 native flowering plants responded differently to 7 years of warming
stories.summary: Research on King George Island examined how two native Antarctic plants responded to long-term warming. Antarctic hairgrass displayed reduced hydraulic conductivity and photosynthesis compared to those in natural conditions. In contrast, Antarctic pearlwort increased both its hydraulic conductivity and photosynthetic capacity. This study provided insights into contrasting adaptive strategies of these plants under sustained environmental changes. These findings highlight the need to understand species-specific responses to climate change effects.

stories.title: Hyderabad hosts global real estate dialogue as IREC 2026 brings 2,000+ delegates to HITEX
HC orders CBI probe into corruption allegations involving Punjab CM’s office OSD
Michigan collector's $30 estate sale find turned into a Gertrude Abercrombie artwork worth $1.35 million
stories.summary: In a stunning turn of events, Gertrude Abercrombie's painting, Alderman Merriam's Shells, was auctioned for $1,352,600 after being found at an estate sale for just $30. Having been lost for 75 years, the piece drew significant attention at Freeman's auction house, far exceeding expectations. A dedicated collector meticulously verified its authenticity, marking a remarkable resurgence for Abercrombie in the contemporary art scene.

stories.title: SC issues notice to Centre over Central Vista library plan, seeks reply in 3 weeks
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has urged the Centre to submit a comprehensive report regarding library facilities. The inquiry centers on the designated space for the current book collection within the Central Vista project framework. Since 2011, around two lakh books have been stored without being unpacked, prompting worries from court officials.

stories.title: Delhi riots: HC rejects pleas seeking FIR against political leaders over 'hate speeches'
How flydubai security failure, across 3 countries, almost led to 'Israel’s 9/11’
'Want to see who modified Form 6': SC refuses to pass interim order to suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar
stories.summary: The Supreme Court refused to suspend Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid allegations regarding unilateral decisions. Petitioners challenge decisions made without approval from other commissioners, citing possible violations of electoral regulations. Kumar's modifications to the voter registration process have raised questions about their legality and adherence to the law. The Election Commission maintains that differing opinions are normal and does not invalidate its orders.

stories.title: Black rat removal helped Zannone shearwater pairs rise from 27 to 80
‘10 ko poora desh aa raha hai’: TMC vows support to CJP; AISA’s Neha claims journalist Rosie detained- top developments
Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
stories.summary: In a surprising blunder, US President Donald Trump claimed that 125 million individuals participated in India's presidential election, sparking confusion given Brazil's recent electoral events. His remarks drew attention to his concerns over the integrity of the US electoral system. Social media users quickly slammed the President and highlighted inaccuracies in his understanding of India’s election process.

stories.title: 'Shameful': AAP shares video, says Delhi Police ‘abusing’ protesters at Jantar Mantar
Government set to halt sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses diversion for ethanol
‘Gyanesh must quit right away': Opposition backs Justice Bhuyan’s 'SIR strikes at Constitution's heart' remark
DNA reveals the origin of rats found on Lord Howe Island after eradication
stories.summary: Black rats were believed to have been completely eliminated from Lord Howe Island, only for researchers to rediscover them in 2021. Through genetic analysis, they traced the rats back to the island’s prior population rather than any from the mainland of New South Wales. This finding sparked debates about how these rodents survived the eradication. Consequently, a swift initiative was launched to eradicate the newly returned rats.

stories.title: Justice Bhuyan's remarks prove CEC violated Constitution: Congress
stories.summary: Congress General Secretary Jairam Ramesh stated that Justice Ujjal Bhuyan affirmed the right to vote's significance in the Constitution. He emphasized that this opinion indicates a violation by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Ramesh argued that Bhuyan's remarks undermine Kumar's position as a constitutional authority. Additionally, he suggested that Kumar should resign due to losing his moral authority.

stories.title: Brazil election: Lula, Flavio Bolsonaro head to runoff after tight first-round vote
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face each other in a runoff election. Neither candidate obtained the majority required during the first round of voting. The runoff election is scheduled for October 25, 2026, with major issues such as corruption and cost of living impacting the campaign. Both candidates are expected to appeal to voters from eliminated candidates.

stories.title: Crews remove 850,000 cubic yards of toxic sediment from Ohio's Cuyahoga River
India's political will needed to extradite Sheikh Hasina: Bangladesh
stories.summary: Bangladesh is optimistic that India will expedite the extradition process for former PM Sheikh Hasina. Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi stated that legal processes are currently in motion. State Minister Shama Obaed Islam emphasized the importance of political will from both nations. Meanwhile, outgoing Bangladeshi high commissioner Riaz Hamidullah met with Indian External Affairs Minister Dr. S Jaishankar to discuss mutual interests.

stories.title: Flydubai co-pilot allegedly tried to crash plane after hijack attempt failed
stories.summary: An Omani co-pilot attacked the captain of a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv. Following the assault, he attempted to crash the aircraft into the Saudi desert. Investigators are looking into whether the co-pilot cut the engines' fuel supply during this crisis. Emergency codes were transmitted to air traffic control indicating both a general emergency and a suspected hijacking.

stories.title: Mynas introduced to control a coconut pest later became pests themselves
stories.summary: In 1915, common mynas were introduced to the Cook Islands to mitigate a coconut pest problem. Unfortunately, these birds multiplied rapidly, encroaching on the territories of native species and invading agricultural lands. Their escalating presence led to the establishment of a bounty program on Atiu Island, aiming to control their growing numbers. This situation highlights the unintended consequences that can arise from introducing new species into fragile ecosystems.

stories.title: Man’s $3 Goodwill painting turns out to be a 1650 Flemish work worth $190,000
stories.summary: In a remarkable twist of fate, a former antiques dealer purchased a painting for just $3, suspecting it held greater value. Appraisers on Antiques Roadshow estimated its worth between $20,000 and $30,000, but the auction result astonished everyone, fetching $190,000. This stunning Flemish piece, dating back to around 1650, serves as a testament to the hidden gems that can be discovered in thrift shops and donation centers.

stories.title: Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman
stories.summary: Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman expressed concerns regarding the functioning of the Election Commission in India. He highlighted the issue of illegal removal of voters from electoral lists, especially in West Bengal. Nariman noted that 90 lakh voters were disenfranchised, with many not having access to justice. He emphasized the need for reform in the appointment process of election commissioners to ensure fairness.

stories.title: US withdraws all bombers from UK's Fairford base after suspected terror plot
stories.summary: The United States has withdrawn all bombers from RAF Fairford following an investigation into a suspected terror plot. The withdrawal occurred shortly after several people were arrested in connection with the alleged attack plans. British authorities indicated potential Iranian involvement, while Tehran firmly denied these claims and summoned the British ambassador. Additionally, the US maintains military presence in the Middle East with several ships heading to the region.

stories.title: How farmers are helping reverse farmland wildlife decline
stories.summary: The resurgence of corn buntings and various wildlife species showcases the power of collaborative conservation work initiated by local farmers. Through the Martin Down and Allenford Farmer Clusters, projects were implemented to improve habitats throughout their farms. This endeavor has led to impressive increases in populations of butterflies and grey partridges over the past ten years. Continued financial investment and diligent monitoring are essential to uphold these successful biodiversity initiatives.

stories.title: 1 dead as Russian drones hit desi pharma plant in Ukraine
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Sumy region, six Russian drones attacked the Kusum Group's pharmaceutical plant, killing one engineer and injuring others. The main structure of the facility was largely destroyed during the targeted strike, which occurs amid a pattern of similar attacks. The company estimates damage from this incident could exceed $50 million, impacting operations significantly.

stories.title: Florida road test finds incinerator ash had no groundwater impact over 10 years
External affairs minister S Jaishankar says US has chosen to become 'lonelier power'
stories.summary: S Jaishankar stated that India aims to mediate in the Russia-Ukraine conflict through dialogue and diplomacy. India has recently proposed ideas addressing issues like grain and energy exports to both nations. Jaishankar emphasized America's changing global position and the implications of China's rise on international relations. India is also facing domestic repercussions due to the ongoing conflict, including commercial shipping disruptions.

stories.title: 25 paisa/kg wheat MSP hike an 'insult': Samyukta Kisan Morcha
stories.summary: Farmer organisations represented by Samyukta Kisan Morcha rejected the government's announced minimum support prices for Rabi crops. They described the small increase for wheat as an insult rather than acceptable compensation. SKM called for a revision of MSPs and urged states to offer bonuses to farmers. Additionally, they highlighted the impact of rising diesel and input costs on farming.

stories.title: 'Look Out Circular' against parents of man who secretly took away child to US
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has indicated consequences for parents of a man who abducted his daughter to the US. This decision came during a case regarding child custody between NRI couples. The father has been ordered to return to India with the child within four weeks. If he fails to comply, his parents will face legal consequences. The court emphasizes the importance of the child's connection with her mother.

stories.title: Meet Nathan, the Texas seventh-grader who turned shellfish waste into a water-cleaning project
stories.summary: Nathan Gael Montelongo, a seventh-grader from La Joya, Texas, created a project using chitosan. He collected discarded shellfish shells to produce chitosan powder and tested its effectiveness on polluted water. Studies showed that chitosan improved water clarity and benefited zebrafish embryos in experiments. Nathan designed a prototype raft that could automate water quality monitoring and treatment.

stories.title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan
stories.summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan condemned the extensive deletion of voter names from electoral rolls due to the special intensive revision process. He emphasized that such actions undermine the core principles of the Indian Constitution and disenfranchise millions of citizens. Bhuyan highlighted that the right to vote is essential for free and fair elections in India. He urged that no citizen should be denied the right to vote without due process.

stories.title: 3 million face masks could be used to build 1 km road, Australian study finds
stories.summary: Engineers at RMIT University have discovered a groundbreaking method to recycle single-use face masks by integrating them into road construction. By blending shredded masks with recycled concrete aggregate, the researchers aim to enhance road materials while tackling the problem of mask waste. Their findings suggest that approximately 3 million masks could be utilized in constructing a one-kilometre, two-lane road.

stories.title: Seattle removes 900 tons of driftwood yearly; 80% is reused for wildlife habitat
Meet the Indian-origin seventh-grader who boosted atmospheric water output by 117%
stories.summary: Ankith Burki, a seventh-grader from BASIS Independent Silicon Valley, created an atmospheric water generator for his project. He utilized low-frequency sound waves to improve the efficiency of water collection. Testing revealed a 117 percent increase in water production under specific sound conditions. His work earned him a finalist position in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.

stories.title: UK: 2 teenagers jailed for 10 years for arson at Indian restaurant in London
stories.summary: Two 17-year-old teenagers were sentenced to 10 years for an arson attack at Indian Aroma. The incident occurred on August 22, 2025, when they threatened diners with weapons. Their actions led to severe burns for multiple victims, including a couple who suffered life-threatening injuries. The court emphasized the planning and intent behind the attack, which resulted in serious harm. The motive for this violent act remains unknown.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Pakistani prisoner dies by suicide in jail
stories.summary: Shahid Imran, a 36-year-old Pakistani undertrial prisoner, was found unconscious in his jail cell early Sunday. He was a resident of Sargooda district in Punjab, Pakistan. Authorities rushed him to GMCH where doctors declared him brought dead. The incident occurred at the high-security central jail in Jammu. An investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death is likely to follow.

stories.title: Kashmiri teacher fights period stigma, one village at a time
stories.summary: Aasima Jan works diligently in north Kashmir, focusing on menstrual health awareness to help girls stay in school. She began her efforts after witnessing the stigma around menstruation affecting attendance rates among female students. Monthly sessions in villages educate families about menstrual hygiene and encourage open discussion about the topic. Aasima also distributes sanitary pads, highlighting their importance for health and hygiene.

stories.title: How Ankith Burki built a machine that extracts water from air
Meet the eighth-grader who built a low-cost air sampler to study rural health surveillance
stories.summary: Bailey Quinn Frank has created a groundbreaking air sampler designed to enhance health surveillance in rural areas. Utilizing basic materials such as fans and filters, this device collects airborne bacterial DNA. Findings revealed notable variations in bacterial composition between indoor and outdoor spaces. As a finalist in the Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge, Bailey exemplifies the use of practical tools in tackling public health issues.

stories.title: €100 typewriter turns out to be WWII Enigma machine, sold for €45,000 at auction
stories.summary: A German Enigma machine sold for €100 at a Romanian flea market surprised many when it fetched €45,000 at auction. The machine, thought to be a regular typewriter, was identified by a cryptography professor who recognized its historical significance. After purchasing it, the professor cleaned and repaired the machine to prepare it for auction. This Enigma machine was used during World War II for military communications.

stories.title: Beyond advocacy: Government steps up diplomatic push for Ukraine settlement
'Little bit more involved': Jaishankar says India has 'gone beyond advocacy' to end Russia-Ukraine war
2 killed, 25 injured as gunfire erupts at homecoming party in Georgia
Singeetham Srinivasa Rao: Seven decades, many worlds of cinema
Bon Jovi’s foundation helped turn former Army Medical Center into housing for 77 homeless veterans
stories.summary: Jon Bon Jovi’s Soul Foundation backed a housing project at the former Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington, DC. The development opened in 2019 with 77 permanent supportive housing units for formerly homeless veterans. The project was part of a wider redevelopment of the former 66-acre military medical centre.

stories.title: Mumbai Police registers FIR against organisers of Thackerays' anti-SIR march
India successfully demonstrates its first free-space quantum-secure communication link for over 5.5 km
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking trial, Indian startup QNu Labs, in collaboration with BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar, successfully tested free-space quantum key distribution. This trial established a secure quantum communication channel over a considerable distance, boasting a quantum bit error rate of under 5%. With the integration into BISAG-N’s Vedic Kavach platform, secure key sharing and end-to-end message encryption are now possible, paving the way for advancements in India’s secure communication framework.

stories.title: Baltimore shooting: 12-year-old girl killed in crossfire after parking dispute
Uttarakhand CM Dhami, Union ministers Kiren Rijiju and Jual Oram lead massive roadshow, attend 'Aadi Rangotsav Festival' in Khatima
Ex-Army jawan among 2 held for 'passing' information to Pak on defence movements: Assam CM
Cornell sexual assault case: Woman at centre of rape allegations got threats to withdraw lawsuit, lawyer says
Monthly stipend for senior, junior resident doctors to increase from Rs 75,000 to Rs 1 lakh: Uttarakhand CM
stories.summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday announced that stipends for both Senior and Junior Resident doctors in the state have been raised significantly from approximately Rs 75,000 to over Rs 1 lakh per month.

stories.title: 300+ objections as Maidstone residents oppose former hotel conversion into 42 studios for 65 people
stories.summary: More than 300 objections have been filed against plans to convert Maidstone’s former Grange Moor Hotel into 42 studio apartments for an estimated 65 people. Residents say they are concerned the development could increase pressure on parking, local infrastructure and the neighbourhood, with some describing themselves as “devastated” and saying they would not have bought their homes.

stories.title: CM Pushkar Singh Dhami chairs first-ever cabinet meeting in Champawat to boost border area development
'Equal share and equal respect': Congress's reply to Akhilesh's seat-sharing pitch
No whataboutery can justify voter disenfranchisement, says SC judge; oppn says CEC 'exposed'
Texas landowners feared border wall would cut off Rio Grande access; judge blocks Big Bend construction
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a federal judge has temporarily halted the construction of border barriers in Texas' Big Bend area. Local landowners and environmental advocates express concerns about restricted access to the Rio Grande, claiming the barriers would disrupt the ecosystem and infringe on constitutional rights. The federal government asserts that security measures necessitate these barriers. This decision has sparked six lawsuits contesting the planned border initiatives.

stories.title: Farm groups protest low Rabi MSP hike, call it an insult
Social, rights activist Harbans Bharowal remembered upon his demise in Brampton
Donald Trump’s climate cuts left thousands jobless; Climate Reserve created a lifeline for 50 experts
stories.summary: Donald Trump’s second-term climate cuts scrapped billions in research funding and left thousands of federal workers jobless. In response, climate experts launched Climate Reserve, a multimillion-dollar initiative helping displaced scientists find new roles and revive disrupted projects. The group expected to place 50 experts in new positions while preserving critical climate research and expertise.

stories.title: He paid $30 for a painting that sold for $1.35 million
stories.summary: At a recent estate sale, a man bought a Gertrude Abercrombie painting for only $30. Upon confirming its authenticity at an exhibition, he opted to auction the piece. Titled Alderman Merriam's Shells, the painting was anticipated to sell between $150,000 and $250,000. Remarkably, it sold for a staggering $1,060,000 at Freeman's auction, setting a new high for the artist and highlighting the incredible value of art investments.

stories.title: 'I do not accept': Ex-Maha CM Chavan rejects Raj Thackeray’s election boycott call amid SIR row
CEC protest intensifies in Delhi; AISA, AAP workers detained as protesters face barricades
From India to Australia: How 6 countries got caught up in flydubai terror
stories.summary: On September 30, the flydubai Flight FZ1073 faced a cockpit attack when Omani co-pilot Hammam al-Hammami stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar. The injured pilot bravely opened the cockpit door, allowing crew and passengers to subdue the co-pilot. The flight was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where al-Hammami was apprehended by authorities. Investigations have since been undertaken by several countries into al-Hammami’s background and possible extremist ties.

stories.title: 'Russia stood by us when our territorial integrity was under threat': Jaishankar
Retired FBI agent’s decade-long mission to rediscover 30 ‘lost’ apple varieties
stories.summary: In 2012, retired FBI agent Dave Benscoter began searching for forgotten apple varieties after discovering unidentified trees in a churchgoer’s orchard. What started as curiosity became a decade-long mission. Alongside fellow apple enthusiasts, Benscoter has helped rediscover 30 once-lost varieties while preserving historic apple trees across the Pacific Northwest for future generations.

stories.title: US man convicted of killing motorist to be resentenced after court rejects AI video of victim forgiving him
Texas city to pay $175,000 after SpaceX site it owns overpumps 128m gallons of groundwater
stories.summary: The McGregor City Council has reached a settlement regarding penalties related to groundwater overpumping caused by SpaceX. The city will allocate $175,000 for this resolution and commit to a 25-year groundwater monitoring program. However, residents are concerned about who will bear these costs, urging that SpaceX should take financial responsibility.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: BJP attacks Cong over silence on Capt Machchhar, CJP alleges FIR refusal against ACP, Imran Khan’s party protests in Pak
Lionel Messi's foundation helped fund Barcelona's €37M cancer centre
Indian-origin US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi introduces bills to help immigrant doctors, nurses
300 students take on AI, deepfake fraud challenges at BIT Mesra hackathon
India can launch surgical strikes on Pakistan, but can't hold talks: Mani Shankar Aiyar
Bengal to bring law against land and love jihad, implement UCC in 6 months: CM Suvendu

New lizard species found above 15,750 feet in Peru’s harsh Andes landscape
Leonardo DiCaprio gave $1 million to a Seychelles debt swap that protected 410,000 sq km of ocean
stories.summary: Seychelles protected 30% of its ocean by 2020 through a debt conversion deal linked to long-term conservation. The plan safeguards 410,000 sq km of ocean, while allowing sustainable fishing, tourism and other economic activities. Leonardo DiCaprio Foundation was among the private funders supporting the financial transaction.

stories.title: Antiques Roadshow Valuation: $100 Kleitsch find pegged at $500,000; painting later sells higher
stories.summary: A painting by Joseph Kleitsch that cost $100 in 1939 later gained a valuation of $500,000. The artwork depicts early Laguna Beach and showcases Kleitsch's significant contributions to California Impressionism. Following its appearance on Antiques Roadshow, the painting sold for an undisclosed amount exceeding the television valuation. It subsequently featured in exhibitions at the Irvine Museum and Laguna Art Museum in later years.

stories.title: 'Same cheap rhetoric': CM Vijay slams Stalin, DMK over 'vile' remarks against women
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay condemned M K Stalin and the DMK for derogatory attacks on women. He spoke during a campaign rally in Dharapuram, highlighting the need for respectful discourse. Vijay asserted that his remarks were made as a son and brother of Tamil Nadu women. He warned of legal consequences for continued derogatory comments from DMK leaders.

stories.title: 'US has deliberately become a lonelier power': EAM Jaishankar on shifting world order
'Good thing': Union minister praises Rahul's Satyagraha website, then takes swipe at opposition
'What has changed in 17 years?': Rahul Gandhi hits out at BJP over Bihar flood crisis
Where will India be 5 to 10 years from now? EAM Jaishankar answers
stories.summary: During the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, S Jaishankar elaborated on India's potential to rise swiftly in the global power arena within the next decade. He pointed out the country's robust growth trajectory and advantageous demographic trends. Additionally, Jaishankar contrasted the significant influence held by the United States and China with that of current middle powers, recognizing the complexity of evolving global power dynamics.

J&K: Security forces launch search op for suspected terrorists in Rajouri, Udhampur

Zelenskyy vows to hit Russian refineries as infrastructure warfare escalates
Ancient Mammal Fossil Unearthed: Workers find 40–45 million-year-old bones; scientists probe mystery species
stories.summary: In a remarkable find during construction in Oceanside, California, fossilized remains were unearthed at a considerable depth. Expert paleontologist Joseph El Adli confirmed the identification of the bones, prompting a meticulous excavation effort. These fossils, dating back 40 to 45 million years from the Eocene Epoch, are under investigation to discern if they belong to brontotheres or amynodonts.

stories.title: Godfrey Hounsfield’s CT scanner revealed a brain cyst in the first scan in 1971
In 1963, scientist swabbed his daughter’s throat; her virus strain led to a mumps vaccine in 1967
stories.summary: In 1963, scientist Maurice Hilleman collected a mumps virus sample from his five-year-old daughter Jeryl Lynn. Researchers weakened the virus to develop a vaccine, which was approved in 1967. The vaccine, based on the Jeryl Lynn strain, remains in use and helped transform the fight against mumps in the US.

stories.title: 'Police whose job is to provide security is making women feel threatened': Priyanka Gandhi on Jantar Mantar incident
‘She will continue’: Thiruvananthapuram mayor denies BJP councillor Sreelekha resigned from post
stories.summary: The controversy began after a message purportedly posted by Sreelekha in a WhatsApp group of residents in her ward said she had submitted her resignation to the Mayor and would give a copy to the District Collector on October 5. Rajesh had initially said he received a resignation letter from Sreelekha on September 30 but had not sent it to the Corporation Secretary.

stories.title: CJP protests outside police station after 3 women journalists allege sexual harassment by cops
No room to roam: The cost of a crowded planet for wild animals
'Who is safe?' Delhi minister Sirsa attacks Punjab govt after Mad Sandhu killing
‘If you manufacture a dictator, we will bury it’: Uddhav, Raj launch joint protest against CEC
Historic Atlanta mansion cut in half and moved to save it
stories.summary: Historic Randolph-Lucas-Jones House was saved from demolition by new owners who relocated it in 2013. Built in 1924 for a descendant of Thomas Jefferson, the house required significant restoration after moving. The removal involved careful dismantling of the structure to reduce weight and manage logistics effectively. Restoration efforts were extensive, demanding creative financial planning to ensure the project continued. The house honors preservation advocate Christopher M.

stories.title: ‘Dog-whistle politics’: Kerala CM Satheesan slams CPM over Malappuram remarks
Shonda Rhimes sells restored Hancock Park mansion for record $21 million
UK collector's £15 teapot sold for £575,000 after experts identified rare Bartlam piece
stories.summary: A broken teapot bought for £15 at a 2016 auction was identified as a rare piece made by John Bartlam in South Carolina in the 1760s. It later sold for £460,000 at auction, reaching £575,000 with the buyer’s premium, and was acquired by The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.

stories.title: ‘Gyanesh ka resignation to lekar rahenge’: Congress calls for fresh protest in Delhi
‘Journalists must be allowed to work freely’: Press Club 'shocked and dismayed' over Jantar Mantar police action
'Not afraid of death': Co-pilot's chilling admission after trying to crash flydubai jet
Puerto Rico seventh-grader turns plantain peels into mulch, cutting weeds by up to 53%
stories.summary: Wileidy Feliciano-Rivera, a seventh-grader from Puerto Rico, transformed discarded plantain peels into biodegradable mulch. This innovative project addressed plastic waste and showcased potential agricultural benefits. EcoMusa, the resultant mulch, effectively reduced weed growth during testing while retaining moisture and lowering soil temperatures. Wileidy's work has garnered recognition as a finalist in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.

stories.title: Mojave Desert search finds 6 new bee population groups; why tiny poppy specialist escaped endangered listing
stories.summary: Recent surveys have revealed six new population groups of the Mojave poppy bee, surprising biologists with the species’ extended range and resilience. Despite this positive news, a population group in Utah was unfortunately noted as lost. Findings suggest that the Mojave poppy bee does not currently warrant protection under the Endangered Species Act, but conservation efforts will persist to enhance its habitat monitoring.

stories.title: Russia cuts education and healthcare budget as war spending hits new high
stories.summary: Russia's financial burden is not limited to military spending. The government is also spending more on servicing its debt as high interest rates increase borrowing costs. Debt-servicing costs in 2027 are expected to be 21.6% higher than originally planned. They are projected to account for 9.4% of total government spending next year and could rise further to 10.6% by 2029.

stories.title: IC 814 hero Captain Devi Sharan pens a tribute for Capt Smit
Message to Congress? Akhilesh Yadav says ‘it’s not about seats, it’s about victory’
Sydney shopper’s A$4 cup turns out to be worth A$75,640
stories.summary: A shopper discovered a unique Chinese libation cup at a thrift shop in Sydney, Australia. They bought the cup for A$4 despite its significant chip. After assessing the item, a Sotheby's specialist appraised it at A$20,000 to A$30,000. The item was later auctioned for A$75,640, significantly exceeding the original purchase price. This event highlights the potential hidden value in thrift store finds.

stories.title: NSW planted bitou bush to stabilise dunes; it now threatens native ecosystems across 46% of coast
stories.summary: Bitou bush was intentionally planted along the New South Wales coast to stabilize sand dunes. This plant has since spread extensively, covering 46% of the coastline and threatening native vegetation. Infestations of bitou bush replace native plant species and alter animal habitats throughout the region. A Threat Abatement Plan has been established to manage and contain this invasive species effectively.

stories.title: ‘Gandhi, Nehru, Ambedkar are India’s soul, mind, backbone’: Dipke's jibe at Centre
US Marine arrested in Japan over murder, robbery of local woman
‘He was so scared’: SP MP on ally Rahul Gandhi skipping Amethi in 2024 Lok Sabha polls
stories.summary: "Had there been no alliance (with the Samajwadi Party), they (Congress) wouldn't have won a single seat. It even reached a point where their top leader Rahul Gandhi was ready to give up his seat. He contested from elsewhere (Raebareli) instead of Amethi. He was so scared," SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel said.

stories.title: ‘Crushing democracy in their DNA’: Shivraj on Congress demanding return to ballot papers
SC steps in over relocation of 135-year-old Delhi library housing 8.5 lakh books
stories.summary: The suo motu case, titled "In Re: 135-Yr-Old Library 8.5 Lakh Books– And No Room In The New Central Vista Plan", was registered on October 3. The concerns centre on where the library and its vast collection would be housed if Shastri Bhawan is demolished. Reports said the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Central Public Works Department were still looking for suitable space for the library.

stories.title: Trump leaks senator’s number after row over clock-change bill: What’s the dispute
stories.summary: Under the current system, Americans move their clocks one hour forward in March and one hour back in November. Moving the clock forward means sunrise and sunset appear one hour later on the clock. If the sun would normally rise at 7 am and set at 6 pm, the clock change would make them appear as 8 am and 7 pm. This gives people more daylight in the evening.

stories.title: ‘Will create a lot of trouble’: Owaisi warns of protests bigger than Jantar Mantar over Form 7
‘Blatant lie’: China slams US panel’s ‘genocide’ claim after Starbucks opens first Xinjiang stores
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry has condemned a US congressional committee's criticism of Starbucks for opening stores in Xinjiang. The US claims genocide against the Uyghur minority in the region, which China denies vehemently. Despite the accusations, Starbucks intends to continue its business operations in Xinjiang. The company recently expanded through a joint venture in China, increasing its nationwide presence.

ShinyHunters hacker in FBI data theft held in Jordan
'He prayed before attack': Machchhar tells Netanyahu chilling flydubai cockpit ordeal

Insurance companies want policyholders to pay 10% of health claims
PK Mishra: India must stay open, but not become vulnerable
Rs 3,750 crore RCom fraud: CBI names ex-LIC executive
Finance system resilient, economy braved West Asia crisis: RBI governor
stories.summary: 'Can't afford to be complacent, must stay alert'
