Resource security key as global economy faces uncertainty: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman
Hormuz blocked, but Gulf crude shipments at pre-war level
Indians live longer than Pakistanis, lag Bangladeshis, says WHO
Jimmy Carter’s Georgia farm solar project once supplied 60% of Plains’ power
'Do not come to USA for your masters': Ed-tech entrepreneur warns Indian students about returning with huge debt
Kashmir professor removed for ‘harassing’ students
Author Garth Stein lists his 1924 Seattle home for $2.45M
stories.summary: Garth Stein and his wife are selling their Seattle home after living there for 25 years. They purchased the property in 2001, aiming to raise their children there. The home has been extensively renovated while maintaining its original character and charm. Located in the Mount Baker neighborhood, the house features stunning views and modern amenities. This marked listing reflects their transition as their youngest child heads to college.

stories.title: Drug addicts turn to painkillers amid Nasha Mukt crackdown in J&K
Green Card holder's mother denied B1/B2 visa to attend housewarming ceremony: They did not ask for any documents
PoK woman crosses LoC in Rajouri, detained
1 dead, 55 hurt in J&K as Bengal bus hits hillside, vehicle sent for rescue overturns
Tony Stewart’s 20,000-sq-ft Indiana ranch drops from $30M to $18.9M after two price cuts
stories.summary: Tony Stewart’s Hidden Hollow Ranch in Indiana has returned to the market for $18.9 million. The 415-acre property has a 19,713-square-foot main house with six bedrooms, an 8,700-gallon aquarium, indoor stream, bowling alley and golf simulator.

stories.title: Road injuries 10th leading cause for deaths in India: WHO report
Laid off on the last day of OPT, Indian techie lands job with US company in India within 40 days, says, 'I was not living there, I was just surviving'
O'Connor ranching legacy began in 1834; 6,409 acres of Texas prairie protected 191 years later
stories.summary: The historic T.M. O'Connor Ranch in Texas has gained a notable conservation easement, protecting nearly 6,409 acres of precious coastal prairie while enabling ranching operations to persist. Made feasible through a combination of federal and private funding under the RESTORE program, this area plays a pivotal role in supporting over 300 distinct wildlife species and rare flora. This agreement showcases a united front for conservation efforts alongside sustainable farming solutions.

stories.title: Boy, 6, wrote ‘Chocolate Bar’ for friend with rare liver disorder; book raised $1 million
stories.summary: At 6, Los Angeles boy Dylan Siegel wrote and sold a book calledChocolate Barto help fund research into his best friend Jonah’s rare liver disorder. What began as a child’s idea grew into a fundraising effort that had raised $1 million by 2014.

stories.title: Indian man arrested and charged in California for drunk driving, running over a woman and then fleeing the scene
Zelensky claims Ukraine ‘de-occupied’ around 140 km of territory from Russia
A 10.22-kg rock used as a Michigan barn doorstop was identified as a new iron meteorite
stories.summary: In 1939, a meteorite was unearthed on a Michigan farm and innocently pressed into service as a doorstop for many years. It wasn't until 2018, following the fall of another meteorite, that subsequent owners saw its true value. Central Michigan University performed an analysis and confirmed it as a new IIIAB iron meteorite, shedding light on the crucial role of personal specimens in advancing scientific knowledge.

stories.title: Iowa family’s 84-year farming legacy ends as 1,209 acres go up for auction
stories.summary: On October 30, a landmark auction will take place for the 1,209-acre farmland portfolio owned by the Woods family in Fayette County. This well-preserved parcel boasts high-quality soil, attracting a variety of potential buyers—from local farmers to investors and recreational users. The hybrid auction setup will enable competitive bidding on individual lots, marking the culmination of the family’s 84-year legacy with the land.

stories.title: Sally Quinn and Ben Bradlee bought Grey Gardens for $220,000; it later sold for $15.5M
stories.summary: In a momentous deal for historic preservation, Sally Quinn and Ben Bradlee acquired the storied Grey Gardens estate in 1979 for $220,000. Following a meticulous restoration, it emerged as a cultural hallmark tied to the Beales. Its remarkable sale for $15.5 million in December 2017 underscores the lasting interest in uniquely significant properties, concluding nearly forty years of history for this iconic location.

stories.title: Russia to take 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, Jaishankar tells panel
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar briefed a parliamentary committee on India's engagement with Russia and Ukraine. He highlighted bilateral trade expansion and India's aim to send skilled workers. The minister discussed India's diplomatic efforts to facilitate dialogue for ending the Ukraine conflict. Additionally, he noted the government's initiatives to release Indian nationals in the Russian military. Jaishankar emphasized India's commitment to secure economic interests and safeguard Indian citizens abroad.

stories.title: ‘Will sign those checks’: Trump repeats $5,000 promise to US adults if Republicans win 2026 midterms
India summons Pak envoy over 'cross-border infiltration', rejects Ferozepur claims
Agra court grants bail to 6 Cong workers arrested for defacing CEC Gyanesh Kumar's ancestral home
Helicopters, influencers and nail art: The money trail of 2026 assembly elections
stories.summary: The BJP and Congress have filed their election expenditure reports following several assembly elections this year. The BJP recorded a hefty expenditure of Rs 529.39 crore across five states, whereas Congress spent Rs 248.55 crore. These contrasting figures unveil the distinct priorities of the political parties, particularly in West Bengal and Keralam.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav asks SP leaders to keep seat-sharing concerns internal amid friction with Congress
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav, president of the Samajwadi Party, encouraged leaders to express seat-sharing concerns privately. Tensions arose after Shiv Pal Singh Patel criticized Congress' demand for 150 seats in upcoming elections. Patel emphasized that Congress should receive a more realistic allocation based on their previous performance. Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Mishra stated that top leadership will decide the seat allocation.

stories.title: Four North Carolina homes repaired after Helene face demolition after FEMA buyouts
stories.summary: In the aftermath of Hurricane Helene, four homes in the Cottages at Cypress Run neighborhood in Hendersonville face demolition due to severe flooding. Previously, these homes were repaired through homeowner efforts and community volunteerism. To address the persistent flood threats, homeowners have chosen FEMA's voluntary buyouts, aligning with the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program's initiative to convert affected land into green spaces, thereby reducing future flood risks.

stories.title: Queensland dairy farmer opened four campsites after drought forced her family to sell 40 cows
stories.summary: Agritourism is gaining momentum among Australian farmers struggling with drought-related financial pressures. Landowners like Libby Rough are transforming their properties into camping havens, creating alternative income streams. This shift not only aids in sustaining their farms during tough times but also promotes local agricultural education among visitors. Moreover, local authorities are streamlining regulations to encourage this thriving sector, enhancing community engagement with farming practices.

stories.title: Elon Musk's baby mother Ashley St Clair says it's 'karmic' that Shivon Zilis 'got played' after what she did to Grimes
UK-Iranian man arrested over suspected RAF Fairford terror plot released on bail
'Example of their frustration': Shivraj Singh Chouhan slams Congress for calling Modi 'illegal' PM
1987 Buick GNX with 30 miles jumps from $200,000 to $427,000 in 2 years
Georgia begins 10-year forest restoration at 132-acre Towaliga Preserve with data-centre partnership
stories.summary: The Towaliga Preserve is about to launch an ambitious 10-year forest restoration project, backed by QTS Data Centres. This significant initiative aims to revitalize 132 acres, focusing on ecosystem management and biodiversity enhancement. Throughout the decade, contractors will engage in tasks like invasive species control and planting native trees. After the project, the Southern Conservation Trust will ensure the area remains cared for and healthy.

stories.title: Indian man with US Green Card challenges his immigration detention; DHS reveals his criminal record in court
'Anti-party activities': AAP suspends Punjab MLA after he claims teacher shortage in emotional video
'No deadline for Sheikh Hasina's return', says Indian high commissioner in Bangladesh
stories.summary: High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi addressed the extradition request for Sheikh Hasina from Bangladesh, stating that the matter is under legal review, preventing a set timeline for her repatriation. He clarified that India had no involvement in her arrival, citing the dire circumstances in Bangladesh. As relations between India and Bangladesh grow increasingly strained, the new Bangladeshi government remains resolute in pursuing Hasina's extradition.

stories.title: 'Ask cops to wear name plates': CPI MP detained during protest at Jantar Mantar writes to Amit Shah
Teaching is just the start: The crushing burden on India's college teachers
Wisconsin diver finds 17-foot canoe underwater, radiocarbon dating puts it at 1,000 years
stories.summary: A fascinating discovery was made by diver Mark Schachtner: an ancient dugout canoe dating back about 1,000 years in Pewaukee Lake. In partnership with Native Nations, the Wisconsin Historical Society is carefully documenting this important archaeological treasure. Researchers have assessed its condition and theorized its submersion history. This find not only contributes to Wisconsin's storied history of ancient canoes but also sheds light on Indigenous practices.

stories.title: Michigan commits $89 million to restore polluted Detroit and Kalamazoo rivers by 2040
stories.summary: Michigan's Reclaim the Rivers initiative is set to invest $89 million to tackle pollution in the Detroit and Kalamazoo rivers. This funding is dedicated to sediment removal, restoring habitats, and increasing public access for recreation. State officials envision a significant transformation by 2040, working to reverse years of industrial damage and improve water quality and ecological health across communities and the Great Lakes.

stories.title: Adopted man discovers Grammy winner Michael McDonald is his biological father
stories.summary: A St. Louis man adopted as a baby nearly 60 years ago discovered that Grammy-winning musician Michael McDonald was his biological father after a previously unknown half-brother took a 23andMe DNA test. The discovery led to meetings with both his birth mother and McDonald, followed by a family reunion that also introduced McDonald to his grandchildren.

stories.title: BJP loses majority in Thiruvananthapuram corporation after Sreelekha's resignation; LDF watches closely
Canada's largest gold heist of 2023: 'Fugitive' Simran Preet Panesar can't leave India; 'If he's hiding, he's hiding in plain daylight'
57 new deep-sea species discovered in Argentina’s Mar del Plata Canyon, including ‘Loki’ sea cucumber
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking deep-sea voyage off Argentina, scientists uncovered 57 brand new marine species alongside five previously unclassified genera. Using a remotely operated vehicle, they pulled samples from the Mar del Plata Submarine Canyon. Among these marine marvels was a unique and translucent sea cucumber whimsically dubbed Loki. A subsequent collaborative workshop was instrumental in accelerating the species identification process, highlighting the astonishing biodiversity of the South Atlantic's deep ecosystems.

stories.title: Cleveland factory once tied to auto history sells for $300,000, avoiding demolition
Astronomers spot gas falling onto a neutron star, revealing how matter reaches its surface
stories.summary: On February 1, 2025, a research team used the XRISM telescope to study GX 301–2. They captured a unique event of gas falling onto a neutron star. The observations revealed changes in iron absorption lines from redshift to emission over time. The study suggests multi-phase accretion and indicates interactions with the stellar wind. These findings provide new insights into how neutron stars feed on surrounding matter.

stories.title: 6 missing after Gulfstream jet disappears near Nantucket after takeoff from Bermuda
Adult Homo erectus fossil confirms species appeared in Africa 2 million years ago
stories.summary: Researchers have described 18 previously unpublished hominin fossils from South Africa, including an adultHomo erectusfossil dated to 2 million years ago. The findings support the species’ first appearance in southern Africa at that time and provide evidence of microevolution inP. robustus.

stories.title: Vijay's TVK joins INDIA bloc meet in Tamil Nadu, Congress calls it 'historic day'
stories.summary: Manickam Tagore, the president of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee, celebrated the significant inclusion of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam in the INDIA alliance. The assembly was pivotal in calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar due to discrepancies in electoral rolls. Notable participants, Aadhav Arjuna and Maria Wilson, emphasized the urgency of the issue, with protests planned across Tamil Nadu to amplify their demand for accountability.

stories.title: How a US pest-control effort turned Asian lady beetles into an invasive species
stories.summary: Originally imported to the United States for biological pest control, the multicoloured Asian lady beetle, or Harmonia axyridis, has turned invasive. Competing with native ladybugs, this species disrupts ecosystems. While it helps manage aphid populations, its autumn behavior drives adult beetles to invade homes, creating an unwanted nuisance. This case serves as a cautionary tale about the unintended effects of introducing nonnative species into local environments.

stories.title: 'Most comprehensive plan': Ukraine confirms India playing role in mediating energy truce in Black Sea
stories.summary: Ukraine has expressed readiness to explore India's comprehensive proposal for ending the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. During recent communications, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha emphasized the importance of India's mediation role. India's external affairs minister S Jaishankar affirmed continuous engagement with both Kyiv and Moscow regarding potential solutions. Ukraine is open to discussing limited ceasefire arrangements around energy infrastructure and safe Black Sea shipping.

stories.title: Florida sea captain spent years searching before buying a Scottish castle
California tech company owner arrested over alleged $300 million China chip-smuggling scheme
A Moroccan mine built a road from phosphate waste rock; field tests cut dust emissions by 91%
stories.summary: In Morocco, a phosphate mine has implemented an innovative road surface made from waste rock generated during phosphate extraction. This robust, three-layered pavement design not only successfully supports heavy mining vehicles but also helps manage dust emissions effectively. Testing resulted in a notable decrease in airborne dust and enhanced road quality, with an anticipated 15 percent boost in productivity for mining operations, while also cutting down maintenance expenses.

stories.title: New York men cut 4 trees on neighbour’s land, face $35,000 award
DJ Alok has helped restore 3 million sq m of native forest in Brazil
Doudna team finds ancient CRISPR ancestor with unusual gapped DNA code
Ohio girl’s $768 lemonade stand grows into nonprofit that raises over $5 million for hospitals
stories.summary: After her time at Cincinnati Children's Hospital, Payton Obert initiated a lemonade stand to assist children in distress. What started as a simple venture has evolved into Payton's Lemonade Stand, amassing over $5 million for various children's charities. The nonprofit not only supplies toys and necessary items to kids facing illness but also encourages community participation, proving that even small gestures can spark tremendous positive impacts.

stories.title: 'AAP asked you not to': Congress leader claims CJP refused party's help during Assam detention
Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
stories.summary: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta has reported significant progress in waste management at landfill sites throughout the city. The government has successfully reclaimed land and aims to eliminate existing garbage mountains while managing fresh waste effectively. New waste processing facilities have been inaugurated at Okhla, Ghazipur, and Singhola, each designed to process thousands of metric tonnes daily.

stories.title: Muskegon Lake had 347,350 tons of debris and 190,000 tons of contaminated soil removed
stories.summary: Muskegon Lake in Michigan has been officially delisted from the EPA's Areas of Concern list, marking a monumental milestone in restoration efforts. Over decades, key initiatives addressed challenges such as habitat degradation, pollution in soils, and shoreline hardening. With around $80 million dedicated to the cause, revitalized wetland habitats now support thriving fish and wildlife communities. This achievement heralds a brighter future for both the environment and local residents.

stories.title: Texas family has owned a 650-acre Lake Palestine ranch since 1940; a $10 million deal will turn the property into a new state park
stories.summary: In a strategic move for conservation, a sprawling 650-acre ranch in East Texas is set to transform into a state park. Acquired by the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation from the long-time Pollard family, this land has a rich history dating back to 1940. The park’s development will proceed in stages, initially offering guided access before introducing more facilities for visitors.

stories.title: Kansas artist spent 30 years filling his 70-acre property with 600 metal totems
Pakistan kills 5 TTP militants as violence escalates on Afghanistan border
stories.summary: In a decisive operation, Pakistani security forces eliminated five militants affiliated with Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This mission was executed based on critical intelligence that pinpointed various militant hideouts. Alongside this successful strike, the forces seized a substantial arsenal of weapons and ammunition. This action is a response to the recent surge in violence linked to the TTP, emphasizing the military's ongoing commitment to combatting terrorism in the region.

stories.title: Shopper’s C$5 thrift-store painting turns out to be a David Bowie original, sells for C$108,120
stories.summary: A lucky shopper stumbled upon a remarkable David Bowie painting at a donation center, priced at just C$5. After expert verification, it was revealed to be D Head XLVI from Bowie's iconic Dead Heads series. Shockingly, the artwork was auctioned for an astounding C$108,120, setting a record for Bowie's art. This astonishing find underscores the thrill of discovering hidden gems and the significance of artistic provenance.

stories.title: 'Recovering well': MEA provides update on flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar attacked by co-pilot
From ‘tareekh pe tareekh’ to justice within 3 years: Amit Shah hails BNS, overhaul of criminal laws
Eight Amazon rope bridges logged 15,000 wildlife crossings with zero roadkill in Brazil
Minors used to deter police action at CJP’s Mumbai protest? NHRC seeks report
Arkansas man finds rare 6.03-carat diamond after 13 years of hunting
Congress resets Team Uttar Pradesh: 5 clear messages for BJP and Akhilesh Yadav
stories.summary: Congress has overhauled its Uttar Pradesh unit ahead of the 2027 UP assembly election, appointing three-time MLA Aradhana Misra Mona as state president and Imran Masood as working president. The Congress reshuffle brings Brahmin, Muslim, OBC, Dalit and women representation into its leadership team, signalling a push to rebuild its organisation, expand its social base and strengthen its position in talks with Samajwadi Party.

stories.title: China’s Zijinshan mine turns waste into roads that withstand 100-ton trucks
In the 1970s, an Italian priest sold 12,000 piranhas to Europe; 55 years later his proceeds have funded 350m bridges and an 800m airstrip
stories.summary: Giovanni Gallo, an Italian Jesuit priest, moved to Marajó Island in Brazil in the 1970s. He organized the preservation and export of 12,000 piranhas to fund community infrastructure projects. These projects included bridges, a cemetery, a dock, and an airstrip for local residents. Gallo also founded the Museu do Marajó, which showcased local history and archaeology.

stories.title: 658 unmarked graves found at two remote Australian cemeteries after specialist search
stories.summary: A groundbreaking project has identified 658 previously unmarked graves at the White Cliffs and Menindee cemeteries in Australia. Utilizing advanced non-invasive scanning techniques, Hunter Geophysics successfully located these burial sites, ensuring no disturbance to the ground. This initiative aims to enhance cemetery management and heritage conservation, with plans for memorialization at White Cliffs for those honored. Such efforts emphasize the crucial need to preserve local history and cemetery documentation.

stories.title: 55 Indians still in Russian army: New Delhi presses Moscow at key meet, take action against agents
Spain bar collapses: 11 injured after building traps 25-30 people inside
'No evidence of fracture': Bengal govt to probe Mamata Banerjee's 2021 'injury'
Jammu-Srinagar highway: 1 killed, 56 injured in twin accidents in J&K's Ramban
Meet Daniel Cox, the student behind a chemical-free weed control system
Garland Bel-Air Estate Sale: Judy Garland home sells for $11.1 million; links to Hollywood’s Golden Age
stories.summary: The historic Bel-Air estate once owned by Judy Garland has been sold for $11.1 million, slightly below its listing price of $11.495 million. Built in 1938 by the renowned architect Wallace Neff, this traditional-style home showcases five bedrooms and seven bathrooms, set amid lush surroundings. Its ties to Garland's rise in Hollywood continue to intrigue potential buyers drawn to its storied past.

stories.title: 81 years after British submarine sank Nazi U-boat, Norway faces mercury threat from its wreck
stories.summary: Norwegian authorities are grappling with a serious mercury contamination issue stemming from the sunken U-864 submarine, which met its fate during World War II. Recent investigations discovered leaking mercury containers, prompting worries about environmental repercussions. The government is now exploring strategies to mitigate this contamination, with sealing the wreck being one of the options under consideration by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries in Norway.

stories.title: A Florida owner planned 52 homesites on his 625-acre ranch; county agrees to pay $7.8 million to stop development
stories.summary: In a bid to safeguard a crucial ecological area, Collier County has finalized an agreement to buy Wildflowerz Ranch, preventing any residential construction on its expansive 625 acres. Valued at approximately $7.8 million after two years of negotiations, this acquisition underscores the county's dedication to conservation and wildlife protection. Additionally, the ranch's current cattle operations will remain intact under a lease that lasts until the end of 2027.

stories.title: FSSAI steps up festive food crackdown as adulteration raids intensify
stories.summary: Over 4,100kg khoya, paneer destroyed in Delhi; 10,000kg adulterated paneer seized in Mewat in past month

stories.title: 'Could no longer defend the indefensible': Former AAP spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joins Congress
stories.summary: Priyanka Kakkar, a former Aam Aadmi Party spokesperson, joined the Congress party after leaving AAP. She criticized AAP's leadership saying that she could no longer defend the "indefensible". Kakkar also expressed admiration for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's resilience in facing political challenges and supported his criticisms of the Chief Election Commissioner.

stories.title: Delhi Police registers 3 FIRs over protests demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
Malnourished Mississippi stray became FEMA search dog; now 2026 Dog of the Year
After Chandrayaan-3, ICMR asks scientists to attempt the ‘impossible’ in healthcare
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has launched its “First in the World Challenge”, inviting researchers to develop breakthrough vaccines, drugs, therapeutics, diagnostics and other health technologies that have never been thought of, tested or tried anywhere in the world. The initiative will offer up to Rs 8 crore for a single project, depending on how advanced the proposed innovation is.

stories.title: Pennsylvania man turns old car parts into giant yard sculptures
Nearly half of India’s medical colleges fail to comply with NMC disability-unit directive
John Denver guest house gets fixes; buyer sells for $8.2M
stories.summary: John Denver's former guest house and music studio in Aspen sold for $8.2 million in November 2025. The recent buyer undertook significant renovations, including a modern kitchen and structural improvements. This property spans 5 acres within a gated community and offers stunning views from Aspen to Snowmass. It consists of two structures totaling 2,912 square feet, including a guest house that served as Denver's studio.

stories.title: Two Iranians in UK charged over terror plot targeting Manchester’s Jewish community
stories.summary: In a grave development, two Iranian nationals, Rahman Salehi and Salam Ahmadyan, face charges in the UK over an alleged terror conspiracy targeting Manchester's Jewish community during Yom Kippur. They stand accused of carrying out reconnaissance and attempting to procure materials for an improvised explosive device. Prompt intervention by authorities on September 20 thwarted the plot, ensuring the safety of the community from any imminent danger.

stories.title: Tribunal Lets £76m Claim Proceed: ex-Gitpod VP wins disability case; payout still undecided
stories.summary: Shannon Burns is currently involved in a significant legal battle against Gitpod regarding her employment termination. She has won a disability discrimination case, but compensation has not yet been awarded. Burns is seeking £76 million, arguing her dismissal disrupted her technology career. A tribunal recently allowed her claim to proceed despite Gitpod's attempts to limit it.

stories.title: $9.99 thrift-store painting was meant for cat art; it sold for $34,375 at Sotheby’s
stories.summary: Beth Feeback, an artist hailing from North Carolina, stumbled upon an extraordinary deal at Goodwill when she purchased a large painting for merely $9.99. A tip from a friend led her to uncover its true worth—a stunning geometric abstract by Ilya Bolotowsky. The piece notably fetched $34,375 at Sotheby's, thanks to its connection to the Weatherspoon Art Museum.

stories.title: Cornell rape victim ‘failed’ by people bound to protect her: New York governor
Two Iowa farmers quit pigs; their old hog barns became a mushroom business
Pope vs Anthropic: Why 'AI consciousness' is dividing Silicon Valley and Vatican
stories.summary: Anthropic has spent months consulting religious scholars and other experts about how AI systems should behave and what values they should follow. The company has held private discussions with scholars from around the world and required participants to sign nondisclosure agreements, according to the Times. The effort comes as Anthropic pursues rapid expansion, with the company potentially reaching a valuation of $2 trillion.

stories.title: Bangladesh extends official Durga Puja holidays to 3 days, steps up security
Rahul Gandhi launches 'Satyagraha' website for information on current protests across India
Pakistan logs over 1.2k rebel attacks in 9 months of ’26, security crisis deepens
Camp David huddle: Trump team discusses Iran war, possible Yemen offensive
Pacific to pacify ties? Washington sends US admiral to India as relations face strain
stories.summary: The US Embassy said the trip is meant to push forward the "major defense partnership" and deepen cooperation between the two militaries. Its list of topics includes digital transformation, emerging technologies and regional strategic stability. It also names "defense energy resilience" and an "increasingly competitive technology landscape", though it does not spell out what either would involve.

stories.title: RHS Rocket Science Experiment: ISS flight slows seed growth; Mars food plans still viable
stories.summary: In 2015, ESA astronaut Tim Peake carried rocket seeds to the International Space Station, launching a groundbreaking research project. Upon his return, 8,600 UK schools engaged in a citizen science experiment analyzing the seeds. The outcomes indicated that while the seeds' growth and aging were influenced by space conditions, they remained viable.

stories.title: 'I am Hanuman to Rahul Gandhi': Ajay Rai after being replaced as UP Congress chief

Bellamy was known for films including His Girl Friday and The Awful Truth.

stories.title: NHAI to inspect 17 highways awarded at 15% below estimates
stories.summary: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is set to implement special inspections on 17 highway projects that were awarded at least 15 per cent below the estimated costs. These inspections aim to uphold quality standards and will begin with initial reviews by December, followed by further checks in six months. Teams of seasoned engineers will oversee the inspections, and any quality inconsistencies will be rectified in line with contractual obligations.

stories.summary: The INDIA bloc, under Congress's leadership, is gearing up for a vigorous campaign against electoral misconduct and the Election Commission's authority. Their strategy includes widespread protests and a pivotal 'Save Democracy March' to elevate public consciousness while pressuring for essential reforms. Additionally, the bloc intends to approach the Supreme Court about ongoing electoral challenges. Among their key proposals are reinstating ballot voting and refining voter registration methods.

stories.summary: South West Water has been fined £7.8 million after pleading guilty to 18 charges linked to hundreds of sewage spills across Devon and Cornwall between 2015 and 2021. stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled out an outright ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, aiming instead for a compromise between health and cultural practices. Fireworks will only be allowed during specific times, with an emphasis on using environmentally friendly options that satisfy rigorous safety standards by licensed producers. Continuous engagement with Russia is ongoing to ensure the safety of affected Indian nationals. Citizens are urged to verify job offers and avoid unregistered agents.

stories.title: India's monsoon rainfall ends 13% below normal, fourth-lowest since 2001
stories.summary: India recorded 87.4 percent of its long period average rainfall during this year's southwest monsoon. The country received 759.4 mm of rain, which is 13 percent below normal. El Niño significantly contributed to the below-average rainfall, especially noted in southern and western regions. Despite a late surge in rainfall, several areas faced substantial deficits, particularly Punjab and South India. The overall monsoon season ended as the driest since 2015.

stories.summary: The INDIA bloc meeting focused on alleged electoral irregularities and the opposition’s protest plan, but a warm exchange between Sonia Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee drew attention.

stories.title: An Ohio farmer facing $1 million in medical debt hoped a solar lease would pay $540,000 a year
stories.summary: In Ohio, farmer Wayne Greier's financial struggles intensified when a planned solar project fell through due to local resistance and new rules, leaving his family's renewable energy plans in jeopardy. Compounded by $1 million in medical debt from recent health issues, Greier was forced to offload land and equipment, jeopardizing his farming business. He has emerged as an advocate for farmers' property rights to help protect others from similar hardships.

stories.title: Flydubai flight incident: Netanyahu says Israel preparing for other ‘potential threats’
stories.summary: A flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv experienced a serious incident that required an emergency landing. Following a cockpit altercation, one pilot was arrested and investigated by Saudi authorities. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the situation was managed and the safety of passengers was prioritized. Warplanes were scrambled in response to potential hijacking fears but were later stood down.

Their love blossomed into a large family, with 13 children resulting in a remarkable lineage of more than 120 descendants by 2025. The couple earned Guinness World Records' title as the longest-married living couple of different sexes.

stories.summary: During a conservation project in Cape Cod's Wellfleet Bay, volunteers stumbled upon a remarkable two-headed diamondback terrapin hatchling weighing just 5.2 grams. Known as bicephaly, this rare condition opens doors for valuable research. Currently receiving veterinary care, its health and growth are being closely monitored, underscoring ongoing efforts to safeguard this at-risk turtle species and its environment.

stories.title: Upanishads to Mahabharata: NCERT explains roots of national, SC mottos
stories.summary: The NCERT has introduced a groundbreaking Class IX social science textbook that bridges modern principles of governance with ancient Indian wisdom. By drawing connections between India's national motto, values upheld by the Supreme Court, and revered texts like the Mahabharata, this textbook advocates for key governance themes such as accountability, inclusiveness, and transparency. These concepts underline the need for various societal roles in fostering public welfare and ensuring democracy thrives.

stories.title: A Nashville man paid $2.48 for a document at a thrift store in 2006; it proved to be a rare...
stories.summary: While browsing a thrift store in Nashville, Michael Sparks stumbled upon an astonishing find: a rare 1823 copy of the Declaration of Independence, priced at only $2.48. Upon delving into its history, Sparks recognized its immense value and chose to auction it. To his amazement, the document fetched $477,650 at auction, enriching the known collection of surviving copies and transforming Sparks into a local legend.

stories.title: 'Reckless': Prince Harry, Meghan's children targeted by 'European paparazzi' at UK school
stories.summary: Concerns have arisen regarding Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's children's safety as European paparazzi have been spotted lurking near their new school, jeopardizing their privacy. This move back to Britain was intended to protect their family. Harry's longstanding battle against media invasions began after the death of Princess Diana. The couple has previously changed schools due to similar security issues, and the brothers’ relationship continues to face challenges.

stories.title: Kurt Cobain’s old apartment is now an Airbnb for Nirvana fans
stories.summary: Kurt Cobain’s former studio apartment in downtown Olympia has made its debut as an Airbnb listing, allowing fans a chance to stay where Nirvana’s iconic music was birthed. The cozy apartment, available for a minimum of two nights at $250 to $300 per night, features original decor and memorabilia from Cobain's time. Visitors often rave about the rich history and the convenient location near downtown amenities.

Their remarkable achievements earned them the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, and future expansions may enhance the reach of this technology.

Its revival has turned it into a notable landmark in Ypsilanti, and it is currently listed for $1.13 million, exemplifying the power of adaptive reuse.

As Indian refiners brace for a decline in Russian oil supplies, competition with China is pushing them toward pricier oil options.

stories.summary: A couple in Tucson, Arizona, transformed glass bottles into a 2,700-square-foot home over several decades. The property has now been listed for sale, attracting interest from folk art enthusiasts.

As Ukraine grapples with a lack of US-made Patriot missiles, the capability of its air defenses is being severely tested. Ukrainian officials claim that these strikes are a strategic move by Russia to weaken their defense.

stories.title: 575+ Nevada volunteers removed 120,125 pounds of waste across 26 Truckee River sites in one day
stories.summary: On September 26, over 575 passionate volunteers dedicated their time to a significant cleanup effort in Nevada's Truckee River watershed. Their hard work resulted in the removal of an astounding 120,125 pounds of waste, which included both litter and invasive weeds. This collaborative initiative also focused on planting vegetation and enhancing storm drains, all aimed at safeguarding the local ecosystem.

stories.title: In 2002, a 3.5km sea wall was breached in five places at a 283-hectare Essex arable farm
stories.summary: In October 2002, a sea wall breach in Essex transformed farmland into a coastal wetland, increasing saltmarsh areas. This project, supported by various environmental organizations, aimed to restore natural habitats and manage coastal erosion. Marine life flourished, and biodiversity increased rapidly in the newly flooded areas after the breach. Traditional farming on higher land continued alongside saltmarsh restoration, contributing to sustainable agriculture.
